title: Director, Digital Consulting Services
description:
The Director, Digital Consulting Services provides strategic and operational leadership for digital consulting functions that assess, prioritize, and advance technology solutions in support of Dana-Farber’s clinical, research, administrative, and operational goals. This role leads teams responsible for collaboration and productivity platforms as well as digital innovation initiatives, translating organizational needs into secure, scalable, and value-driven solutions. The Director partners across Information Services and Institute leadership to establish roadmaps, govern service delivery, and oversee a portfolio of medium- to high-complexity initiatives. This position requires strong leadership, sound judgment, and the ability to balance innovation, user experience, operational efficiency, and compliance in a complex healthcare environment.

Located in Boston and the surrounding communities, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is a leader in life changing breakthroughs in cancer research and patient care. We are united in our mission of conquering cancer, HIV/AIDS, and related diseases. We strive to create an inclusive, diverse, and equitable environment where we provide compassionate and comprehensive care to patients of all backgrounds, and design programs to promote public health particularly among high-risk and underserved populations. We conduct groundbreaking research that advances treatment, we educate tomorrow's physician/researchers, and we work with amazing partners, including other Harvard Medical School-affiliated hospitals.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Develops and executes the strategy, operating model, and multi-year roadmap for Digital Consulting Services, ensuring alignment with Dana-Farber priorities, Information Services goals, and evolving organizational needs. Establishes objectives, deliverables, timelines, and success measures for the function.
  • Leads multiple teams responsible for collaboration and productivity platforms and digital innovation services, overseeing the evaluation, selection, implementation, optimization, and lifecycle management of digital solutions that improve communication, efficiency, workflow performance, and user experience.
  • Partners with clinical, research, administrative, and operational leaders to understand business challenges, identify opportunities, and translate needs into actionable initiatives, service offerings, and technology recommendations. Oversees intake, prioritization, and demand management processes to focus resources on the highest-value work.
  • Directs cross-functional programs and medium- to high-complexity initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, technologies, and dependencies. Ensures effective use of project, product, and service management methodologies; monitors scope, schedule, risks, issues, and outcomes; and communicates progress through reporting and executive updates.
  • Establishes governance and operational standards for supported platforms and services, including administration, service levels, evergreen planning, adoption strategies, user support coordination, training alignment, usage analytics, and continuous improvement. Evaluates performance and identifies opportunities to optimize value, standardization, and sustainability.
  • Ensures solutions and recommendations align with Institute requirements for cybersecurity, data protection, infrastructure, compliance, and technology policy. Collaborates closely with peer Information Services teams and enterprise partners to avoid duplication, address integration needs, and maintain a secure and supportable digital ecosystem.
  • Oversees vendor and external partner relationships related to digital tools, consulting services, and innovation initiatives, including product evaluation, service oversight, contract support, and budget stewardship for one or more cost centers. Maintains awareness of industry trends and emerging technologies to inform strategic planning and responsible innovation.
  • Supervises staff. Hires, develops, and manages staff to achieve organizational goals. Sets clear expectations, delivers feedback, and monitors performance for quality, efficiency, and compliance with policies and procedures. Mentors staff, fosters career growth, and cultivates a positive and productive work environment.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Strong knowledge of digital strategy, healthcare technology, collaboration and productivity platforms, digital workflow solutions, and innovation practices within complex healthcare or academic environments.
  • Solid understanding of information services operations and the interdependencies among applications, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data governance, compliance, and user support functions.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess business needs, develop strategic roadmaps, and translate organizational priorities into practical, scalable, and measurable technology solutions.
  • Strong program and project management skills, including scope definition, prioritization, resource planning, timeline development, risk mitigation, and oversight of multiple concurrent initiatives.
  • Ability to lead effectively in a matrixed environment and influence stakeholders across departments, functions, and leadership levels without sole direct authority.
  • Excellent consultation, facilitation, relationship-building, and customer service skills, with the ability to establish trust and credibility with clinical, research, administrative, operational, and executive stakeholders.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex technical and operational information clearly to diverse technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to use metrics, dashboards, and analytics to monitor performance, assess adoption, identify opportunities for improvement, and communicate outcomes and business value.
  • Strong financial and operational acumen, including experience managing budgets, overseeing vendor relationships, supporting governance processes, and balancing innovation with cost stewardship and operational sustainability.
  • Sound judgment, adaptability, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage ambiguity, maintain confidentiality, support change management, and stay current with emerging technologies and their practical application in healthcare.

Minimum Job Qualifications

Education Required

  • Bachelor's Degree

Area of Study Required

  • Information Technology, Computer Science, Health Care Administration, Business Administration, Informatics, or a related field.

Experience Required

  • 8 years of progressively responsible experience in information services, digital consulting, digital strategy, healthcare technology, product management, project/program management, or a related field required.
  • 5 years of management experience leading professional staff, cross-functional initiatives, and complex portfolios required.
  • Experience translating clinical, operational, research, or business needs into technology-enabled solutions required.

Experience Preferred

  • Experience leading digital transformation, collaboration platform strategy, workflow optimization, or digital innovation initiatives in a large healthcare system, academic medical center, or similarly complex environment preferred.
  • Experience with budget management, vendor management, and governance processes preferred.

License/Certification/Registration Preferred

  • Project management, agile, product management, IT service management, or other relevant technology certifications preferred.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • Staff supervised: Application analysts including principal, senior, and II (7+), platform architect (1), project managers (1+), executive assistant supporting multiple VPs and AVPs (1).

Patient Contact:

  • None

At Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, we work every day to create an innovative, caring, and inclusive environment where every patient, family, and staff member feels they belong. As relentless as we are in our mission to reduce the burden of cancer for all, we are committed to having faculty and staff who offer multifaceted experiences. Cancer knows no boundaries and when it comes to hiring the most dedicated and compassionate professionals, neither do we. A career at Flex offers the opportunity to make a difference and invest in your growth in a respectful, inclusive, and collaborative environment. If you are excited about a role but don't meet every bullet point, we encourage you to apply and join us to create the extraordinary.

Job Summary





To support our extraordinary teams who build great products and contribute to our growth, we’re looking to add a Product Engineer located in Salt Lake City, UT.

Reporting to the Engineering Manager the Product Engineer will be responsible for receiving, evaluating, cleaning, and customizing all technical information / documentation from the customer related to their product, derived from a New Product Introduction (NPI) or a design change to establish all necessary processes to manufacture it by maintaining its design and performance integrity.

What a typical day looks like:

  • Handle product transfer and new product set up.
  • Support production by assessing product engineering issues of diverse scope that arise on production line.
  • Suggest improvements to process to obtain improved quality and production yield.
  • Solve product related problems and perform failure evaluation related to product issues.

  • Safety Requirements and regulations compliance identification
  • Engineering Drawings Interpretation of parts and assemblies.

  • Request, handle and administrate golden samples, engineering samples of final product and/or piece parts
  • Establish, operate, and maintain a standard method for technical information interchange with the customer to control and preserve information of NPI transferred projects

  • Evaluate and identify course of action of Product Change Notification (PCN) and Manufacturing Change Order (MCO)
  • Ability to take additional responsibilities of the Manufacturing Engineer depending on the size and complexity of the customer product.

The experience we’re looking to add to our team:

  • Typically requires a Bachelor of Science Degree in related field or equivalent experience.

Ability to apply mathematical operations to such tasks as frequency distribution, determination of test reliability and validity, analysis of variance, correlation techniques, sampling theory and factor analysis.
  • Ability to analyze problems, design experiments, conduct a design for manufacturing analysis, collect data, establish facts and draw valid conclusions. Testing: oscilloscope, cable and harness testing, trouble shooting, component testing, logic analyzer. Inspection: bare board, systems, components, cable and harness, microscope, measuring tools. Mechanical & Electrical Tools: taps and dies, alignment tools, measuring tools. Office skills: telephones, data entry, office software to include, word processing, spreadsheet and presentation package.

title: Senior Vice President - Head of Core Infrastructure Platforms (CIP)
description:
Head of Core Infrastructure Platforms (CIP), Pune

Senior Vice President

Pune, India

About Infrastructure Technology

The Global Infrastructure organization builds and maintains the critical technology backbone that enables Jefferies to operate at scale, delivering secure, resilient, and high-performing IT services that power the business. We drive innovation through solutions such as cloud and hybrid adoption, network resiliency, platform modernization, and automation. The organization is structured into several specialized sub-domains: Core Infrastructure Platform, Public Cloud, Digital Workspace, Networking, Telecom & Multimedia, and International Infrastructure. Our teams collaborate globally to ensure Jefferies’ technology platforms are highly available, secure, scalable, and cost-effective.

Core Infrastructure Platforms

The Core Infrastructure Platforms function lays the foundation for Jefferies’ IT, designing, operating, and optimizing the essential compute, storage, operating systems, and database platforms that support all business-critical applications. Our mission is to deliver secure, resilient, and high-performance datacenter and cloud solutions for global operations.

Organized into four teams, Global Systems Engineering, Unix Engineering, Windows Engineering, and Database Engineering, this group drives operational excellence, security, high availability, compliance, and continuous improvement across our technology estate.

By championing automation, standardization, and proactive monitoring, and by working closely with application, security, and business teams, we ensure our environments are robust, stable, and scalable. Through this collaborative approach and a relentless focus on modernization, Jefferies’ infrastructure remains agile and adaptable, ready to meet the evolving needs of our global business.

Job Summary

Jefferies is seeking a dynamic, hands-on, and strategic Senior Vice President (SVP), Head of Core Infrastructure Platforms (Pune). This executive technical leader will lead automation, operations, and modernization of Jefferies’ platform stack, with a focus on critical platform domains: databases, virtualization, storage, backup, compute, and Unix/Windows server infrastructure. Based in Pune, India, the SVP will lead the Pune CIP team and be accountable for technical excellence, operational resilience, and end-to-end Pune led delivery supporting the US, EMEA and APAC estate. This role reports to the Head of GCC, Pune (primary) and the Global Head of Core Infrastructure Platforms, Jersey City (secondary).

This is not a pure management or “middle-layer” role. The ideal candidate is a hands-on domain expert who remains technically current, acts as a trusted escalation point and decision-maker, and independently resolves complex infrastructure and operational challenges rather than simply escalating them.

Success in this role comes from earning the trust of engineers and global business stakeholders through demonstrated technical mastery, incident command, and the delivery of solutions that enable strategic business outcomes. The position requires deep technical expertise paired with proven people leadership to build, mentor, and scale high-performing teams supporting 24/7 capital markets operations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Global Platform Leadership: partner with global leads on the vision, engineering standards, and operational governance for Jefferies’ core infrastructure stack: database, virtualization, storage, backup, compute, Unix/Linux, and Windows server platforms, across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments.
  • Local Management of the Infrastructure Team: direct managerial responsibilities for Infrastructure Technology team members located in the Jefferies Pune office (Networks, Telecom, Digital Workplace, Cloud, CIP, Service Delivery).
  • Modernization & Cloud/Hybrid Adoption: Drive modernization, cloud/hybrid adoption, automation-first delivery, and standardization across all domains, balancing operational excellence with innovation and optimization. Lead strategic integration and optimal workload placement between on-premises and cloud resources, as business and regulatory requirements permit.
  • Hands-on Technical Escalation: Serve as the final point of escalation and technical incident lead during major outages, performance, or security incidents. Analyze real-time symptoms, ask the right diagnostic questions, and guide teams towards root-cause resolution.
  • Solution Delivery: Architect and deliver practical, high-impact solutions for business and application teams, actively collaborating with CIO leadership, BU leads, and local metro SVPs/VPs worldwide.
  • Operational Resilience: Own and continuously improve resilience, high-availability, recovery, and compliance strategies across the global platform estate.
  • Global Team Development: Partner with global leads in NYC, London, and HK to cultivate a high-performing, distributed team of engineers and architects, primarily based in India. You will mentor leaders and engineers, promote end-to-end ownership, and develop problem-solving capability.
  • Stakeholder Partnership: Partner with business units, application teams, and senior platform leaders to align technical priorities, communicate platform direction, and enable local-global business outcomes.
  • Technical Standards & Documentation: Author, maintain, and enforce robust operational standards, SLAs, playbooks, and knowledge base for platform operations and incident response.
  • Post-Incident Review & Learning: Lead technical post-mortems and deep-dives, drive remediation, and foster a culture of continuous technical learning.
  • Regulatory & Risk Alignment: Execute robust security, compliance, vulnerability management, and audit readiness for mission-critical infrastructure in a highly regulated financial services environment.

Mandatory Qualifications & Skills

  • Experience:
    • 15+ years in IT infrastructure/platform engineering and operations, with at least 5 years in global technical leadership (financial services or complex enterprise IT preferred).
    • Proven recent, hands-on experience with at least three of: database platforms (SQL/Oracle/etc), virtualization (VMware/Hyper-V/KVM, Nutanix), storage (SAN/NAS), backup/DR, Unix/Linux, and Windows server engineering and operations.
    • Track record as a solution owner, not just a conduit, able to independently architect and deliver technical outcomes in critical environments.
  • Core Competencies:
    • Deep technical expertise, able to lead troubleshooting, ask the right questions, synthesize technical indicators, and command resolution during platform issues and outages.
    • Domain credibility, regarded by engineers and senior IT partners as the go-to technical escalation contact.
    • Record of driving platform modernization, cloud/hybrid/cloud adoption, automation, and cost/risk optimization.
    • Strong foundation in regulatory, compliance, and operational risk management for infrastructure.
    • Executive presence, able to command trust in both technical and business forums, and partner with C-levels, application owners, and metro engineering leaders.
    • Outstanding stakeholder management, communication, prioritization, and conflict resolution skills, on both local (India) and global scales.
    • Experience designing and enforcing technical standards, SLAs, and incident management frameworks.
  • Certifications (optional, but valued):
    • Recognized certifications (RHCE, MCSE, VMware, Nutanix, NetApp, AWS/Azure/GCP, ITIL, etc.)

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or equivalent required; Master’s degree preferred.

What Success Looks Like

The SVP delivers a world-class platform that serves as a resilient, secure, continuously modernizing backbone for all Jefferies business applications, across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments. You lead actively, commanding incidents, delivering solutions, and growing your team’s technical and operational capability. You are trusted by engineers as a technical authority, by CIO/BU leaders as a business partner, and by the enterprise as the leader who enables robust, scalable solutions tightly aligned with the business's needs.

Equal Opportunity Employer: Jefferies values diversity and is committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Who You Are

You are dependable, organized, and enjoy working with technology. You take pride in doing things the right way, pay attention to the details, and enjoy solving problems. You are eager to learn, comfortable asking questions, and excited to build a career in enterprise IT while working alongside experienced technology professionals.

title: Director, Core IT Integration Delivery Lead
description:
Grant Thornton is seeking a Director, Core IT Integration Delivery Lead to join the team. Approved office locations can be found below.

Grant Thornton GTech’s vision is centered around enabling scalable, secure, and repeatable technology integration for acquired companies. The Core IT Integration Office is responsible for integrating acquired firms into the firm’s enterprise technology environment through a standardized, factory-style model that is governed centrally, executed through partners and in-country teams, and repeatable across the acquisition portfolio.

The Director, Core IT Integration - Technical Delivery Lead owns end-to-end technical delivery across the portfolio. The role is directly accountable for five Core IT components: tenant consolidation, ServiceNow, data migration and archival, network security, and branch office integration. It leads the workstream leads who own each of those components, sets sequencing and architecture direction across them, and manages the implementation partners and in-country resources that perform the work. Seven further Core IT components are delivered by Information Security, People & Culture, and Finance. This role does not deliver those, but is accountable for the sequencing seams between them and its own scope, so that dependencies hold and no entity stalls waiting on an unmanaged handoff.

Execution is delivered through implementation partners and regional resources. The Grant Thornton team owns the standard, the plan, the readiness decisions, the quality of what is delivered, and the outcome for the business. This role directs partner delivery rather than performing it, and is expected to know the technology well enough to review designs, question estimates, validate results, and make decisions under pressure. Scope decisions anchor to four tests: security, cost optimization, standardization, and enabling Global Delivery Center support.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Own the integrated technical delivery plan across the acquisition portfolio, sequencing entities into waves that balance entity priority, size, readiness, dependency, partner capacity, and business impact.
  • Manage concurrency across entities so that parallel execution stays within the delivery system’s throughput, and re-sequence when readiness, funding, or partner capacity changes.
  • Own delivery of tenant consolidation, covering migration of acquired Microsoft 365 and Entra tenants into the Grant Thornton tenant, including identity, mail, collaboration content, device management, and associated Azure subscription and workload moves.
  • Own delivery of ServiceNow onboarding for acquired entities, covering configuration data, service catalog and fulfillment alignment, support group structures, integrations, and transition into the enterprise support model.
  • Own delivery of data migration and archival, covering the Snowflake-based pipelines that feed system migrations and the durable archival of legacy data for retention, compliance, and future reuse.
  • Own delivery of network security, covering the Zero-Trust landing zone, regional hub readiness, segmentation, routing, and secure remote access for each acquisition.
  • Own delivery of branch office integration, covering connectivity, local network and endpoint baseline, site readiness, and retirement of inherited network infrastructure.
  • Coordinate with the owners of the remaining Core IT components, including identity directory sync, workforce systems, identity governance, security integration phases, intranet, and financial consolidation, managing dependencies and sequencing across those boundaries.
  • Sequence delivery to run concurrent with Information Security’s phased model rather than behind it, and manage the dependency under which full identity-driven security controls complete only after tenant consolidation.
  • Hold security review and sign-off as a gate before interconnect and go-live, and resist schedule pressure to bypass it.
  • Coordinate with the customer relationship management workstream and other capability programs that depend on Core IT sequencing, including where staffing sits outside this team.
  • Own and mature the integration factory model, increasing the share of each integration that runs to a standard pattern and reducing the variable component that drives cost and schedule risk.
  • Own the per-entity estimating model, including size banding, and maintain its accuracy by testing estimates against actuals as entities complete.
  • Manage cost per user and cost per entity as governed delivery metrics, working with partners and sourcing to improve unit economics as volume grows.
  • Prepare cost estimates, business cases, and variance analysis to support funding decisions made by Integration Office and Chief Technology Office leadership.
  • Direct implementation partners, systems integrators, and in-country resources through design, build, migration, cutover, and stabilization, holding delivery to enterprise standards, committed dates, and quality expectations.
  • Review and challenge partner designs, bills of materials, effort estimates, and delivery plans before acceptance, and confirm that what is proposed matches the standard rather than the partner’s default approach.
  • Support scoping, statement of work development, and commercial negotiation for integration partners, in coordination with sourcing, legal, and Integration Office leadership.
  • Evaluate delivery partners by region and workstream, maintaining competitive tension, regional coverage, and the ability to scale capacity up and down as the wave plan requires.
  • Establish readiness gates for each entity covering identity, data, endpoint, application, security, communications, and support coverage, and hold cutover decisions to documented evidence.
  • Lead cutover execution across workstreams, including runbooks, command center operations, go and no-go decisions, escalation paths, business validation, and defect triage.
  • Run hypercare after each migration, drive post-cutover issues to resolution, confirm exit criteria, and transition entities cleanly into steady-state support.
  • Deliver each entity into a condition that allows Global Delivery Center teams to support it at scale, and coordinate the support transition directly with the Global Delivery Center.
  • Track retirement of inherited infrastructure, licensing, and contracts after migration so that legacy run cost is removed rather than carried.
  • Run delivery to GTech project and portfolio management standards, including backlog management in Azure DevOps, integrated scheduling, RAID management, and Tier 1 program status reporting.
  • Represent Core IT technical delivery in enterprise Integration Management Office forums and coordinate waves with peer tracks across Information Security, Data, People & Culture, and Finance.
  • Provide executive-ready reporting on progress, risk, cost, partner performance, readiness, and stabilization, calling out decisions needed rather than reporting activity alone.
  • Lead the workstream leads accountable for tenant consolidation, ServiceNow, data migration and archival, and network and branch office integration, setting direction, priorities, and performance expectations.
  • Build and develop the dedicated Grant Thornton integration team, including recruiting, onboarding, capability development, and bench depth sufficient to run multiple entities concurrently.
  • Define the operating model between the dedicated Grant Thornton team and partner-supplied regional capacity, and adjust it as the portfolio scales.
  • Lead delivery across multiple countries and time zones, working through local technology leadership and in-country resources.
  • Account for jurisdictional requirements in entity planning, including data residency, privacy, statutory retention, local procurement, and equipment import constraints.
  • Build and maintain working relationships with acquired-firm technology leadership through the transition, providing enough clarity on timing and impact for local teams to plan around the work.
  • Advise due diligence and pre-close assessment activity led by Enterprise Architecture and other teams, contributing integration sizing, sequencing, and feasibility input without owning the assessment.
  • Own the post-entity lessons learned process and convert findings into playbook updates, readiness gates, estimating revisions, and backlog items visibly reflected in the next entity’s plan.
  • Maintain the technical delivery playbooks, standard designs, runbooks, and readiness checklists that make each successive integration faster and more predictable than the last.
  • Lead cross-functional teams through ambiguity, competing priorities, and acquisition-driven timelines while maintaining controls and decision discipline.
  • Influence stakeholders across functions without relying on formal authority, ensuring decisions are made in time to protect the schedule.
  • Maintain high professional standards, protect confidential acquisition information, and communicate with clarity and precision.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise technology delivery, infrastructure, platform implementation, or technology program leadership, including accountability for multi-workstream delivery.
  • Demonstrated experience leading concurrent implementations across identity, collaboration, service management, network, and data workstreams, with enough technical depth in each to review designs and make decisions without deferring.
  • Experience leading Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and Azure migration or consolidation programs, including tenant-to-tenant migration and the identity dependencies that govern sequencing.
  • Working knowledge of enterprise network security architecture, including segmentation, cloud landing zones, hub topologies, and secure remote access.
  • Working knowledge of enterprise service management platforms and the configuration data, support structures, and process alignment required to onboard a new entity.
  • Working knowledge of enterprise data migration and archival patterns, including pipeline-driven migration and long-term retention of legacy data.
  • Experience directing delivery through third-party implementation partners and offshore teams, including scope definition, deliverable review, estimate challenge, and performance management.
  • Track record of leading cutovers for business-critical platforms, including readiness criteria, go and no-go decisions, escalation management, and hypercare.
  • Experience building repeatable delivery models, factory approaches, or standardized playbooks applied across multiple entities or business units.
  • Experience leading and developing technical leaders, including workstream or team leads.
  • Strong planning and program management discipline, including backlog management, integrated scheduling, dependency tracking, RAID, and executive reporting.
  • Experience preparing cost estimates and business cases, and managing delivery against unit-cost targets.
  • Ability to lead delivery across multiple countries and time zones, working through local leadership and regional resources.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level decision materials and practical direction to engineering and partner teams.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field required; advanced degree or relevant certifications preferred.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience supporting merger, acquisition, divestiture, or carve-out technology integration, particularly in a serial acquirer or private equity backed environment.
  • Experience integrating acquisitions across multiple countries, including data residency, language, telephony, procurement, and in-country support considerations.
  • Familiarity with the platforms in scope, including Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, Azure networking, next-generation firewall and secure access platforms, ServiceNow, and Snowflake.
  • Experience transitioning integrated entities into a global delivery center, shared service, or managed service support model.
  • Experience retiring inherited technology estates, including decommissioning, contract wind-down, and removal of legacy run cost.
  • Familiarity with enterprise architecture review processes, cybersecurity control requirements, and IT service management operating models.
  • Experience contributing integration feasibility and sizing input to due diligence or pre-close assessment activity.
  • Experience developing partner performance scorecards, delivery governance routines, and repeatable readiness models.
  • Experience operating in a professional services, consulting, accounting, or complex global enterprise environment.

Success Measures

  • Entity integrations are delivered on schedule and within the approved cost envelope, without material disruption to client service or business operations.
  • The share of each integration that runs to the standard factory pattern increases across successive waves, and variable scope is identified during discovery rather than during execution.
  • Cost per user and cost per entity decline as the model matures, and estimating accuracy improves as measured against actuals.
  • Portfolio throughput increases, measured as entities completed per period, without proportional growth in dedicated headcount.
  • Consolidated entities reach the condition that allows full identity-driven security controls to complete.
  • Entities transition into Global Delivery Center supportable condition at go-live rather than after an extended stabilization period.
  • Inherited infrastructure, licensing, and contracts are retired on a tracked schedule after migration, with the associated run cost removed.
  • Dependencies across components delivered by other teams are managed so that no entity stalls on an unowned handoff.
  • Partner designs, estimates, and deliverables are reviewed and challenged before acceptance, and rework from late findings declines over time.
  • Lessons learned from each entity are visibly reflected in the plan for the next.
  • Workstream leads operate with clear direction and increasing autonomy, and the team can run multiple entities concurrently.

Reporting Relationship

This roles reports to the Head of Enterprise Architecture.

The base salary range for this position is between $184,000 and $276,000. Placement within the pay range is at Grant Thornton’s discretion, and it is based on multiple factors, including but not limited to, job-related knowledge/skills, experience, business needs, progression within the role, geographic location, and internal equity. At Grant Thornton, compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each position and candidate.

title: AI Engineer
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Where AI Meets Medicine: Build the Future of Drug Discovery in the Heart of Silicon Valley!

Making medicine that’s never been made means doing what’s never been done. If you’re an engineer, scientist, or builder who thrives on problems no one has solved before, this is your invitation; we want you on the team. We are ready to challenge the status quo and push medicine forward, all in the name of health. Are you up for the challenge? If so, join us!

About the Lilly and NVIDIA Partnership

Lilly and NVIDIA are launching a new AI co-innovation lab in the heart of Silicon Valley — an up-to-$1 billion, multi-year commitment to solve drug discovery’s toughest challenges. The lab brings Lilly scientists, technologists, chemists and biologists together with NVIDIA engineers under one roof. Together, we are building purpose-built foundation and frontier AI models trained on Lilly data at scale, tightening the feedback loop between automated wet labs and computational dry labs, designing the next generation of medicines for millions of patients across the globe.

What You’ll Be Doing

As an AI Engineer, you will turn advanced AI models into reliable tools that support drug discovery. You will build, train, evaluate, and deploy AI systems, working closely with AI Scientists to shape model design and technical decisions. This is a hands-on role with opportunities to contribute to both engineering and scientific innovation. You'll collaborate with AI Scientists, ML Ops Engineers, Data Engineers, and NVIDIA experts to develop cutting-edge AI solutions.

How You’ll Succeed

  • AI and Automation Execution: Develop and apply innovative AI techniques to solve complex business challenges, creating tailored solutions that drive strategic value and transform clinical research processes that support AI scientists.
  • Full Stack Development: Build and implement AI-driven models and applications across the full stack, from backend services to frontend interfaces.
  • System Architecture and Design: Design and uphold resilient system architectures to guarantee optimal performance, scalability, and security across all platforms.
  • Handle large scale model development.
  • Cross-Disciplinary and Organization Collaboration: Effectively engage with colleagues to gather innovative ideas and insights, fostering a collaborative environment that inspires and motivates team members to innovate and explore creative solutions in AI development.
  • Ethics and Compliance in Development: Adhere to ethical guidelines in AI usage and data handling, ensuring compliance with all relevant regulations and maintaining the highest standards of data privacy and security.
  • Elevate engineering excellence through architecture reviews, code quality leadership, and mentorship, while safeguarding Lilly's proprietary data, models, and intellectual property.

What You Should Bring

  • Advanced Python with production experience in PyTorch or JAX, and a track record of taking machine learning models from research code to working systems.
  • Hands-on distributed training on multi-GPU, multi-node infrastructure (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, or Megatron), with GPU performance profiling and optimization.
  • Experience optimizing and serving models for inference (Triton, vLLM, or TensorRT-LLM) with containerization and scheduling (Docker, Kubernetes, Ray, or Slurm).
  • Experience building evaluation and benchmarking for models — including designing the tests that reveal where a model fails, not only where it succeeds.
  • Full stack capability — a backend language, front-end familiarity (JavaScript with a framework such as React), and API design — enough to build the interfaces through which scientists actually use a model.
  • Comfort with the scientific Python stack (NumPy, SciPy, Pandas); C++ or CUDA for performance-critical work is a strong plus.
  • Experience with cloud AI/ML platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) alongside on-premises GPU clusters.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to navigate ambiguity in a highly technical environment.
  • Strong written and verbal communication and demonstrated ability to partner well with research scientists.
  • Experience with distributed training or large-scale model deployment on GPU infrastructure.
  • Prior experience working across the full stack of an AI application — data, model, service, and interface.

Your Basic Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • 4+ years of hands-on engineering experience building machine learning systems, including taking models from research or prototype into real working use.

Location & Work Flexibility
This role is based at our Silicon Valley Hub. We offer a flexible hybrid work model, with three days onsite and two days working remotely each week, supporting both collaboration and work‑life balance.

description:
About Our Job

What We Offer

The City and County of Denver offers a competitive salary commensurate with education and experience. The full pay range for this position is $39.56 - $61.32 an hour, based on your experience and education. We also offer generous benefits for full-time employees which include but is not limited to:

  • Free RTD Eco Pass
  • Competitive medical, dental and vision plans effective within 1 month of start date

Location

This position reports on site at the Republic Plaza building located at 370 17th St, Denver, CO 80202, Monday through Friday 8:00AM - 5:00PM.

Who We Are

The Mission of the Denver District Attorney's Office is to professionally and competently prosecute crimes and investigate criminal activity on behalf of the people of the State of Colorado and to seek equal justice for all in the criminal justice system. Our mission also includes the prevention and deterrence of crimes, supporting the well-being of victims, participating in the community, being transparent and accountable, and, improving the criminal justice system to provide fair alternatives to incarceration in appropriate cases.

What You'll Do

As a Firearms Relinquishment Criminal Investigator you will be responsible for proper case investigations, interview complainants, victims and witnesses as well as periodically consult with complainants and victims regarding the progress of cases until they have been officially closed. Through investigative procedures, investigators will direct their best efforts in the prevention and suppression of crime, and in the detection and apprehension of criminal suspects.

Additional Firearms Relinquishment Criminal Investigator duties include:

  • Reviews all new domestic violence cases filed by Denver Police, including all reports and witness statements, as well as all relevant criminal justice and social media databases, in order to determine if there are firearms in the home and/or in the control of the charged suspect(s)
  • Documents all information relating to firearms in the DA internal database
  • Determines investigative techniques and case strategies; gathers, evaluates, and preserves evidence, analyzes the evidence, prepares spreadsheets or summary charts on financial or voluminous data, and determines the presence or absence of criminal activity
  • Prepares affidavits for arrest warrant, search warrants, and subpoenas, serves parties involved in legal action, and may prepare interrogatories, production requests, and answers in civil litigation
  • Provide reasonably requested information and assistance to other units within the Office of the District Attorney and maintain an efficient level of cooperation and coordination in affected areas. Assist and maintain close cooperation and positive working relationships with other law enforcement agencies
  • Other duties as assigned

This position requires certification as a Colorado Peace Officer (POST) at the time of application, and requires a valid Driver’s License at the time of application. Please do not apply if you do not possess these certifications.

We appreciate your interest and are excited for the opportunity to build a strong team for the City and County of Denver.

What You'll Bring

Our ideal candidate will have all or some of the following:

  • 5+ years of professional level experience conducting comprehensive investigations of complex criminal and civil cases
  • POST certified and familiarity with drafting arrest/search warrants
  • Familiarity with criminal justice databases
  • Familiarity with the use of social media databases
  • Background in investigating cases involving family violence with a particular emphasis on intimate partner violence
  • Bilingual in another foreign language strongly preferred

Required Minimum Qualifications

We realize your time is valuable so please do not apply if you do not have at least the following required minimum qualifications:

  • Education requirement: Bachelor's Degree in Criminal Justice or a related field
  • Experience Requirement: Four (4) years of previous police experience, two (2) of which must be at the level of Criminal Investigator (e.g. Police Detective) or any equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Education/Experience Equivalency: One (1) year of the appropriate type and level of experience may be substituted for each required year of post-high school education.

Additional appropriate education may be substituted for the minimum experience requirements

  • License/Certifications: A valid Driver's License at the time of application. Requires a certification as a Colorado Peace Officer (POST) at the time of application. Licenses and certifications must be kept current as a condition of employment

Required Documents

To be considered for this position, you must include the following on your job application (upload the multiple attachment(s) to the Resume/CV section on the My Experience tab):

  • Resume
  • A redacted copy of your most recent arrest or search warrant you wrote

Application Deadline

title: Data Modeler
description:
About the Role

As a Data Modeler at TVH, you will play a central role in shaping how our global organization structures, understands, and leverages its data. Operating across all core business domains (e.g., Customer, Supplier, Item, Product, Equipment, HR, Finance, Commercial, Operations, …), you will design, develop, and maintain high-performing Logical Data Models (LDM) and Physical Data Models (PDM) that power enterprise reporting, analytics, and operational applications.

You will translate diverse cross-domain business requirements into clear, standardized, and scalable data structures. Working closely with Domain Architects, Data Engineers, and Data Stewards, you will ensure our logical abstractions align perfectly with business reality while our physical implementations maximize database performance and data accessibility.

Key Responsibilities

  • Enterprise Logical & Physical Data Model Design:

    • Design, construct, and maintain normalized Conceptual and Logical Data Models (LDM) across all enterprise domains, establishing clear entities, attributes, relationships, and business definitions.

    • Translate LDMs into optimized Physical Data Models (PDM) tailored for target database platforms, balancing storage efficiency, index strategies, and query performance.

    • Reverse-engineer legacy source systems and translate complex domain requirements into normalized, reusable data structures.

    • Produce and manage comprehensive data documentation, including ERDs (Entity-Relationship Diagrams), data dictionaries, and data mapping lineage.

  • Domain Alignment & Standards Governance:

    • Drive consistent data modeling standards, naming conventions, and design patterns across all domain modeling initiatives.

    • Partner with Data Governance teams to incorporate standardized business glossaries and enterprise metadata standards directly into model structures.

    • Conduct data model reviews with technical and business teams to ensure cross-domain consistency and avoid data duplication.

  • Cross-Functional Technical Collaboration:

    • Work hand-in-hand with Domain Architects to ensure domain models fit seamlessly into TVH’s target data architecture strategy.

    • Collaborate with Data Engineers to guide the physical realization of models and support optimized ETL/ELT pipeline design.

    • Partner with Data Analysts, Data Stewards and Business Partners to validate logical assumptions, clarify business logic, and refine domain models as needs evolve.

  • Model Optimization & Quality:

    • Profile source data using SQL to uncover structural edge cases and validate cardinality before finalizing logical designs.

    • Refine physical schemas for cloud data warehouses, adjusting partitioning, clustering, and denormalization strategies to meet performance SLAs.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience focused specifically on Logical Data Modeling (LDM) and Physical Data Modeling (PDM) across multiple business domains.

  • Deep expertise in diverse modeling paradigms: Relational/Entity-Relationship (3NF), Dimensional Modeling (Star/Snowflake), and Denormalization concepts.

  • Strong proficiency in SQL for deep source system profiling, data mapping, and schema validation.

  • Hands-on experience with modern cloud data warehouses (preferably GCP BigQuery, Snowflake, or Databricks) and relational database platforms.

  • Proficiency with enterprise data modeling tools (e.g., Erwin, PowerDesigner, SqlDBM, or similar).

  • Solid understanding of Data Warehousing principles, metadata management, and ETL/ELT architecture.

  • Fluent in English with excellent communication skills to articulate complex logical structures to both business stakeholders and engineering teams.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with Data Vault 2.0 modeling methodologies for enterprise scale.

  • Exposure to real-time or streaming data modeling patterns (Event-driven architectures).

  • Understanding of data privacy impact on data design (e.g., handling PII attributes across global domains).

  • Experience working in Agile/Scrum distributed software delivery teams.

title: Project Manager
description:
Why DataMap

DataMap builds really cool technology and implements, integrates, and runs source-to-pay for some of the largest companies in the world, including Google. Coupa named us Innovation Partner of the Year in 2026, and Coupa points customers to us for Microsoft ERP integrations. We are also a Microsoft, Boomi, SAP, and Oracle partner, and most of our work sits where finance process meets system design.

We perform enterprise-scale work. Projects run on real deadlines and real budgets, the people who trained you are still in the room, and a project manager who keeps a program on the rails is noticed by clients and by leadership.

We are an AI-first company. Project managers here work with AI in the loop on planning, status reporting, and documentation, and it changes what one person can carry.

How we hire

Apply, and you'll get a nine-minute problem-solving assessment. That's the entire first round. Based on scores and the number of applicants, the next step is an interview.

The role

The Project Manager owns delivery of Coupa implementations end to end: procure-to-pay, invoicing, Coupa Pay, expenses, sourcing, contract lifecycle management, and supplier enablement, plus the ERP integrations that go with them (NetSuite, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Acumatica, Workday, Oracle, and others).

You are the single point of accountability for your accounts from SOW signature through go-live, hypercare, and handoff to production support. You run the plan, the budget, the client relationship, and the change management workstream, and you lead our functional consultants, integration developers, and solution architects alongside client sponsors, their finance and IT teams, and Coupa's own team. You also identify expansion opportunities on your accounts and follow through to close them.

This is a client-facing role for someone who has delivered enterprise software in a consulting or IT project environment and wants real ownership.

  • Reports to: VP of Operations
  • Location: Based at our Overland Park, KS headquarters. Relocation assistance is available.
  • Travel: Rare. Most work is delivered from Overland Park. A specific project may require travel depending on customer needs.
  • Compensation: $80,000 to $110,000 base plus performance bonus, depending on experience
  • Eligibility: Must be authorized to work in the United States

What you'll do

Own delivery

  • Plan and run Coupa implementations from kickoff to hypercare exit: scope, timeline, resource plan, RAID log, weekly status reports, and steering committee cadence
  • Manage the engagement budget: track hours and actuals against the SOW baseline, forecast utilization, and protect margin
  • Drive the delivery workstreams (design, reference data collection, integration design and testing, UAT, cutover) to milestones, and manage ERP and third-party dependencies
  • Chair kickoff, weekly client status, and steering committee meetings, and produce executive-ready decks and decision logs
  • Run the formal readiness assessment and go-live sign-off with the client PM and sponsor as the gate for exiting hypercare and closing the engagement
  • Lead the consultants on your engagements rather than just scheduling them: set the bar, then hold them to it so deliverables are delivered, customer expectations are exceeded, and adoption is achieved

Own the commercial relationship

  • Support SOW scoping and estimates with Sales and delivery leadership, and hold the line on scope once signed
  • Identify out-of-scope requests early and convert them into change orders
  • Support milestone invoicing and month-end revenue reporting for your engagements
  • Identify expansion opportunities on your accounts and follow through with Sales and Customer Success to close them, along with production support and renewals

Own change management and adoption

  • Run the organizational change management workstream: stakeholder analysis, change impact assessment, and readiness planning
  • Build and execute communication plans for executive sponsors, business owners, end users, and suppliers, and coordinate with supplier enablement on onboarding and go-live outreach
  • Mobilize a client-side change network of sponsors, champions, and super users
  • Define the training approach and run a train-the-trainer model so the client is self-sufficient at handoff
  • Track adoption after go-live, identify resistance and capability gaps, and drive reinforcement through handoff
  • Lead the consultants on the change workstream the same way: set the bar, then hold them to it so communications and training land, customer expectations are exceeded, and adoption is achieved

Build the practice

  • Contribute to DataMap's delivery methodology: playbooks, templates, and status and readiness artifacts
  • Direct the Project Coordinators assigned to your engagements
  • Bring AI tooling into planning, reporting, and documentation, and share what works

What success looks like in the first year

  • Your engagements deliver on time and on budget, with margin at or above plan
  • Weekly status reports and RAID logs go out on cadence for every account, with no surprises at steering committee
  • Out-of-scope work is captured in signed change orders rather than absorbed
  • Clients sign formal readiness and go-live acceptance, and hypercare exits on schedule
  • Client satisfaction on your accounts is strong enough that they reference us and buy again
  • At least one template or process improvement you authored is in use across the practice

Where it leads

We promote from within, and quickly for people who earn it. Project Managers here typically move toward:

  • Senior Project Manager, running our largest and most complex Coupa programs and a portfolio of concurrent engagements
  • Director of Project Management, owning methodology, staffing, and delivery performance across the practice and leading the PM team

What we're looking for

Required

  • 3+ years of project management experience delivering enterprise software, ERP, or SaaS implementations
  • Led projects independently with budget accountability and delivered them on time and within scope
  • Managed client stakeholders, including executive sponsors, and run status and steering meetings
  • Hands-on experience with change management activities on an implementation: stakeholder communications, training coordination, readiness planning, and adoption tracking
  • Strong command of project planning, critical path, dependency tracking, and delivery tooling (Smartsheet, Jira, MS Project, or similar)
  • Clear written and verbal communication and executive-ready documentation
  • Managed multiple concurrent projects while keeping each on track
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience

Preferred

  • Consulting or professional services experience with services revenue or utilization accountability
  • Delivered Coupa implementations (P2P, Invoicing, Pay, Expenses, Sourcing, CLM, Supplier Management) or another source-to-pay platform
  • Working knowledge of procure-to-pay and accounts payable processes: requisitions, purchase orders, invoice matching, approvals, payments, and expense reporting
  • Familiarity with ERP integrations (NetSuite, SAP, Dynamics 365, Acumatica, Workday, Oracle) and integration concepts (REST APIs, SSO/SAML, iPaaS such as Boomi or Workato) sufficient to partner with developers
  • PMP, CAPM, or CSM; Prosci/ADKAR; Coupa certification

Benefits

  • Competitive base salary and performance-based bonuses
  • Unlimited vacation and a flexible work environment
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Health insurance with a generous employer contribution
  • Hands-on mentorship and paid certifications

Apply

If you don't meet every requirement, apply anyway. We'd rather hear from people with strong delivery instincts than wait for a perfect resume.

DataMap is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. If you need an accommodation during the application or interview process, let us know.

title: Person In Charge (PIC)
description:

Job Description: As a primary contact for customers, the Person In Charge (PIC) provides friendly, courteous, and helpful service. During the absence of the Store Manager and the First & Second Assistant Managers, the PIC is in charge of the store, with analogous authority to make necessary decisions to operate the store at maximum profit, efficiency, and superior customer service. When in charge of the store (generally at night) the PIC will supervise the store employees. The PIC also acts as a Cashier-Checker (see job description). title: Principal Agentic Engineer
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


About the Team

Tech@Lilly builds and maintains capabilities using pioneering technologies like the most prominent tech companies. What differentiates Lilly IT is that we redefine what's possible through tech to advance our purpose, creating medicines that make life better for people around the world, including data-driven drug discovery, connected clinical trials, resilient enterprise platforms, and intelligent digital operations. We hire the best technology professionals from a variety of backgrounds, so they can bring an assortment of knowledge, skills, and diverse thinking to deliver creative solutions in every area of our business.

The Digital Core team leads Lilly's transformation into the Digital and AI era. They inspire digitally empowered teams to new ways of working and accelerate innovation and agility. This team powers and advances the entire company by building and maintaining world-class technology capabilities and platforms.

Lilly Capability Centre India (LCCI), Hyderabad, is Lilly's premier Global Technology Hub, harnessing data, AI, analytics, and digital solutions to revolutionize healthcare and improve patient outcomes worldwide.

Role summary

You own the agentic resolution platform end to end — both the cloud-native substrate it runs on and the intelligent agents that run on top of it. From Kubernetes, CI/CD, and observability through agent runtime, LLM patterns, retrieval, evaluation, and human-in-the-loop boundaries, you write the production code, design the architecture, and set the engineering bar that lets automation deflect routine operational work before it ever reaches a human.

This is a senior individual-contributor role that is both strategic and deeply hands-on. You ship production platform services and agentic capabilities, make the build-vs-buy calls on tooling and model access, and partner with the senior architect on the patterns that scale. Success is measured by rising deflection, sustained toil reduction, platform availability and developer velocity, and the ability to scale agentic intelligence through systems and people — not individual effort.

What you'll be doing

1) Agentic resolution platform — intake to action

  • Architect the agentic resolution platform end to end: intake, classification, action execution, verification, and human-in-the-loop fallback.

  • Build the agent runtime and orchestration layer: agent state and memory, tool integration, multi-agent coordination patterns, and confidence-thresholded handoffs to humans.

  • Define agent-decision observability, audit-ready posture, and the data contracts that let the platform consume durable fixes from upstream engineering teams.

2) LLM application patterns, knowledge, and evaluation rigor

  • Design production LLM patterns: prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), structured outputs, multi-model routing, and hybrid retrieval over the knowledge corpus.

  • Own the knowledge-base strategy as a compounding deflection lever — every resolved incident becomes training data and structured retrieval input for future automation.

  • Establish evaluation and guardrail frameworks for non-deterministic systems: automated evals, quality scoring, drift detection, and feedback loops that compound agent quality over time.

3) Cloud-native platform — build and operate

  • Architect and operate Kubernetes (EKS or equivalent) at scale for container and serverless workloads supporting agentic and LLM inference traffic patterns.

  • Write production platform services and internal tooling (Python or Go) that automate provisioning, deployment, and operational workflows — not just infrastructure configuration.

  • Define and maintain infrastructure as code (Terraform) integrated with a major cloud's AI stack (AWS Bedrock/SageMaker, Azure AI Foundry, or Vertex AI), with secrets management and audit-ready posture for regulated environments.

4) CI/CD, observability, and developer experience

  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines tuned for agentic and AI workloads: model and agent versioning, canary rollouts, evaluation gates, and rollback.

  • Own the observability stack (Prometheus/Grafana/OpenTelemetry plus enterprise tooling) and instrument platform health, agent-decision telemetry, and model-inference metrics.

  • Establish SLOs, SLIs, and reliability standards for both platform and agentic system health; design self-service patterns and golden-path templates that accelerate delivery.

5) Cross-team partnership, security, and talent development

  • Partner with the Reliability Engineering team on which production patterns become agent-assisted automations, and with senior architects on the patterns that scale.

  • Own security posture: network policies, pod security, secrets rotation, vulnerability scanning, and access controls in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.

  • Set the engineering bar through code quality standards, architectural reviews, and role modeling; mentor senior engineers in agentic AI, LLM application patterns, and platform engineering. Influence engineering leaders to adopt automation-friendly patterns at the source, not just downstream.

How you will succeed

  • Be recognized as the senior technical authority for agentic platform engineering in your area.

  • Demonstrate measurable, sustained improvements: rising deflection rates, reduced toil, fewer recurring incidents, faster resolution, platform uptime, and deployment velocity.

  • Ship production platform services and agentic capabilities that tangibly move the deflection and developer-experience numbers.

  • Scale agentic intelligence through systems, standards, and people — not individual heroics.

What you should bring

Required

  • 10+ years of progressive technology experience with substantial hands-on architecture and delivery of automation, AIOps, agentic systems, or cloud-native platforms at enterprise scale.

  • Demonstrated ownership of measurable deflection or operational-toil-reduction outcomes in a production environment — with the numbers to show it.

  • Deep technical fluency in agentic system design: agent runtimes, multi-agent orchestration, tool integration, memory and state management. Practical experience with at least one major framework (LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or MCP).

  • Production experience with LLM application patterns: prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), structured outputs, and multi-model routing.

  • Deep cloud-native background: Kubernetes (EKS or equivalent) at scale, container workloads, infrastructure as code (Terraform), and at least one major cloud's AI stack (AWS Bedrock/SageMaker, Azure AI Foundry, or Vertex AI).

  • Proven ability to build and ship production platform services and tooling — not just configure infrastructure. Expert-level Python (async, packaging, performance) for production services; Go also welcome.

  • Strong CI/CD engineering experience for AI and agentic workloads: model and agent deployment, versioning, canary/blue-green strategies, evaluation gates, and rollback.

  • Observability for AI systems: metrics, logs, traces, and agent-decision telemetry using Prometheus/Grafana/OpenTelemetry, plus at least one enterprise stack (Splunk, Datadog, or Dynatrace).

  • Demonstrated rigor in evaluation and guardrails for non-deterministic systems — automated evals, drift detection, human-in-the-loop verification, and feedback loops.

  • Strong security engineering foundation: network policies, secrets management, vulnerability scanning, and access controls in regulated environments.

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a closely related field.

  • Exceptional communication skills, including the ability to translate technical strategy for senior business and technology leadership.

This is a hybrid role spanning agentic AI, LLM patterns, cloud-native platform, and developer tooling. We expect strong depth in 2–3 of these areas with the breadth and judgment to learn adjacent domains. Not every tool listed is required.

Preferred

  • Working knowledge of operational ML: anomaly detection, event correlation, alert-noise reduction, and model/agent monitoring in production.

  • Experience with AI observability tooling (e.g., LangSmith, Weights & Biases, custom telemetry pipelines).

  • Hands-on experience with ServiceNow integration patterns and chat-based intake platforms (e.g., Microsoft Teams).

  • Experience with vector databases and hybrid retrieval architectures.

  • Experience building internal developer platforms (IDP), self-service provisioning, or platform-as-a-product tooling.

  • Backend development skills beyond infrastructure tooling: REST/gRPC API design, database design, message queues, distributed systems patterns.

  • Experience with policy-as-code, automated compliance checks, or shift-left security tooling.

  • AWS cloud platform fluency, including EKS, Bedrock, SageMaker, and cost-optimization tooling.

  • Familiarity with FinOps practices and cloud cost governance.

  • Experience operating in highly regulated industries (life sciences, financial services, healthcare).

  • Prior experience standing up a new engineering capability from a small founding team.

  • Frontend experience (React, TypeScript) for internal dashboards and developer portals.

Leadership expectations

  • Acts with enterprise-first mindset, beyond individual products or teams.

  • Drives accountability, clarity, and engineering rigor across the team.

  • Builds trust through consistency, technical depth, and follow-through.

  • Raises the capability of the organization, not just personal output.

  • Leads through what they build and how they write, not through org-chart authority.

Additional information

Availability to work flexible work hours is/may be required. This team supports continuous operations and may require non-standard work hours, including some work on weekends and holidays. Appropriate adjustments in benefits will be provided for employees working non-standard hours where applicable.

title: 71.SCHOOL SECU COOR (200).078
description:
Human Resources announces openings for a 1.0 FTE School Security Coordinator position. This is a 200-days, Grade N-SS position. GENERAL STATEMENT OF DUTIES Under the general direction of the Lead School Safety Coordinator (SSC) is responsible
for maintaining order and discipline by providing safety and protection for students, staff, equipment, and property. This
position ensures compliance with applicable laws, codes, rules, and regulations; responds to fire and intrusion alarms in
addition to helping staff, students, parents, citizens, and public agencies. SSCs are expected to model and promote a
positive, productive, and safe campus climate. This position has no law enforcement authority.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE CLASS
(May not include all duties performed.)
Initiate contact with individuals on school grounds or surrounding property to assure visitor authorization. Manages
school access by monitoring gates and other points of entry throughout the school to ensure that students possess
permission to leave school grounds, parents, visitors, vendors, and contractors are appropriately identified and escorted.
Assists administration in performing searches of students and school property. Deescalates confrontations between
students, parents, visitors, and community members while on school property. Escorts students to and from class and the
main office as requested by administrators and staff. Assist administrators and law enforcement during emergency drills,
investigations, and safety inspections. Maintain a high level of visibility on campus through hallway foot patrols of
assigned areas during, before and after school hours. Oversees and coordinates parking and bus regulations on school
grounds and reports accidents on school property. Monitor and assist in controlling crowds at special and athletic events;
observe and report misuse of facilities, vandalism, or other unauthorized activities. Work collaboratively with school site
administration and law enforcement personnel in the coordination of security services. Responds to inquiries from
students and parents regarding campus security issues for the purpose of providing information, direction and/or referral
for addressing inquiry. Report observances of any evident pertaining to criminal activity to school administration and law
enforcement authorities as directed. Assists with developing effective school-community relations and in maintaining a
human relations climate which promotes a positive school environment. Participate in required training and professional
development as it relates to the responsibilities and functions of the position.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
PHYSICAL ATTRIBUTES The usual and customary methods of performing the job's functions require the following physical
demands: walking, running, lifting, carrying, pushing, and/or pulling; some stooping, kneeling, crouching, and/or crawling. Generally,
the work requires 10% sitting, 70% walking, and 20% standing. The job is performed under temperature extremes and under
conditions with some exposure to risk of injury and/or illness.
HAZARDS/UNUSUAL DEMANDS
May be required to testify in court. May be required to operate school vehicles in the performance of assigned duties. Observation
and supervision of parent pick-up and drop-off traffic areas may be needed at times but at no times will traffic control and/or directing
traffic be performed by the School Safety Coordinator.
EXPERIENCE:
REQUIRED EDUCATION, TRAINING, AND EXPERIENCE
High School Diploma or equivalent (e.g., General Education Development, G.E.D.) required. Bachelor’s Degree in Law Enforcement,
Criminal Justice, Security Management, Homeland Security, or a related field preferred. Must be 21 years of age or older and
successfully pass a finger-print background check. Two (2) years of experience or training in a security related field is required.
Experience providing safety/security in an education setting (i.e., K-12, high-education, etc.) is preferred. LICENSE/CERTIFICATION
A valid state issued Driver’s License. Must possess a School Security Officer (SSO) Certification as defined by the Virginia Code or
be able to obtain it within 30 days of assignment/hire.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES
This position requires the skills to perform multiple tasks with a potential need to upgrade skills to meet changing job conditions.
Specific skill-based competencies required to satisfactorily perform the functions of the job include adhering to safety practices;
operating standard office equipment including software; preparing and maintaining accurate records. This position requires the
knowledge to perform basic math; understand written procedures, write routine documents, and speak clearly; and analyze
situations to define issues and draw conclusions. Specific knowledge-based competencies required to satisfactorily perform the
functions of the job include health standards and hazards, safety practices and procedures. This position requires the ability to
schedule activities; gather and/or collate data; and use basic, job-related equipment. Flexibility is required to work with others in a
wide variety of circumstances: work with data utilizing specific, defined processes; and operate equipment using standardized
methods. Ability is also required to work with a diversity of individuals and/or groups; work with a variety of data; and utilize a variety
of job-related equipment. Problem solving is required to analyze issues and create action plans. Specific ability-based competencies
required to satisfactorily perform the functions of the job include adapting to changing work priorities. communicating with diverse
groups; maintaining confidentiality; working as part of a team. setting priorities; working with frequent and sustained interruptions.

title: Vikarier på Hunddagis 2026
description:
Timvikarier till hunddagis i Stockholm – för dig som verkligen kan hundar!

Har du praktisk erfarenhet av hundar, tycker om ett aktivt arbete och är en person som andra kan lita på? Då kanske du passar i vårt vikarie­team på Emerita!

Vi söker flexibla timvikarier som kan arbeta på våra olika hunddagis i Stockholmsområdet. Du hoppar in när ordinarie personal är sjuk eller har semester, men också när vi behöver extra hjälp – exempelvis vid inskolning av nya hundar eller under perioder med högre arbetsbelastning.

Arbetet passar dig som uppskattar variation och kan vara flexibel både när det gäller arbetstider och arbetsplats. Ibland kan behovet uppstå med kort varsel. Därför är det mycket viktigt att du regelbundet läser och svarar på våra samtal och meddelanden – även om svaret är att du inte kan arbeta just den dagen. Vi söker personer som är lätta att få kontakt med, kommunicerar tydligt och inte lämnar meddelanden obesvarade.

Vem söker vi?

Vi söker dig som:

  • har praktisk erfarenhet av att hantera och arbeta med hundar
  • kan läsa hundars kroppsspråk och känner dig trygg med olika raser, storlekar och personligheter
  • är aktiv och trivs med långa promenader utomhus i alla väder
  • är flexibel och kan hoppa in vid sjukdom, semester och andra personalbehov
  • är ansvarsfull, punktlig och tar hundarnas trygghet och säkerhet på stort allvar
  • är uppmärksam, initiativtagande och kan behålla lugnet i olika situationer
  • kan arbeta både självständigt och tillsammans med andra
  • svarar på samtal och meddelanden och meddelar tydligt om du kan arbeta eller inte

Erfarenhet från hunddagis, hundrastning, kennel, hundpensionat, djurvård eller liknande är meriterande. Även lång och gedigen praktisk erfarenhet av egna hundar kan vara relevant.

Vi söker inte bara någon som tycker om hundar – vi söker dig som förstår dem, kan hantera dem tryggt och är beredd att ta ett verkligt ansvar för deras vardag.

Språk

I vår internationella arbetsgrupp talar vi svenska, engelska, ryska och ukrainska.

För vissa placeringar kan du söka även om du ännu inte talar svenska eller engelska, förutsatt att du kan kommunicera tydligt med de kollegor du arbetar tillsammans med. Ange i din ansökan vilka språk du talar och på vilken nivå.

Körkort

På vissa av våra arbetsplatser är B-körkort ett krav. Ange därför tydligt i din ansökan om du har B-körkort och känner dig trygg med att köra bil.

Anställning

Anställningen är på timbasis och arbetstiderna varierar utifrån verksamhetens behov.

Vi söker i första hand dig som vill arbeta med oss åtminstone under hela den kommande säsongen, från september till augusti, och bli en återkommande och viktig del av vårt vikarie­team.

Skicka din ansökan och berätta:

  • vilken praktisk erfarenhet du har av hundar
  • varför du tror att du skulle passa i vårt team
  • när och hur flexibelt du kan arbeta
  • vilka delar av Stockholm du kan arbeta i
  • vilka språk du talar
  • om du har B-körkort

Välkommen med din ansökan till Emerita – vi ser fram emot att lära känna dig!
