title: Intern | Competition Practice | Helsinki
description:
Who We Are:

We are one of the world’s leading economic consulting firms. We strive to recruit and develop talented people to work together to produce meaningful economic analysis of exceptional quality, and to create a positive impact on our clients and society.

Our Competition Practice provides expert economic advice on competition policy, economic and financial regulation, public policy and the assessment of damages in complex disputes.

We are looking to hire junior economists to help us to provide advice to our clients on some of the most high-profile cases before the European Commission, the General Court and national competition authorities, regulators and courts.

We believe that working in diverse teams, where everybody’s views are considered and respected, helps us to deliver work of the highest standards of quality and integrity.

About the role:

We pride ourselves on providing Interns with an opportunity to make a significant impact from day one. As an Intern you will gain extensive hands-on experience of working at an economic consultancy. You will contribute to cases in a variety of ways, working closely with senior staff to understand the issues that face the client, relating those issues to relevant economic theory, and supporting the analysis with solid and persuasive empirical evidence.

Interns typically join us for 3 to 6 months during, in-between, or shortly after completing their economics degree(s). Please indicate in your cover letter when you would be available to start your internship.

For those applying whilst completing their Bachelor's degree, please note that our Intern candidates are usually hired in their final year. We would consider only exceptional second-year students. If you are in your second year and unsuccessful in your application, we would encourage you to apply again next year.

Key responsibilities:

  • Analysing qualitative and quantitative client data to better understand how competition works in their industry

  • Reviewing literature and contributing to discussions about the theoretical and empirical approach

  • Conducting empirical analysis using Excel and Stata

  • Drafting reports summarising analysis

  • Participating in client meetings and conference calls

Skills/profile sought:

  • Currently undertaking or recently completed Bachelor’s (final year only), Master’s, or Ph.D. in economics from a leading university, ideally with focus on microeconomics, and econometrics. Study of Industrial organisation would be desirable.

  • Highly analytical

  • Strong organisational and communication skills

  • Accuracy and attention to detail

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team

  • Stata and Excel skills desirable

  • Fluency in English and Finnish or a Scandinavian language

Benefits of working at Compass Lexecon:

  • Competitive salary and benefits

  • A wide variety of interesting and challenging projects

  • An international team with a broad range of backgrounds and experience

  • A blend of professional and academic environments

  • The opportunity to work with top law firms, corporations, government bodies and academics

  • A steep learning curve, coupled with a supportive and collaborative team

  • The opportunity to contribute from day one

For more information about Compass Lexecon and the role, please feel free to contact the Helsinki recruitment team via email at european.recruiting@compasslexecon.com.

When drafting your application:

Please note that applications for this position will close on 13th November 2026. If you are interested in this role, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

A complete application consists of a cover letter, CV, grades transcripts, an academic writing sample, and two academic references.

We acknowledge that AI is now commonly used for drafting, however we emphasize the importance of personalization to truly reflect your unique experiences. We are able to recognise applications that are solely created using AI and those that demonstrate individuality.

What does our interview process look like?

Our interview process for Interns includes one 60-minute interview with both motivational and technical questions. All interviews are currently being conducted virtually.

Compass Lexecon is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We appreciate that recruitment agencies may have speculative CVs that they wish to submit to Compass Lexecon. To avoid any ambiguity around fees, please note that speculative CVs received by Compass Lexecon, that have not been authorised in advance by the Recruitment team, will be ineligible for an agency fee.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analysing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

title: Test Lead - Finance, Risk, & Tax CONTRACTOR
description:
Technology Americas | Test Lead – Finance, Risk & Tax – CONTRACTOR | New York

About ING:

In the Americas, ING’s Wholesale Banking division offers a broad range of innovative financial products and services to domestic and international corporate and institutional clients.


When you come to work at ING, you’re joining a team where individuality isn’t just accepted, it’s encouraged. We’ve built a culture that’s fun, friendly and supportive – it’s the kind of place where you can be yourself and make the most of whatever you have to offer.

We give people the freedom to take risks, think differently, take ownership of their work, and make great things happen. We’re here to help you get ahead. And with our global network, there’s plenty of scope to take your career in new directions, perhaps even ones you’ve never considered. ING Americas follows a hybrid work model, allowing for in-office / work from home flexibility. Hybrid work arrangements vary based on business area.


Sound like the kind of place you’d feel at home? We’d love to hear from you.

About the position:

ING is seeking an experienced, hands-on Test Lead to establish and coordinate the testing approach for Finance, Risk and Tax reporting deliverables within a major local and global internal program. The consultant will lead test planning and execution across a broad portfolio of data and reporting capabilities supporting management, internal and regulatory reporting needs.

The scope of reporting requirements includes Shared National Credit (SNC) regulatory reporting; Risk management reporting, Tax Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet reporting; and Finance reporting solutions built on Power BI. The role will coordinate testing across source systems, data ingestion, data models, simplified views, consumer lenses, mappings, interfaces, and downstream reports.

This role will formalize a practical testing operating model for the workstream and provide day-to-day leadership for test preparation, execution, evidence, defect governance, reporting, and stakeholder coordination. The strongest candidate will combine regulatory-reporting and data-testing experience with the ability to create structure quickly, challenge incomplete requirements, reconcile outputs across complex data flows and drive defects to closure across local and globally distributed teams.

About the department:

ING Americas Technology supports local business delivery while operating within ING's global technology model. The Finance, Risk and Tax workstream brings together U.S. Finance, Risk, Tax, Data, Architecture, Engineering, Technology Risk, Testing and global delivery teams to define, source, map, test and deliver the data and reporting capabilities required for the future U.S. operating model.

The team coordinates U.S. reporting requirements and acceptance criteria with downstream reporting solutions such as Power BI. The Test Lead will work closely with business report owners, business analysts, data specialists, developers, platform teams and vendors to create a consistent, traceable and audit-ready approach across the workstream.

Responsibilities:

As a Test Lead, you will be responsible for:

  • Define and implement a risk-based, end-to-end testing strategy and operating model for Finance, Risk and Tax reporting deliverables.
  • Create and maintain the integrated test plan, scope, schedule, entry and exit criteria, roles and responsibilities, environments, data needs, dependencies, evidence standards and reporting cadence.
  • Coordinate system integration testing, data validation, end-to-end testing, user acceptance testing, regression testing, dry runs, and business sign-off activities across the workstream.
  • Translate business requirements, reporting rules, business requirement documents, source-to-target mappings and acceptance criteria into clear test scenarios, test cases, and expected results.
  • Validate data completeness, accuracy, lineage, transformation logic, aggregation, reconciliation and report presentation from systems of record through ingestion, FRIDA data models and views, consumer lenses and downstream reporting tools.
  • Lead testing for SNC regulatory reporting, including validation of critical data elements, product and data-pattern coverage, data mappings, report outputs and supporting evidence.
  • Lead testing for Risk management reports, including Local Sector RAS and Country Risk reporting, with validation of calculations, thresholds, filters, dimensions, aggregation levels, drill-down behavior and Power BI outputs against approved requirements and source data.
  • Lead testing for Tax Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet reporting, including validation of mapping rules, calculations, state or entity-level outputs, reconciliations and business acceptance.
  • Coordinate testing of Finance reports and semantic models, including product-by-product data coverage and reconciliation to agreed source and accounting information.
  • Establish test data requirements and coordinate the preparation, refresh, masking, access, and availability of representative data across test environments.
  • Ensure coverage of positive, negative, boundary, exception, historical, late-adjustment and data-quality scenarios, including missing, duplicate, inconsistent or rejected records.
  • Own defect governance, including defect logging, severity and priority alignment, triage, assignment, aging, retesting, closure, root-cause visibility and escalation of risks to delivery or regulatory readiness.
  • Maintain execution and defect records in Azure DevOps or approved workstream tooling, ensuring test cases, results, evidence, defects, requirements and approvals remain traceable.
  • Facilitate daily test coordination, defect triage and readiness reviews across business, data, engineering, reporting, vendor and global platform stakeholders.
  • Produce concise testing dashboards and governance updates that clearly distinguish planned, executed, passed, failed, blocked and deferred tests; open defects; decisions required; residual risks; and readiness for sign-off.
  • Confirm that non-functional and control requirements are tested where applicable, including access, security, auditability, retention, resilience, monitoring, data-download controls and operational support readiness.
  • Support production-readiness activities, including dress rehearsals, cutover validation, initial reporting cycles, aftercare, control evidence and handover to business and technology owners.
  • Coach analysts, developers and business testers on test-case quality, evidence expectations, defect documentation and consistent execution practices.

Qualifications and Competencies

  • 7+ years of software testing, data testing, quality assurance or test management experience, including delivery of complex technology, data or regulatory-change initiatives in a large, matrixed organization.
  • Demonstrated experience leading testing for Finance, Risk, Tax, regulatory reporting, management information or other data-intensive reporting capabilities within financial services.
  • Strong understanding of end-to-end data flows, including source systems, ETL or ingestion, data models, transformation rules, data warehouses or marts, semantic layers and downstream reporting tools.
  • Hands-on experience designing test strategies, integrated test plans, scenarios, test cases, expected results, execution controls, traceability matrices, defect processes and test completion reports.
  • Strong data-validation and reconciliation skills, with the ability to compare source data, transformed datasets, calculations and report outputs and identify where discrepancies originate.
  • Experience testing data mappings, interfaces, batch files, APIs, business rules, calculations, aggregations, filters, thresholds, hierarchies, and report visualizations.
  • Strong defect-management experience, including severity assessment, triage facilitation, root-cause coordination, retesting, closure evidence, and risk-based escalation.
  • Experience coordinating business users, subject-matter experts, developers, data engineers, architects, platform teams and third-party vendors through SIT, UAT and end-to-end testing.
  • Ability to create a workable testing structure where processes, ownership, requirements or environments are still developing, while maintaining delivery momentum and control discipline.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain data and testing issues to non-technical stakeholders and summarize readiness, defects and residual risks for senior stakeholders.
  • Strong documentation discipline and the ability to maintain clear, traceable, review-ready and audit-ready testing records and evidence.
  • Comfort operating in a regulated financial-services environment and handling sensitive financial, risk, tax and customer data.
  • Working knowledge of Agile and traditional delivery methods and test-management tools such as Azure DevOps Test Plans/Boards, Jira, ALM, qTest or comparable platforms.
  • Working knowledge of SQL or equivalent data-query techniques for validating datasets, transformations, and reconciliations.
  • Preferred:
  • Experience testing U.S. regulatory reports, particularly Shared National Credit (SNC), regulatory finance or risk reporting.
  • Experience with FRIDA or comparable enterprise Finance and Risk data platforms, including data models, simplified views, consumer lenses and controlled data consumption.
  • Experience with Power BI or comparable business-intelligence platforms.
  • Understanding Finance and accounting data, including inventory, general ledger, Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet, product, counterparty and reference data.
  • Understanding credit-risk and management-information concepts such as exposure, risk-weighted assets, risk appetite thresholds, country risk, sector risk and credit-quality measures.
  • Experience validating critical data elements, source-to-target mappings, data lineage, data quality controls and reconciliations across multiple upstream systems and product types.
  • Experience planning or executing parallel runs, dry runs, regulatory submission rehearsals, reporting-cycle validation or production aftercare.
  • Experience with test automation or repeatable data-comparison approaches using SQL, Python, Power Query, Excel or comparable tools.
  • Familiarity with technology risk and control requirements for access, auditability, evidence retention, data downloads, security, resilience and operational readiness.
  • Relevant testing certifications such as ISTQB, Certified Software Test Professional, Agile testing certification or equivalent practical experience.

Hourly Rate: $76-97

ING is a committed equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of diverse backgrounds and hire without regard to race, gender, religion, national origin, citizenship, disability, age, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by law. We celebrate these differences and rely upon your unique perspective to innovate and seize new opportunities. Come as you are.

ING Bank does not have a commercial banking license in the U.S. and therefore not permitted to conduct a commercial banking business in the U.S. Through its wholly owned subsidiary ING Financial Services LLC, and its affiliates, it offers a full array of wholesale products such as commercial lending and a full range of FM products and services.

title: Technical Sales Engineer
description:
Gendon Polymer Services Inc.

As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway—you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. We’re committed to making a positive impact on the world, providing you with diverse learning and working opportunities, and fostering a culture where everyone’s empowered to be their best.

The Field Engineer serves as the technical interface between the company and its customers, providing expertise in polymer materials, plastics processing, and application development. This role supports customers in resolving technical challenges, optimizing manufacturing processes, evaluating new material technologies, and ensuring successful implementation of the company's products in the field. Field Engineer works closely with customers, engineering, operations, sales, and quality teams to deliver practical solutions and drive customer success.

Marmon Aerospace & Defense Group delivers high‑performance wire, cable, and connectivity solutions engineered for the demanding needs of aerospace, defense, space, and advanced industrial applications.

Gendon Polymer Services is a specialty compounder based in Bolton, Ontario, Canada. Gendon, a Berkshire Hathaway company, is prime developer of custom compounds for a wide range of applications from wire and cable to building and construction, as well as highly engineered technical compounds for injection molding applications.

Benefits

We offer a competitive and well-rounded benefits package, including:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Vacation, Personal Time Off and paid holidays

  • Short-term and long-term disability (STD/LTD) coverage

  • Life insurance

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

  • Tuition reimbursement

  • Employee discounts

  • Salary Range: $139,000.00 - $173,500.00 CAD
    (Depends on industry specific and overall years of experience)

Key Responsibilities in the Role:

  • Develop a strong understanding of polymer and plastic materials, including material selection, formulation, processing, and end-use performance.
  • Provide technical support to customers by troubleshooting processing, manufacturing, and product performance issues related to polymer compounds and cable materials.
  • Collaborate with customers to identify root causes of material and processing challenges and implement effective corrective actions.
  • Support qualification and commercialization of new materials through plant trials, process optimization, small-scale wire extrusion trials, and performance evaluations.
  • Assist customers with extrusion, compounding, and cable manufacturing processes to improve productivity, quality, and product consistency.
  • Evaluate field performance data and customer feedback to drive continuous improvement and new product development initiatives.
  • Work closely with engineering, operations, sales, and quality teams to ensure successful implementation of new technologies and products.
  • Conduct on-site customer visits, technical presentations, and training sessions related to material performance, processing, and application development.
  • Provide recommendations on material selection, processing conditions, and product design based on application requirements and industry standards.
  • Prepare technical reports documenting trial results, troubleshooting activities, customer interactions, and recommendations.

Key Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Materials Science, Polymer Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Plastics Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience requried
  • Strong understanding of polymer science, plastics engineering, and material characterization.
  • Knowledge of polymer processing technologies including extrusion, compounding, and wire & cable manufacturing.
  • Experience troubleshooting manufacturing and product performance issues.
  • Ability to analyze technical data and identify root causes of material and process-related problems.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to customers and cross-functional teams.
  • Familiarity with fluoropolymers, HFFR compounds, polyolefins, engineering thermoplastics, and thermoset materials is preferred.
  • Understanding of wire and cable industry standards and applications is an asset.
  • Ability and willingness to travel 50% of the time throughout North America, including the United States, Canada, and Mexico, to support customer visits, technical troubleshooting, product trials, and business development activities.

Following receipt of a conditional offer of employment, candidates will be required to complete additional job-related screening processes as permitted or required by applicable law.

title: Electronics Soldering Technician II
description:
WORK LOCATION: Huntsville, AL

FLSA STATUS: Non-Exempt

SALARY RANGE: The anticipated salary range for this role is $23.00 to $31.00 per hour. This range reflects a good faith estimate based on the targeted level for the role and typical compensation benchmarks across U.S. locations. Actual compensation may vary depending on the selected candidate’s qualifications, experience, geographical location, and internal alignment.

SUMMARY

The Electronics Technician is an integral part of our production team. Under moderate supervision, the Electronics Technician builds assemblies within established timeframes and to document specification, ensuring that all work and components meet rigorous quality standards. The Electronics Technician displays keen attention to detail and supports others in the shop and throughout the company, both technically and as teammates. The electronic technician verifies that products meets all functional requirements, and completes required configuration and calibration activities.

RESPONSIBILITIES

The following job functions are a basic requirement but are not limited to and may be assigned other duties.

  • Manufactures and assembles cables and wire harnesses, by soldering wires into connectors (cup soldering) and crimping various terminals to populate into housings
  • Tests and performs functional checks on completed assemblies
  • Fills out travelers and documents components’ progress through the shop and handles Lot/Serial tracking for product traceability
  • Regularly uses production tools and equipment including soldering irons, wire cutters, stripper/crimpers, Windows-based PCs, etc.
  • Performs in-process configuration, calibration, and verification on equipment
  • Performs functional and mechanical check outs as required
  • Supports improvement of Test equipment and procedures
  • Communicates effectively with management and teammates to discuss challenges and support problem resolution
  • Assumes all other responsibilities as assigned

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • High School Diploma/GED
  • 1+ years of experience soldering and/or hand crimping
  • Experience in a production setting

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with cup soldering and JST/Molex crimping
  • IPC 620 certification or similar
  • Familiarity with electronics
  • Familiar with AS9100 standards
  • Familiarity using a microscope

REDWIRE DEFENSE TECH BENEFITS

  • Matching 401(k)
  • Paid PTO
  • Paid holidays
  • Medical, vision, and dental insurance
  • Group Short-Term & Long-Term Disability
  • HSA and FSA Options
  • Critical Care Plan
  • Accident Care Plan
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan

CLEARANCE REQUIREMENTS

This position may require access to information that is subject to compliance with the International Traffic Arms Regulations (“ITAR”) and/or the Export Administration Regulations (“EAR”). To comply with the requirements of the ITAR and/or the EAR, applicants will be asked to provide specific documentation to verify a US person’s status under the ITAR and the EAR.

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The work environment may involve a standard office setting while also incorporating elements of a production area. Employees will use standard office equipment, including computers, and must demonstrate stamina to sit or stand while maintaining attention to detail despite potential interruptions. The role may require occasional activities such as walking, climbing, stooping, crouching, and bending. Vision is necessary for reading printed materials and a computer screen, while hearing and speech are essential for effective communication both in person and over the telephone. Additionally, the position may necessitate travel by air or automobile. Employees may be required to use personal protective equipment, including safety glasses, safety shoes, and shop coats, to ensure safety in the production environment. Employees may be able to lift up to 30 pounds as needed.

REDWIRE DEFENSE TECH IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information. Redwire Defense Tech is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. To request reasonable accommodation, contact Human Resources. Continued employment remains on an “At-Will” basis.

title: Refrigeration 313A Journeyman
description:
BUILD YOUR CAREER AT BLACK & MCDONALD

Black & McDonald is an integrated, multi‑trade service provider that safely delivers high quality construction, facilities management, and technical solutions. We are a family-owned and family-run company that employs thousands of highly skilled and talented professionals across North America. With over 100 years of diverse market experience, we are a forward‑thinking organization with a strong track record of delivering operational excellence and customer-focused solutions that stand the test of time.

ABOUT THIS CAREER OPPORTUNITY

Black & McDonald’s Southwest Ontario team is growing! If you are an independent, enthusiastic, and driven professional searching for an opportunity to build a solid foundation for your career, this position is for you. The Refrigeration Journeyman position is located in Hamilton or London, Ontario, and requires travel throughout Southwest Ontario.

The Refrigeration Journeyman is primarily responsible for the operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, and installation of industrial and recreational refrigeration systems. This role supports a wide range of customers including arenas, recreation facilities, industrial plants, cold storage facilities, food processing operations, and process cooling applications. The successful candidate will possess strong technical expertise, excellent customer service skills, and a commitment to safety and operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform preventive maintenance, inspections, troubleshooting, and repairs on industrial and recreational refrigeration systems.
  • Service and maintain ammonia, CO₂, glycol, and synthetic refrigerant-based systems, including compressors, condensers, evaporators, pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, and associated equipment.
  • Diagnose and repair refrigeration control systems, electrical components, sensors, valves, and safety devices.
  • Perform refrigerant leak detection, recovery, charging, and evacuation in accordance with regulatory and environmental requirements.
  • Support the operation and maintenance of arena refrigeration systems, ice-making equipment, and related mechanical systems.
  • Inspect refrigeration equipment and identify deficiencies, recommending corrective actions to improve system reliability, efficiency, and performance.
  • Read and interpret mechanical, electrical, P&ID, control schematics, and manufacturer specifications.
  • Update and maintain service records, inspection reports, drawings, O&M manuals, and other documentation related to refrigeration systems.
  • Install, retrofit, and commission refrigeration equipment and system components as determined by the Manager.
  • Recommend materials, parts, and equipment required to support maintenance and service activities.
  • Respond to emergency service calls and participate in on-call rotations as required.
  • Complete preventive and demand maintenance tasks and accurately document work performed through electronic work order systems.
  • Work directly with customers to ensure complete satisfaction and provide technical recommendations where appropriate.
  • Work in compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act, applicable regulations, and Black & McDonald safety policies, including proper use of personal protective equipment and reporting of hazards or unsafe conditions.

COMPETENCY REQUIREMENTS

  • Communicates Effectively
  • Continuous Learning
  • Customer Focus
  • Problem Solving and Innovation
  • Teamwork and Collaboration

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS

  • Skilled Trades Ontario Certificate of Qualification for Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Systems Mechanic (313A).
  • Completion of a recognized Refrigeration and Air Conditioning program.
  • Valid G1/G2 Gas Technician License considered an asset.
  • Refrigeration Operator Certification considered an asset.

WORK EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

  • Minimum 3-5 years of experience servicing industrial and/or recreational refrigeration systems.
  • Strong knowledge of ammonia, CO₂, and conventional refrigeration systems.
  • Experience working in arenas, ice rinks, food processing facilities, cold storage facilities, or industrial process cooling environments is preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and control-related issues associated with refrigeration equipment.
  • Experience commissioning, servicing, and maintaining compressors, evaporators, condensers, pumps, and associated refrigeration components.
  • Familiarity with PLC-based controls, Building Automation Systems (BAS), and refrigeration monitoring systems is considered an asset.
  • Strong understanding of refrigeration system operating principles, safety requirements, and preventive maintenance practices.

SKILLS, ABILITIES, AND OTHER REQUIREMENTS

  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with the ability to diagnose complex refrigeration system issues.
  • Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, P&IDs, and technical manuals.
  • Excellent customer service and communication skills with a commitment to exceeding customer expectations.
  • A team player committed to working in a safety-focused, quality-driven environment.
  • Comply with all company policies, procedures, and safety standards.
  • Physically capable of lifting up to 30 kg and performing tasks involving bending, climbing, kneeling, and working in confined spaces.
  • Comfortable working from ladders, lifts, scaffolding, and elevated work platforms.
  • Proficient with:
    • Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook)
    • CMMS and mobile work order platforms (DSI experience considered an asset)
  • Willing and able to travel throughout Southwest Ontario and participate in an on-call rotation.
  • Valid Ontario Class G Driver's License with a satisfactory driving record.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain required security clearances, including Vulnerable Sector Screening where required by customer sites.

The expected salary range for this role is determined in accordance with the union collective agreement.

title: HR Operations Senior Analyst
description:
The HR Operations Senior Analyst supports new and existing Workday HCM system functionality and HR operational process design and administration. This role is a lead in the implementation, testing, and support of Workday and other HR systems, and is accountable for data management, case resolution, process documentation, operational administration, and supporting all aspects of functional reporting from all HR systems. Working within the HR Operations team, the Senior Analyst plays a hands-on role in carrying out HR programs and procedures across the colleague's lifecycle. The Senior Analyst is expected to execute all HR Operations processes — owning processes end-to-end, understanding how those processes interconnect with broader HR and firm operations, and maintaining up-to-date process documentation. This individual serves as a senior resource and escalation point within the team, a go-to subject matter expert for complex processes, and a driver of continuous improvement, governance, and knowledge management across HR Operations.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Serves as a Workday HCM subject matter expert for the HR Operations scope catalog and processes, maintaining a thorough understanding of relevant business processes, system configurations, and downstream impacts across HR and the broader firm ecosystem.

  • Administers and maintains Workday Time Tracking and Absence Management modules, including time entry templates, time calculation tags, time off plans, accrual plans, leave of absence types, eligibility rules, and period schedules; partners with Payroll to ensure accurate downstream processing and resolves time entry and absence calculation issues in a timely manner.

  • Conducts and leads regular Workday data audits for transactions entered via Employee Self Service, Manager Self Service and by Local HR to maintain overall data integrity, identifying and resolving inconsistencies in accordance with firm procedures.

  • Owns end-to-end internal compliance audit program participation for assigned areas including I-9 document retention, background check verification, Workday data accuracy audits, and case management quality reviews; drives resolution, tracks findings, and escalates systemic risk to HR Operations leadership.

  • Prepares and inputs people and job data in Workday for employee lifecycle events including new hire, job change, termination, personal data changes, compensation adjustments, position updates, and other required data transactions.

  • Reviews and verifies source data to confirm accuracy and completeness prior to entry; follows up with appropriate parties to resolve discrepancies or missing information.

  • Owns assigned HR processes end-to-end, including maintaining accurate and current process documentation, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and Quick Reference Guides (QRGs)/job aids, Knowledge Bank and templates to support consistency and knowledge continuity across the team; trains team members on process updates and serves as subject matter expert for HR Operations knowledge management.

  • Manages and resolves Workday Help cases as a Level 5 escalated responder and senior escalation resource within the HR Operations team; owns SLA compliance for assigned cases per SOP-2.1.1; guides junior team members on case documentation standards, priority classification, and escalation judgment; conducts periodic case queue quality audits and contributes to case management performance metrics; triages, tracks, and closes tickets within established service level expectations.

  • Serves as a primary technical resource for complex Workday transactions including rescinds, retroactive corrections, duplicate worker resolution, and multi-system corrections; leads downstream impact assessment and coordinates cross-functional alignment (Payroll, Benefits, IAM, Local HR) before executing correction actions; obtains required dual-approval per established protocols.

  • Supports oversight of the People Operations downstream notification process for in-scope transactions; participates in UAT for notification enhancements; serves as a reviewer for daily exception reports and escalations; supports the Partner/IP manual notification process as needed.

  • Manages contingent worker lifecycle transactions in Workday including hire, extension, termination, and data corrections as a senior resource; ensures all CWR notifications and downstream alerts are transmitted per established protocols.

  • Serves as a senior resource for Partner Relations data transactions in Workday including lawyer information updates, admissions tracking, jurisdictions, and bar membership updates.

  • Runs, formats, and distributes Workday reports to key stakeholders on a scheduled and ad hoc basis; leads HR Operations performance reporting and contributes to the development of the HR Operations KPI and scorecard framework; proactively identifies process improvement opportunities and proposes automation or standardization solutions.

  • Inputs and maintains documents in electronic personnel files via OnBase, ensuring proper organization and retrieval standards are followed.

  • Supports Workday system testing, updates, and enhancements, serving as a senior owner and knowledgeable participant in testing and process validation efforts.

  • Assists with HR department projects and initiatives as needed.

  • Performs other related duties as required and assigned

Education and/or Experience:

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree

  • Strong data entry skills, both alpha and numeric

  • High level of attention to detail — must demonstrate use of process and resource materials with keen eye and passion for defect-free process and data accuracy

  • Working knowledge of Workday, Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint

  • Creation, adherence, and continuous improvement of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Quick Reference Guides (QRGs)/job aids, and process flow documentation

  • Strong service delivery mentality with demonstrated experience working with sensitive HR data and case management platforms

  • Demonstrated experience leading or peer-reviewing Workday data processes and SLA-driven case management queues; ability to guide others on documentation standards, priority classification, and escalation judgment

  • Ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the firm, tailoring communication styles to leadership preferences

  • Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with peers, stakeholders, and project team members

  • Curious, self-starter who can navigate complex processes and bring a continuous improvement mindset to processing protocols

  • A minimum of 2 years of experience administering HR systems and data processes

Preferred:

  • Prior HR experience

  • Prior experience with cloud-based Human Resources Information Systems, preferably Workday HCM

  • Experience with HR reporting tools, data quality analysis, and contribution to continuous improvement or automation initiatives

  • Experience with knowledge management, training delivery, or SOP/QRG governance

  • Hands-on Workday administration, with a strong emphasis on Time Tracking and Absence Management modules

Other Skills and Abilities:

The following will also be required of the successful candidate:

  • Strong organizational skills

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

  • Able to work harmoniously and effectively with others

  • No supervisory responsibility

  • Works under supervision

  • Requisite legal education

  • Strong analytical skills to support on legal matters

  • Experience delivering quality work whilst managing competing deadlines

  • Good communication skills

White & Case is an elite global law firm serving leading companies, financial institutions and governments worldwide. Our long history as an international firm means we are perfectly placed to help our clients resolve their most complex legal challenges wherever they may be.

With lawyers operating from more than 40 locations, working in virtually every country of the world, we have invested heavily in building a high-quality full-service practice competing at the top of the market. We are distinguished by our on-the-ground presence in the world’s key financial markets and our strengths in handling complex cross-border work. It’s not just about our global network of offices; it’s the global interconnectedness of the Firm that our people, and our clients, value most. We work well together across geographic and practice boundaries. It’s one of the reasons we attract and retain cross-border work. And why we attract a diverse group of people.

Position Summary

We are seeking a motivated trainee to join our Corporate team for a paid, full-time internship from September 2027 to January 2028. The role is intended for law graduates enrolled in the Master’s Degree for Access to the Legal Profession (Máster Universitario de Acceso a la Abogacía).

The trainee will work closely with partners, associates and other members of the Corporate team, supporting a broad range of domestic and cross-border corporate and commercial matters, including mergers and acquisitions, private equity transactions, corporate reorganizations and general corporate advisory work.

From day one, you’ll be immersed in our high-profile work with the client exposure that will shape your capabilities for years to come. On a daily basis, you’ll tackle global issues and build your experience across established and fast-growth markets, where the rules are still being decided

Qualifications

We are looking to recruit an outstanding trainee with a proactive approach and a genuine interest in gaining hands-on experience from day one. The successful candidate will be eager to work on sophisticated, high-value cross-border corporate transactions in an international environment.

Candidates should hold a Law degree, demonstrate a solid academic background and be fluent in English, with the ability to work in English on a daily basis. They should show initiative, enthusiasm, a positive and collaborative attitude and the ability to work effectively as part of small, high-performing teams.

At White & Case, we value individuality, intellectual curiosity and the energy candidates bring to challenging work. The trainee will have the opportunity to contribute to complex and cutting-edge matters while developing practical legal skills alongside our partners, senior associates and the wider Corporate team.

Location and Reporting

This role is based in Madrid and reports to the partners of the Corporate – M&A practice. We don´t offer a rotation program across practice areas, so it is important that you have a genuine interest in Corporate - M&A.

How to Apply

You must apply online and upload your CV and academic records. Your academic records must state your overall grade average. Optional to attach a cover letter to the application.

Applications without academic records or without overall grade average will be automatically rejected.

A selected group of candidates will be invited by the Madrid Recruitment Team to sit a technical test session at the White & Case offices in late October 2026.

Successful candidates will be invited to attend a round of in-person interviews at our offices with our partners, senior associates and HR team.

Equal Opportunities

White & Case is committed to creating a fair workplace. It is our Firm’s policy to recruit, employ, train, compensate, and promote without regard to race, religion, creed, national origin, age, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, military or veteran status, disability, genetic information, or any other category protected by applicable law.

If you require assistance and/or adjustment to participate in our application and/or interview process, please email us. We will be happy to work with you.

The Firm may modify and amend any job description at any time in its sole discretion. Nothing herein creates a contract of employment or otherwise modifies the at-will nature of employment.

The above is only a general description of the essential duties associated with this position and does not represent an exhaustive or comprehensive list of all duties.

Note to Recruitment Agencies

Our internal Recruitment team manages all aspects of lateral hiring. All agencies must have signed terms of business—specific to the relevant office—before submitting any candidates. CVs or applications sent directly to White & Case partners or employees will also not be considered formal introductions. If you have questions, please contact the relevant Recruitment team. title: Data Scientist
description:

DNV has high ambitions for improving business processes and services by using AI. DNV is now establishing an AI team in Pune to strengthen DNV’s ability to meet ambitious business goals.
You will be part of a leading AI competency and development team located at the two locations Pune and Oslo (DNV headquarters). The AI team focuses on use of AI and machine learning to improve DNV’s maritime global work processes. We create AI systems that enable and support digitalization of DNV’s global production processes and systems as well as creation of new digital services. The AI team consists of experienced data scientists and software developers. You will collaborate in teams with different functional competencies and domain experts. Our deliveries have a global impact through our multi-national organization, and through cooperation with large companies.

Daily tasks / duties:
You will solve real-world business cases and be a key contributor to programming and releasing AI and Machine Learning solutions. You will engage in all project phases, from dialogue with stakeholders to understand the problem to be solved, through data analysis, planning technical architecture and team collaboration on experimenting, programming and releasing solutions through our DevOps cycles to production. You are also expected to actively explore new opportunities for applied AI, to stay up-to-dated with main trends in the AI industry, and to identify how AI may create new business opportunities for DNV.

  • Flexible work arrangements for better work-life balance
  • Generous Paid Leaves (Annual, Sick, Compassionate, Local Public, Marriage, Maternity, Paternity, Medical leave)
  • Medical benefits ( Insurance and Annual Health Check-up)
  • Pension and Insurance Policies (Group Term Life Insurance, Group Personal Accident Insurance, Travel Insurance)
  • Training and Development Assistance (Training Sponsorship, On-The-Job Training, Training Programme)
  • Additional Benefits (Long Service Awards, Mobile Phone Reimbursement)
  • Company bonus/Profit share.
  • You will be part of a strong, international data science team continuously delivering value-adding AI solutions that are integrated into business applications and work processes.
  • You will collaborate with experienced data scientist experts across the two locations Pune and Oslo
  • You will collaborate in cross-functional teams with skilled developers, data engineers and domain experts
  • You enjoy teamwork and you take a holistic view of projects and tasks.
  • You are self-driven and take ownership of the solutions success and value-creation You enjoy seeing your real-world AI solutions come to life, being integrated into tools applications and work processes.
*Benefits may vary based on position, tenure/contract/grade level*
DNV is an Equal Opportunity Employer and gives consideration for employment to qualified applicants without regard to gender, religion, race, national or ethnic origin, cultural background, social group, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, age or political opinion. Diversity is fundamental to our culture and we invite you to be part of this diversity.

Required position qualifications

  • 5-10 years of Machine Learning and AI programming experience
  • You hold a master’s degree or higher in data science, computer science, statistics or another related scientific field
  • You have experience and knowledge with practical AI development and deployment
  • You are an expert in Python development and Machine Learning techniques
  • You have working knowledge of git and docker
  • You have familiarity with DevOps concepts and processes
  • You have good verbal and written communication skills in English

Good-to-have position qualifications

  • Experience and knowledge with practical AI development for integration in business applications
  • Knowledge of Deep Learning and transformer architectures are desirable
  • Experience with systematic evaluation and testing of AI solutions

About you:

  • You are eager to learn about and share knowledge about new technologies and trends
  • You enjoy working in cross-functional teams
  • You are result-oriented and like to solve problems
  • You are curious and eager to understand customers’ needs
Security and compliance with statutory requirements in the countries in which we operate is essential for DNV. Background checks will be conducted on all final candidates as part of the offer process, in accordance with applicable country-specific laws and practices.

title: Education Coordinator
description:
TITLE: Education Coordinator
TEAM/PROGRAMME: Education/GPE GEA LOCATION: Bor- Jonglei State
GRADE: 3 CONTRACT LENGTH: 3 years

CHILD SAFEGUARDING:

Level 3: the post holder will have contact with children and/or young people either frequently (e.g. once a week or more) or intensively (e.g. four days in one month or more or overnight) because they work country programs; or are visiting country programs; or because they are responsible for implementing the police checking/vetting process staff.

ROLE PURPOSE:
The Education Coordinator will assist Programme Manager in ensuring the effective implementation, coordination, supervision and representation of programme activities as required and/or designated by the Programme Manager. Under the supervision and technical support of the Programme Manager, the Education Coordinator will work as part of SCI Education team to provide technical support and guidance to partners guidance to SCI project staff and supervise the overall implementation of the project.

In the absence of the Programme Manager the post holder will manage the programme team and assume all other technical programme activities as they relate to the project. He/she will support the Programme Manager in day to day program management.

In the event of a major humanitarian emergency, the role holder will be expected to work outside the normal role profile and be able to vary working hours accordingly.

SCOPE OF ROLE:

Reports to: Project Manager (technically) and Field Manager (administratively)

Staff reporting to this post: 1 Education Officer.
Direct: 1
Indirect : 1
Budget Responsibilities: None
Role Dimensions: The Education Coordinator will work closely with State Ministry of Education, respective targeted schools and implementing partners to strengthen and build their capacity to deliver, manage and coordinate the program. He/ she will ensure that all girls and boys learn and are safe in a quality learning environment. By improving school access and retention for girls and boys, out-of-school children and children with disabilities. The Coordinator will nurture and maintain relationships with stakeholders inclusive of the Education Cluster as the State Cluster Co-Lead, County Education Departments (CEDs) officials, State Ministry of Education, Schools Teachers, School management Committees and PTAs in learning centres, to ensure timely, to budget and quality programme delivery. The Education Coordinator will collaborate and liaise with colleagues from CP and MHPSS and all other relevant structures within Save the Children to ensure efficiency in programme delivery and full integration.
KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY :

Programme Management
• Coordinate partnerships and take lead in ensuring the implementation of SCI self implemented activities in the Education MYRP.
• Provide technical support and guidance to staff & partners to strengthen their planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting systems on all Education programme activities.
• Oversee and guide the implementation of project activities carried out by implementing partners.
• Monitor partner project progress by engaging in monitoring visits and producing signed off monthly/quarterly monitoring reports.
• Identify partner capacity needs and report to technical managers, MYRP_ECW-GPE PM & Field Manager for support.
• Support programme management through consulting with implementing partners and staff on annual plans & budgets, generating program DIPs, Procurement Plans, budget phasing, monthly forecasts.
• Facilitate joint planning meetings & visits with CP & CRG Coordinator & MEAL team to ensure integration of program activities and efforts.
• Support monthly updating of the IPTT and Output tracker by MEAL team through liaising with partners and officers for information.
• Ensure financial compliance of activities in Education with approval of the respective line managers.
• Participate in budget monitoring by reviewing monthly BVAs and providing feedback for reclassifications, recoding and or other amendments.
• Support partners in producing quality monthly narrative reports and provide MYRP_ECW-GPE PM with information for the compilation of biannual and annual Education program reports to Member and/or Donor.
• Participate in the development of proposals in the department as and when necessary
• Liaise with other Coordinators and Project Officers from other sectors in the field to achieve maximum integration of projects and to further the aims of child rights programming and securing quality and safe learning environments.
• Lead in submitting timely program supplies requests for procurement to be initiated and supplies are delivered on time.
• Ensure Education staff have required capacity and support them through coaching and mentoring in building their capacity.
• Ensuring compliance with donor requirements as well as Save the Children HR, Finance and Procurement procedures and other SCI country policies.
• Ensure that staff and partners provide programme beneficiaries with ongoing, age-appropriate verbal or written information in relevant languages about the behaviour they can expect of staff and representatives, in line with the Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct; and how to raise concerns

Coordination, Representation and Advocacy Support
• Establish, nurture and maintain strong and positive relationships with the State Ministry of General Education and Instruction (MoGEI), relevant Departments, implementing partners and Education Cluster stakeholders within the State for information sharing, exchange of knowledge and coordination of Education programming in the State.
• SCI representation and participation in the State Education cluster meetings and other related Interagency education coordination forums.
• Participate in Interagency multi sectoral needs assessments in the State in response to humanitarian/ emergency situations and other programming related assessments.
• Facilitate advocacy processes on Education related issues within the State inclusive of Safe Back to School Campaigns, Teacher Professional Development advocacy needs and others emanating from the programme.
• Identifying opportunities for cooperation with Government departments and other development agencies in the State and participating in State network engagements related to programme activities
• To attend, participate and contribute in relevant national, regional and international forums as assigned by the line manager.

Renk County Education Cluster Co-Lead
• Co-chair regular and inclusive Education Cluster meetings in the county.

Creativity:

Integrity:

QUALIFICATIONS

title: Scientist, Medicinal Chemistry
description:
Life at BMS

At RayzeBio, every day is an opportunity to ignite meaningful change. As a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bristol Myers Squibb, RayzeBio blends the nimble, pioneering spirit of an emergent biotech with the global expertise and resources of a leading innovator in oncology. Our mission is to develop transformative radiopharmaceutical therapies that offer new hope for patients living with cancer. Here, you’ll join a multidisciplinary team where your ideas are valued, your expertise is amplified, and collaboration is at the heart of everything we do. From day one, expect to make an immediate impact—on our science, on our teams, and most importantly, on patients. Learn more about RayzeBio:


RayzeBio, a Bristol Myers Squibb company, is a dynamic biotechnology company headquartered in San Diego, CA. The company is focused on improving survival of people with cancer by harnessing the power of targeted radioisotopes. RayzeBio is developing innovative drugs against targets of solid tumors. Led by a successful and experienced entrepreneurial team, RayzeBio aims to be the global leader in radiopharmaceuticals

Scientist, Chemistry

Job Description

The Scientist will design and synthesize novel chemical constructs as potential new RPT therapies for cancer treatments. The Scientist I/II will be a highly motivated and technically skilled synthetic organic, peptide or medicinal chemist with excellent interpersonal and communication skills. Candidates will work as part of a team of scientists to synthesize and design both small molecules and peptide analogs to optimize potency, pharmacokinetics, and in vivo efficacy of potential drug candidates. The role is highly technical and will need a person who enjoys working at the bench with high productivity and data analysis skills and a comfort level in working under tight timelines.

Job Responsibilities

Essential duties and responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

  • Design and synthesize small molecule/novel peptide compounds in support of SAR campaigns for pipeline projects.
  • Contribute towards developing SAR on assigned projects, design and synthesize key target molecules to assess chemical/biological hypothesis.
  • Independently plan and execute organic synthesis routes for complex molecules. Utilize modern purification and analytical tools to support synthesis and characterization of target compounds.
  • Work in close collaboration with interdisciplinary team members to provide needed chemistry support to guide programs through lead identification/optimization phases.
  • Work closely with chemists, DMPK, imaging and in vitro/vivo teams to ensure that target compounds are generated in a timely manner to support the screening funnel.
  • Contribute experimental efforts in support of target selection and initiation of new RPT projects.
  • Keep abreast of the literature in the field of RPTs, identify novel concepts and ideas to help advance the state of art in RPT field.
  • Contribute towards IP filings and drafting of publications, presentations.
  • Routinely present research findings, project updates in interdisciplinary team settings.
  • Adhere rigorously to safety guidelines, regulatory standards and company policies and ensure a safe working environment.
  • Uses AI tools to enhance individual productivity and quality of work

Education and Experience

  • BS 5+ years

  • or MS 3+ years

  • or PhD 0 years

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD in synthetic organic, medicinal, or peptide chemistry with 0-4+ years of post-PhD/postdoc experience in Pharmaceutical/Biotech R&D environments demonstrating successful accomplishments and productivity.
  • Experience in working on targeted cancer therapy modalities such as RPTs, ADCs, PDCs is highly desirable.

Skills and Qualifications

  • Well versed in modern synthetic organic/peptide/med chem principles and demonstrated track record of high productivity and achievements in the lab.
  • Multi-step organic synthesis, structure-based drug design, and operation of analytical tools like NMR and HPLC/LC-MS.
  • High scientific curiosity and a learning mindset coupled with strong technical problem-solving skills and strong understanding of the concepts of drug design, SAR analysis, ADME/PK is important.
  • The ability to share data and collaborate with cross functional team members is critical as is the ability to effectively interpret data and plan experiments without supervision.
  • Excellent written and oral communication and presentation skills and ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic, and collaborative environment.

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, reach with hands and arms, and talk or hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and distance vision.

This is a position that requires working in a laboratory environment, protective clothing, gloves, and safety glasses are required while working in a laboratory environment.

title: Simulation Center Educator
description:

The Simulation Educator will collaborate with CHS faculty, healthcare partners, and simulation personnel to develop and deliver high-quality simulation education aligned with curricula, professional competencies, accreditation expectations, and standards of best practice. Faulkner University is a Christian university affiliated with the churches of Christ.

Summary of Duties:

title: Anesthesia Technician
description:
To provide support to the work done the the professional Anesthesia personnel through equipment, supply, operations, maintenance and support.

Direct Patient Care Duties

Anesthetic gas machine set up: 6-8W,3 OB, 2 Endoscopy, 1 EP lab, 28 B-level, 12 JSC that are used by the anesthesia care team (ACT), which includes the daily system pre-check, calibration of Draeger anesthetic machine, assembly of the anesthesia circuit and mask and a complete circuit check. Ready for end use by ACT.

Nitric oxide delivery system: Assemble (special nitric oxide circuit delivery system) and assist with the usage as directed by the anesthesia care team (ACT).

3D echocardiography (TEE) machines. Assemble probe and dental guard. Power up machine and remote cables. Assist with usage as directed by the ACT. Assist anesthesiologist with line isolation issues that impair TEE imaging.

Airway management: Have equipment available daily for use on the anesthesia cart as indicated by the operating room (OR) schedule for the patients receiving anesthesia.

Cardiac rooms: Assemble and assist with the usage of triple channel pumps with designated infusions, cerebral oximetry, general blood administration set, fluid warmers, cables for pressure monitoring, additional drug administration supplies and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE).

Joint and Spine: Assemble total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) infusion pumps, provide additional pulse oximetry, assemble BIS monitors, and assemble line placement for arterial monitoring and assist ACT as directed.

Ultrasound equipment: Assemble probe cover, gel and printing capability for line placement. Assemble and assist with their usage as directed by the ACT.

Video laryngoscopy equipment. Assemble and assist with usage as directed by the ACT.

Fiber optic equipment. Assemble and assist with usage as directed by the ACT.

Difficult airway patients: Assemble and assist with equipment and supplies, including fiber optic, jet ventilation, video, specialty tubes, laser tubes, micro endotracheal tube ( ETT), endotracheal tube exchangers/intubating stylets and laryngeal mask airway (LMA’s) as directed by the anesthesia care team.

Malignant hyperthermia (MH): Equipment and carts are prepared and readily available with special anesthetic equipment assembled and supplied to the anesthesia machine for usage as directed by the ACT.

Massive transfusion: Assemble and assist with usage as directed by the anesthesia care team all equipment for massive transfusion. Includes assembly of the appropriate disposable cassette, filter system and proper infusion tubing for a rapid transfuser. Assemble general blood administration tubing.

Emergency situations arising in any location the OR or in the hospital at large (e.g. ER, patient rooms): All anesthesia technicians are BLS certified and are expected to assist with chest compressions if requested as well as assist with their other duties. Other duties include securing TEE capability, ultrasound, emergency line placement, emergency intubations and/or difficult airway, MH resuscitation, lab draws, blood administration and any other duties as directed by the ACT.

Computer system, network issues both with hard wire connections and cabling are first addressed by anesthesia technicians and then directed to clinical engineering.

Bedside assistance: Assist a member of the ACT in providing patient care. Anesthesia technicians may assist in the moving of a patient, including but not limited to the moving of the patient, IV and pressure lines, ventilation tubing, infusion pumps and oxygen circuits.

They may assist an ACT member by opening sterile supplies or trays.

Patient transport: Assist the ACT in transportation of patients, usually from a remote site, OB or 8W to an off site location that requires the transportation of emergency equipment or ongoing resuscitation. This is often an extension of care involving emergency situations. Assist with assembly of anesthesia equipment in the new location while the patient remains under anesthesia.

General duties that support the Anesthesia Care Team in providing direct patient care

All mechanical, pneumatic and electronic equipment used in the anesthesia department also undergoes general inspection, maintenance, operating, servicing, scheduled cleaning, assembling, calibrating, testing and trouble shooting in the event of performance issues. This includes (but is not limited to) the anesthesia gas machine, anesthesia cart, MH cart, fiber optic equipment, specialty anesthesia storage areas in OR’s A, B, 3 and 4, specialty cardiovascular line placement carts in OR’s A, B, 3 and 4, 3D echocardiography (TEE) machines, ultrasound machines, all infusion pumps (fluid, blood, or medication) that are maintained by the Anesthesia Department and video laryngoscopy equipment maintained by the Anesthesia Department.

Readily available to set-up anesthesia in a remote location( including but not limited to High dose radiation, CT, Cancer Center, Pain Practice Center and the Heart Station). Power down the equipment in the initial location, move and restore the system in the remote location. Includes relocation of anesthesia cart, supplies and additional monitoring as needed. Also includes computer system (Epic) network set-ups.

Prepare equipment and supplies used daily in the Anesthesia Department

Assist with cleaning and turning over the cardiac rooms.

Non patient care duties

Daily documentation of activities assigned.

Document and report any equipment maintenance or failure issues to the Head Anesthesia Technician and/or Clinical Engineering.

Adhere to principles and techniques of biohazards, infection control and standard precautions. This includes cleanliness, sanitation, high level disinfection and sterility measures of supplies and equipment as indicated.

Storage use and safe handling of bulk, cylinder and pipeline gases.

Adhere to the principles of fire, radiation and electrical safety.

Requisition supplies as indicated.

Continuing education on the care, maintenance and proper usage of equipment.

Organization of all materials and supplies used within the department.

Hospital wide sweeps, quarterly and as needed, for wayward anesthesia equipment.

Special projects as requested by Anesthesia Department director or a member of the ACT.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS:

Please describe any specialized knowledge or skills, which are REQUIRED to perform the position duties. Do not personalize the job description, credentials, or knowledge and skills based on the current associate. List any special education required for this position.

EDUCATION: Successful high school graduate or GED with related technical or vocational training preferred.

YEARS OF EXPERIENCE: Preferred 2 to 4 years hospital experience or healthcare facility related to Anesthesia Technician position. O.R. experience preferred.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of regulatory, legislative and Joint Commission standards related to Anesthesia, surgery, and infection control. Knowledge of care and maintenance of technical equipment. Excellent communication skills and organizational ability. Some mechanical ability preferred. BLS certification.

LICENSES & CERTIFICATIONS:

ASAII Certification recommended within 3 years of employment.

title: FPGA Firmware Design Engineer
description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

The Aerospace Corporation's Experiment Lab, xLab, develops prototypes, instruments, pathfinders, and demonstration systems to address our customers' hardest problems at the speed of need. We engage with our customers to conceptualize innovative solutions and deliver impactful products for ground and space and everything in between.

We are looking for an FPGA Firmware Design Engineer (Senior Member of Technical Staff - Embedded Software Engineering) with a passion for design, a commitment to teamwork and a desire to help xLab make a difference to today's challenges. As an FPGA Firmware Design Engineer, you will design cutting-edge firmware solutions that enable mission-critical systems for aerospace applications.

  • Support xLab's rapid prototyping initiatives by delivering high-quality digital hardware solutions for government and commercial aerospace customers

  • Collaborate with systems engineers, hardware engineers, and software developers to integrate FPGA designs into larger system architectures

  • Perform simulation, synthesis, timing analysis, and verification of FPGA designs to ensure functionality and performance requirements are met

This position is onsite in El Segundo, CA., requiring at least 4 days a week onsite.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government. U.S. citizenship is required

  • Proficiency with high-speed interfaces such as SpaceWire, PCIe, Ethernet, DDR memory controllers, or SerDes

title: Maintenance Automation Technician
description:
The Maintenance & Automation Technician is responsible for installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, repairing, and optimizing automated manufacturing equipment, production machinery, robotics, and control systems. This position ensures equipment operates safely, efficiently, and with minimal downtime through preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance practices. The technician supports automation initiatives, facility maintenance activities, equipment upgrades, and continuous improvement efforts to maximize operational performance and reliability.

· Install, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair automated production equipment, robotics, and manufacturing systems.

· Diagnose and repair electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and automation-related issues.

· Troubleshoot and support PLCs, HMIs, industrial networks, sensors, drives, servos, and control systems.

· Perform preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance activities according to established schedules.

· Respond to equipment breakdowns and production interruptions to minimize downtime and maintain productivity.

· Support robotic systems including programming modifications, troubleshooting, and maintenance activities.

· Collaborate with Production, Engineering, Quality, and Tooling teams to optimize manufacturing processes.

· Recommend and assist with the procurement of replacement components, equipment upgrades, and spare parts inventory management.

· Ensure compliance with OSHA regulations, company safety policies, quality requirements, and environmental standards.

· Utilize maintenance software, diagnostic tools, and technical resources to support maintenance activities.

· Safely operate hand tools, power tools, testing instruments, forklifts, lifts, and other maintenance-related equipment as authorized.

· Participate in training and cross-functional development activities to expand technical capabilities.

· Support Lean Manufacturing, Continuous Improvement, and Operational Excellence initiatives.

· Perform other duties as assigned.

· Knowledge of PLCs (Allen-Bradley, Automation Direct, or equivalent), HMIs, and industrial control systems.

· PLC troubleshooting and programming experience.

· Robotics troubleshooting, maintenance, and programming.

· Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, mechanical drawings, and technical manuals.

· Ability to troubleshoot electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, robotic, and automation systems.

· Knowledge of motors, servos, VFDs, sensors, conveyors, and machine vision systems.

· Understanding of industrial networking protocols including EtherNet/IP, Profinet, and Modbus.

· Familiarity with preventive and predictive maintenance techniques.

· Knowledge of Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and continuous improvement methodologies.

· Strong problem-solving, analytical, and organizational skills.

· Ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

· Strong verbal and written communication skills.

· Knowledge of OSHA regulations and industrial safety standards.

· Ability to work independently and within a team environment.
