title: Data Center & IT Asset Management Systems Engineer
description:
The Massachusetts Port Authority is Going Above and Beyond™ for your career. We are a dynamic organization that connects people and businesses to the global community by air, land, and sea. Our employees are essential in moving planes, cargo, and cruise ships safely, efficiently, and sustainably. We are an economic engine, managing real estate assets where people live, work, and play. Together, the properties we own and operate generate $20 billion for the region’s economy.

As the digital heartbeat of our organization, the Information Technology (IT) Department fuels the seamless operation of Massport. Driven by our commitment to excellence, we harness the power of technology to solve real-world challenges and enable the organization to achieve its business goals with exceptional efficiency. Our team embraces development and diversity, constantly seeking new opportunities for innovation and growth, to help shape the future of our agency and set new standards for excellence.

ABOUT YOU

As a Data Center & IT Asset Management Systems Engineer, you are a strategic and forward-thinking technology leader who thrives in complex, mission-critical environments and is passionate about building reliable, scalable, and well-governed technology ecosystems. You bring a strong engineering mindset, exceptional analytical skills, and a commitment to continuous improvement, leveraging data to drive informed decisions, reduce risk, and enhance operational performance. Comfortable balancing technical depth with enterprise-wide collaboration, you communicate effectively across all levels of the organization, influence stakeholders, and translate complex challenges into practical solutions. Success in this role requires intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, attention to detail, and a proactive approach to strengthening infrastructure resilience, data integrity, security, and long-term organizational effectiveness.

What you will do:

  • Leverage your expertise in data center infrastructure, enterprise asset management, and technology governance to deliver resilient, scalable, and well-integrated solutions that support critical business operations and long-term organizational objectives.
  • Drive continuous improvement by establishing technical standards, optimizing processes, implementing automation, and enhancing the accuracy, reliability, and effectiveness of infrastructure monitoring and asset management platforms.
  • Apply strong analytical, strategic, and problem-solving skills to evaluate complex technology challenges, identify opportunities for modernization, manage operational risk, and provide data-driven recommendations that support infrastructure planning and investment decisions.
  • Collaborate with technical and business stakeholders to strengthen cybersecurity, compliance, governance, and operational excellence while serving as a trusted advisor on enterprise technology initiatives, emerging solutions, and best practices.

What you offer:

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Electrical Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a related field required. Advanced degree preferred. Equivalent experience may be considered.
  • 7-10 years of engineering experience with enterprise infrastructure management systems, data center infrastructure management (DCIM) platforms, IT Asset Management (ITAM) solutions, and configuration management databases (CMDBs). Demonstrated experience leading technical programs, designing platform integrations, and exercising independent engineering judgment in complex enterprise environments is required. Prior experience in critical infrastructure, transportation, aviation, or government technology environments preferred.
  • Possess deep expertise in data center infrastructure, enterprise asset management, and CMDB governance, including power and cooling systems, UPS technologies, cloud and virtualization environments, and IT/OT asset lifecycle management.
  • Leverage strong technical, analytical, and communication skills to develop automated integrations, dashboards, and governance frameworks using technologies such as ServiceNow, Power BI, Python, PowerShell, JavaScript, REST APIs, and cybersecurity best practices.

*Click here for detailed job description

WHAT WE OFFER

Collaboration with colleagues at all levels of leadership from all different disciplines, from Aviation to Maritime and beyond. Every day is different at Massport and the breadth of our impact on the Massachusetts region through our facilities provides many opportunities for our employees to grow, learn, and explore the many areas of our business. Our business is all about connecting. We support and take pride in the employees that make those connections possible each and every day.

  • Work/life balance
  • A supportive and inclusive culture
  • Opportunities for growth
  • Providing safe, healthy, and secure work environment
  • Supporting the people and businesses of New England
  • Achieving results and having positive impact
  • Being good neighbors in the communities we serve
  • Protecting the environment

The salary range for this position is $107,000 to $122,000 annually and will be determined based on a variety of factors, including relevant experience, education, certifications, training, specialized skills, and overall qualifications.

title: PTA- Blanding
description:
Full-Time Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA)

Independence Rehab- Four Corners Regional

Blanding UT | Full-Time | Flexible Schedule | Therapist-Owned

Relocation assistance/Sign-On Bonus offered!

Helping People Stay Independent in the Later Chapters of Life

Independence Rehab is seeking a compassionate Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) who finds purpose in helping older adults regain mobility, confidence, and dignity.

You'll work with residents navigating recovery, chronic conditions, and life transitions - providing therapy that truly changes daily life!

Whether you're a new grad looking for mentorship or an experienced PTA wanting a sustainable caseload, Independence Rehab is where clinicians feel supported and patients feel the difference.


What a Day Looks Like

As a PTA in our geriatric clinics, your day is relationship-driven, collaborative, and clinically meaningful:

  • You'll treat a medically complex geriatric population in a setting where time, clinical reasoning, and compassion are valued. You will be challenged every day!
  • Guiding residents through mobility milestones - first steps, safe transfers, returning home
  • Leading gait, balance, strengthening, and functional training sessions
  • Helping reduce fall risk and build confidence with daily activities
  • Collaborating closely with your PT to adjust care plans
  • Working alongside nursing, OT, and speech to support whole-person recovery
  • Celebrating small wins that matter deeply to patients and families

Why Therapists Choose Independence Rehab

We're a small, therapist-owned company that runs therapy operations independently - meaning we advocate for clinicians and protect clinical judgment.

Our therapists often tell us the biggest difference is how supported they feel, personally and professionally. Some specifics that set Independence Rehab apart:

  • Highest average hourly pay in the area ($30-38/hour)
  • Realistic productivity expectations (85-90%)
  • Flexible work scheduling- we really do believe in a healthy work-life balance!
  • Strong corporate involvement but we don't micromanage
  • Stable leadership with low management turnover
  • Autonomy in clinical decision-making
  • Protection from unrealistic facility pressure
  • The therapy team operates independently from nursing management
  • Excellent patient outcomes and a strong reputation in the region
  • Flexible work shift scheduling options

Training & Support

We don't believe in "sink or swim."

You'll receive:

  • Structured onboarding and integration
  • 1:1 documentation and treatment training
  • Mentorship tailored to your experience level
  • Ongoing clinical support when you need it

New grads are welcomed and supported!


Benefits

We invest in our clinicians in ways that support both career and life:

  • Up to 3 1/2 weeks PTO annually
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Continuing Education reimbursement (up to $750/year)
  • Health Savings Account to save for future expenses
  • Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance
  • Free preventive screening benefits
  • Basic Life and Accidental Death Insurance
  • Voluntary Life and Disability Insurance
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Employee Assistance Program to help navigate life's challenges
  • Teladoc- a free service that gives you access to doctors for a variety of services

Requirements

  • Active Utah PTA license in good standing
  • Graduate of an accredited PTA program
  • Interest in geriatric care and functional outcomes
  • SNF experience preferred but not required

If you're a PTA who values meaningful work, supportive leadership, and sustainable expectations, we'd love to talk.

Apply today - we're actively interviewing.

title: Knife Grinder
description:
Hood Plywood, a division of Hood Industries Inc., is seeking a reliable and motivated Knife Grinder for our Beaumont, MS plywood facility. This role is responsible for maintaining the performance and precision of our cutting equipment, ensuring all knives and blades are sharpened, balanced, and properly maintained. The ideal candidate has mechanical aptitude, experience with grinding equipment, and a strong commitment to safety and quality.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Operate and maintain knife grinding equipment to sharpen, grind, and maintain sawmill knives, chipper knives, and related cutting tools.
  • Inspect blades regularly for wear, damage, and defects; perform adjustments or replacements as needed.
  • Follow established grinding procedures to ensure consistency, accuracy, and quality.
  • Monitor blade performance and make recommendations to improve efficiency and longevity.
  • Maintain accurate records of blade maintenance, repairs, and replacements.
  • Work closely with mill personnel to coordinate workflow and prioritize maintenance needs.
  • Troubleshoot equipment issues and perform basic maintenance on grinding machinery.
  • Adhere to all safety policies and procedures to promote a safe work environment.
  • Stay informed on industry best practices and advancements in blade maintenance and grinding techniques.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Previous experience as a knife grinder, machinist, saw filer, or in a similar industrial role.
  • Strong knowledge of knife grinding equipment, techniques, and safety practices.
  • Ability to operate and maintain industrial grinding machinery.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to precision work.
  • Strong problem-solving and mechanical troubleshooting skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, physically demanding environment.
  • Good communication and teamwork skills.
  • Willingness to work flexible shifts, including overtime if needed

Physical Requirements:

  • Perform tasks such as walking, climbing steps, pushing, pulling, maintaining balance, kneeling, squatting, grasping, and standing for long periods.
  • Willing able to work in a hot, cold, noisy, industrial environment.
  • Operate heavy industrial grinding equipment
  • Reach above shoulders and perform repetitive motions.
  • Climb stairs and ladders.
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 lbs. throughout the work shift.

Pay Range: $20.37 - $22.95/per hour

Additional Information:

Hood Industries offers a competitive salary and an excellent benefits package including medical, employee assistance program, dental, vision, cancer, flexible spending account, life, 401k, and LTD, available first of the month following completion of one month of continuous full-time employment.

Hood Industries requires that applicants consent to a background check and a drug screen to continue in the selection process. All employment offers are contingent on meeting our background check standards and successful passing of required drug test. If hired, you will be required to provide documentation indicating your legal right to work in the U.S.

An Equal Opportunity Employer

title: Seasonal Retail Stock - Main Street at Exton Rack
description:
Job Description

Are you ready to thrive in a fast-paced, high-energy environment? As a Nordstrom Rack team member, you'll be continuously moving and collaborating with teammates to create a welcoming and inclusive atmosphere for all customers. You’ll ensure a quick and easy customer experience and keep the store clean and clutter free. Flexibility is key, as you may occasionally work in different areas of the store to maintain the cleanliness of the floor and stockrooms and help customers find great deals.

We have roles available in Sales, Customer Service, Stock, and Fulfillment departments. Apply now and discuss which role interests you most during the interview process.

A day in the life for Sales and Customer Service …

  • Work with the team to ensure the salesfloor stays "runway ready", and is sized and filled in through re-merchandising and straightening throughout the day
  • Assist customers when cashiering with a variety of transactions across different platforms (in-store, online and mobile), which includes operating a point-of-sale system, bagging items of all size, handling bulky sometimes heavy items including boxes, and ensuring a seamless and friendly experience
  • Create a smooth fitting room experience when supporting as a fitting room attendant by greeting and assisting customers and sorting and returning clothing to the floor
  • Create a clean and clutter-free customer experience by sorting and returning clothing to the salesfloor
  • Keep the stockrooms organized and ensure merchandise is properly checked in and accurately ticketed
  • Demonstrate expertise in all technologies used in the store environment
  • Adhere to all operational, merchandise and asset protection standards
  • Promote initiatives like our Nordstrom Rewards program

A day in a life for Stock Support and Fulfillment…

  • Receive, unload freight, unpack and deliver newly arrived merchandise to selling departments
  • Fulfill customer orders in a timely manner following quality standards
  • Prepare and ship customer’s orders following quality, packing and shipping standards
  • Utilize inventory management systems to scan, process and research merchandise shipments in accordance with our inventory control processes
  • Assist in maintaining clean and organized selling floors and stockrooms
  • Provide general support to the store, e.g. set up special events, organize backroom, markdowns, and relocate store fixtures

You own this if you have…

  • Clear, effective communication with strong interpersonal skills
  • Accountability, initiative and a high level of ownership
  • Organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment
  • The ability to work a flexible schedule based on business needs
  • Physical Requirements:
    • Continuous movement for 6-8 hours per shift, which includes frequent bending, twisting, squatting, flexing and reaching in order to handle merchandise and assist customers.
    • Frequent use of hands for grasping, fine manipulation, pushing and pulling
    • Handle bulky and sometimes awkwardly shaped items, which includes reaching for and lifting these items above the head.
    • Regularly lift items weighing up to 10 pounds and occasionally up to 25 pounds
    • Stock and Fulfillment Only: Frequently lift and carry up to 25 pounds and occasionally up to 50 pounds

title: Programme Coordinator, Google Implementation Programme
description:
About Datahash

Datahash is a privacy-centric first-party data platform. Our core product, Datahash Signals, gives marketers low-code, no-code integrations between web, app, e-commerce, CRM, marketing automation and data warehouses on one side and the major ad channels on the other: Meta, Google, TikTok, Snap, Amazon and more. We are one of a handful of badged integration partners across these channels and work with them directly on first-party data adoption programmes, where advertisers are moving to server-side integrations, conversions APIs and privacy-safe measurement. We are bootstrapped, profitable, and run across Dubai, Bangalore, Mumbai and London with clients in EMEA, India, Africa, APAC and the US.

The role

This is a conversation-and-escalation seat, deliberately scoped small. Tracking, classification, reporting, scheduling and follow-up drafting for the Google Implementation Programme are carried by agents; you carry what an agent cannot: partner conversations with Google's programme teams, escalations when a nomination is stuck, purchase order chases with partner finance, and the judgement calls on the programme's weekly progress report before it goes to Google. If you like being the person a partner calls when something needs a human, this is the seat.

What you will do

  1. Be the partner's person. Own the working relationship with Google's programme operations teams across regions: their questions, our escalations, the weekly progress report and the monthly cohort cadence.
  2. Clear the money. Chase partner purchase orders and payout approvals to a 21-day cycle; clear the approved-unpaid backlog with finance and keep it clear.
  3. Escalate. Pick up nominations the desk cannot move (unresponsive advertisers, verification disputes, tag gaps) and resolve them with the partner.
  4. Review before it ships. Read the agent-produced funnel and quality reports for sense before they go to Google; own the corrections.

What success looks like

  • Purchase order cycle at or below 21 days and the unpaid backlog cleared and held.
  • Weekly partner report delivered every week with no corrections from Google.
  • Escalations closed inside the partner's expectations.

How we hire

We move fast and we are transparent about how we decide. An AI assistant helps us screen applications against the must-haves in this description and helps schedule conversations; every decision about a person is made by a person.

Step 1: a short structured screen within two working days of applying. Step 2: a 50-minute conversation with the hiring manager. Step 3: a small case exercise close to the real work, which you present to two or three of us. Step 4: fit and terms with our VP Delivery or Head of Sales and Partnerships, and for senior roles the founder. We aim to give you a decision within five working days of the final conversation.

We evaluate evidence rather than claims, the quality of your questions, how you handle ambiguity, and how naturally you already use AI in your own work.


Requirements

What we need from you

  • One to three years in programme coordination, partner operations, customer success or account management with an external stakeholder you had to manage.
  • Calm, precise written and spoken English; you are comfortable on a call with a large partner's operations team.
  • Comfort with finance basics: purchase orders, invoices, payout terms.
  • Daily use of AI tools; you supervise agent output rather than produce trackers by hand.

Nice to have

  • Experience in a Google, Meta or similar partner programme.
  • Experience with Zoho CRM and Zoho Desk.

Probably not a fit if

  • You expect the job to be building and maintaining trackers; the agents do that.
  • You avoid difficult conversations with partners or finance teams.

Benefits

  • A startup environment backed by a stable, bootstrapped, profitable business.
  • Competitive compensation and one of the most employee-friendly ESOP programmes in the industry.
  • Work from anywhere, on your hours; coworking access when you want a change from home.
  • Health cover for you and your family.
  • Real international exposure: clients and partners across the Gulf, Europe, Africa, India, APAC and the US.
  • A yearly offsite that we take seriously, and a culture that does not.

Datahash is an equal-opportunity employer. We hire on evidence and fit for the work and do not ask for salary history. Compensation is discussed at the fit-and-terms stage.

Position: Senior Therapeutic Area Specialist
Therapeutic Area (TA): Psychiatry
Location: Philadelphia, PA; Philadelphia, PA/Sharon Hill, PA/Cheltenham, PA

At Bristol Myers Squibb, we are inspired by a single vision – transforming patients’ lives through science. The BMS Mission is to discover, develop and deliver innovative medicines that help patients prevail over serious diseases. In oncology, hematology, immunology and cardiovascular disease – and one of the most diverse and promising pipelines in the industry – each of our passionate colleagues contribute to innovations that drive meaningful change. We bring a human touch to every treatment we pioneer.

Join us, build your professional career within one of the most innovative bio-pharma companies, and make a difference.

Position Summary:

The TAS is a critical role in our unique customer model to execute the BMS aspiration to be the BioPharma that delivers the most impactful engagement with Health Care Providers (HCPs), driving adoption of new and existing medicines for appropriate patients.

The primary role of the TAS is to drive demand for BMS medicines within their portfolio for the appropriate patients. To meet the HCPs expectations, the TAS engages them with a differentiated Customer Experience (Cx) through deeper scientific dialogue on and consistent with label, leveraging new ways of working and CE^3.

The role builds and maintains strong professional credibility with regional thought leaders (RTLs) and community-based physicians/HCPs in private practice, medical groups practices, office staff, and other stakeholders in the patient care continuum as their primary point of contact.

The TAS liaises with other BMS functions as needed to deliver an overall higher Customer Experience (Cx) – by meeting HCP needs in a timely and scientific manner. This role will prioritize the safe and appropriate use of BMS products while also focusing on overall business results and performance objectives while exemplifying BMS values.

The TAS role is field-based. A TAS is anticipated to spend 100% of their time in the field with external customers.

Key Responsibilities:

Portfolio Promotion

  • Promotes approved indications of BMS products within a defined territory or region to meet or exceed assigned sales targets in a compliant manner.
  • Creates demand for BMS medicines by articulating in a balanced manner the clinical and scientific rationale for use of products in appropriate patients.
  • Engages with and continuously maintains/grows a high level of scientific expertise in all assigned products and therapeutic areas.
  • Prepares and successfully implements comprehensive territory and account plans.
  • Proactively uses available tools such as CE^3 (once implemented) to derive insights and to dynamically inform call plans. Provides feedback on experience using these tools to leadership to enable continuous improvement.

Fair & Balanced Scientific Dialogue:

  • Demonstrates scientific expertise and passion in using approved scientific resources and publications to present information to HCPs and ensures medical accuracy.
  • Conducts in-office presentations (e.g., lunch and learns) and discusses product-related scientific information with HCPs that is consistent with label.
  • Organizes external speaker programs, selecting speakers from list approved by Speakers Bureau and facilitating scheduling and logistics.
  • Maintains a high level of working expertise on emerging data for approved indications.
  • Engages real-time medical support through Medical on Call to reactively answer unsolicited questions and complex technical inquiries.

Cross-Functional Collaboration:

  • Proactively collaborates with other field teams to ensure the best Customer Experience (Cx) for HCPs.
  • Gathers and shares relevant insights and information internally with the appropriate stakeholders to enable BMS to better serve its customers.
  • Complies with all laws, regulations, and policies that govern the conduct of BMS.

Required Qualifications & Experience:

  • Advanced scientific degree and/or preferred 5+ years of pharmaceutical or biotechnology experience as healthcare sales / MSL / HCP / nurse.
  • Ability to communicate scientific or clinical data accurately and convincingly to help physicians best serve their patients.
  • Demonstrated experience building and maintaining strong credibility with key customers, office staff, and others in the customer influence network via a customer-centric mindset and desire to create positive and differentiated Customer Experience (Cx).
  • Experience in Neurology preferred.
  • Demonstrated strong capability in account management skill sets, superior selling competencies, and proven sales performance track record of meeting or exceeding goals.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively cross-functionally with a positive team mindset and can-do attitude.
  • Strong selling and promotional skills proven through a track record of performance.

Key Competencies Desired:

Customer/Commercial Mindset

  • Demonstrated ability to drive business results.
  • Experience identifying, engaging, and cultivating credibility with customers across the patient care journey.
  • Demonstrated account management skills and problem-solving mentality. Understands the patient journey and can customize engagement and deliver tailored messages.
  • Demonstrated resourcefulness and ability to connect with customers.

Patient Centricity:

  • Understands the patient journey and experience.
  • Has a patient-focused mindset.

Scientific Agility:

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills to articulate scientific and clinical data in an easy-to-understand manner to help HCPs best serve their patients.
  • Has a strong learning mindset and passion for science. Prioritizes staying current with the latest data.

Analytical Capability:

  • Ability to analyze data, such as prescribing patterns, market trends, and HCP preferences. Data-driven insights help TAS strategize and target their efforts effectively.
  • Ability to segment HCPs based on their preferences and other relevant factors. This helps them tailor their communication and product presentations to suit individual HCP needs.
  • Understanding how to interpret and analyze data related to BMS products, customer preferences, clinical data.
  • Ability to use CE^3 to generate insights and do dynamic call planning.

Technological Agility:

  • Understanding, adapting, and effectively using technology in various aspects of healthcare business and interacting with HCPs.
  • Utilizing various digital communication channels such as emails, instant messaging apps, and video conferencing to stay in touch with healthcare professionals, colleagues, and clients. This enables TAS to respond promptly to inquiries, share updates, and maintain effective communication.
  • Competency using CE^3 and other software or CRM tools to collect, enter, and manage quality data in a timely and compliant manner, track interactions, and plan future engagements with healthcare professionals.
  • Ability to use the Medical on Call technology effectively.
  • Being able to navigate and utilize the internet and online resources effectively.
  • Keeping up to date with technological advancements and changes.

Teamwork/Enterprise Mindset:

  • Strong business acumen to understand and analyze business and market drivers and develop, execute, and adjust business plans.
  • Demonstrates a strong sense of learning agility. Seeks out and learns from unfamiliar experiences, and then applies those lessons to achieve better results in subsequent situations.
  • Track record of balancing individual drive and collaborative attitude.
  • Holds a high level of integrity and good judgment, in order to navigate the requirements of the role effectively and compliantly in accordance with BMS policies and procedures.
  • As this position requires the operation of a Company-provided vehicle, offers of employment are contingent upon the candidate meeting the requirements of “Qualified Driver,” as determined by the Company in its sole discretion, including but not limited to the following: 1) at least 21 years of age; 2) a driver’s license in good standing issued by your state of residence; and, 3) a driving risk level deemed acceptable by the Company.

title: Lead Spare Parts Coordinator - Medicine Foundry

The Spare Parts Coordinator serves as the continuity point for MRO supply across the Lilly Medicine Foundry, maintaining uninterrupted parts availability for every building — from staging through delivery, on-site stock management, and returns to Central MRO for rebuild or repair.

Responsibilities

  • Follow up on open order and return statuses with suppliers/internal stakeholders, proactively flagging shortages or delays

  • Support documentation processes (e.g., matching invoices, work orders, desktop requests, tracking approvals)

Basic Requirements:

  • High School Diploma

  • Minimum five years of industrial MRO coordination or planning experience

  • Demonstrated ability to prioritize, set objectives, and meet targets

  • Demonstrated ability to provide high-level customer service

  • Demonstrated ability to work autonomously

  • Demonstrated ability in problem solving

  • Computer proficiency

Other Information:

  • Initial location at Lilly Technology Center, Indianapolis or Parkwood West, Carmel, IN

  • Permanent location at the new Lilly Medicines Foundry in Lebanon, Indiana.

title: Consultant / Senior Consultant - Strategy 3

About Ipsos Singapore

Passionately curious is how we define ourselves at Ipsos. Using market research, we gain an accurate and deep understanding of a person, brand or market to help our client make smart, strategic business decisions. With the potential to change the world in a small and big ways, we strongly believe in what we do, while making sure we have fun while doing it.

Strategy3 is Ipsos’ business and growth advisory firm.
We believe that for any business strategy, marketing plan, brand positioning, or innovation to be successful, it must do three things: be rooted in the organization’s strategy, be informed and inspired by customer research, and it must drive through to actual in-market activation. While many firms advise on growth, very few deliver on all three: traditional management consultancies rarely delve deep enough into the world of the customer; creative firms don’t truly leverage the power of data; research agencies can sometimes lose the big picture amid analysis. 11. Support development and execution of agenda and approach to operating routines including leadership meetings and business reviews.
12. Prepare formal presentations for the CWBO, including regular town halls, leadership meetings, and leadership offsites.
13. Develop and drive consistent adoption of templates, processes, and approaches to streamline core and common functions including meetings, events & client engagement, business overviews, headcount tracking and management, HR initiatives, etc.

15. Support a culture of collaboration and trust through frequent and transparent communication, professionalism, and respect.

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
1. Bachelor’s degree in Business, or equivalent education and related training or experience to include 10+ years of experience in positions that carry increasing levels of responsibility, including experience in strategy or business consulting

3. Excellent communication skills (written and verbal)
4. Strong cross-functional collaboration skills
5. Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to engage with stakeholders at all levels in the organization

Preferred Qualifications:
7. 4+ years of credit, portfolio, and/or relationship management experience
8. Strong knowledge and experience in strategic planning and execution, including creating and executing comprehensive plans associated with business mergers, conversions, product changes, technology releases, policy changes, and line of business strategic plans

10. Proven ability to collaborate across organizational silos
11. Ability to think strategically while delivering tactically
12. Ability to translate and present complex data in a manner that educates, enhances understanding, and influences decisions
13. Advanced skills in data visualization and storytelling
14. Deep knowledge of wholesale banking including corporate, commercial, and payments
15. Strong executive presence and communication skills
16. Sense of urgency and ability to multi-task and manage competing projects in a deadline-driven environment

title: Program Director - Life Sciences
description:
We are seeking an experienced Program Director to drive execution of our Life Sciences Growth Strategy. This role serves as the operational backbone for a cross-functional portfolio of initiatives, ensuring that strategic priorities translate into coordinated, on-track delivery. The ideal candidate combines strong program management discipline with enough technical fluency to work credibly with engineering, product, data, and clinical/regulatory stakeholders, and enough business acumen to keep execution tied to growth outcomes.

This is a high-visibility, individual contributor role reporting into senior leadership, with regular exposure to executive stakeholders and cross-functional teams across the Life Sciences business.

  • Own portfolio execution: Serve as the central point of coordination across the Life Sciences Growth Strategy portfolio, tracking scope, timelines, dependencies, risks, and resourcing across multiple concurrent workstreams.

  • Drive delivery cadence: Establish and run program governance — status reviews, steering committees, roadmap check-ins — that keep leadership and stakeholders aligned on progress and blockers.

  • Manage cross-functional dependencies: Identify and resolve interdependencies between engineering, product, data science, commercial, regulatory, and clinical teams; escalate and unblock issues before they threaten timelines.

  • Translate strategy into execution plans: Partner with leadership to break the Growth Strategy's priorities into structured programs, workstreams, and milestones with clear owners and success metrics.

  • Manage risk proactively: Maintain a live risk and issue log across the portfolio; drive mitigation plans and ensure risks are surfaced to the right decision-makers early.

  • Report on progress and health: Build and maintain portfolio-level dashboards and executive-ready status reporting that clearly communicate progress, risk, and resourcing needs.

  • Support resource planning: Work with functional leads to understand capacity constraints and help sequence work across the portfolio accordingly.

  • Champion process improvement: Identify and implement process, tooling, or communication improvements that increase the speed and reliability of execution across the portfolio.

  • Bridge technical and business conversations: Work fluently with technical teams to understand delivery realities, while translating those realities into business-relevant updates for non-technical stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

  • 14+ years of program or project management experience, including managing complex, multi-workstream portfolios in a technical or product environment.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting or driving execution of a strategic initiative at the organizational level (growth strategy, transformation program, multi-team platform effort, etc.).
  • Strong working knowledge of program management practices: roadmapping, dependency management, risk management, resource planning, and status reporting.
  • Comfort working directly with engineering and technical teams — able to understand technical constraints and trade-offs well enough to manage timelines and risk credibly.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, including experience communicating with and influencing senior leadership.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to synthesize complex, cross-functional information into clear, actionable updates.
  • Proven ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy and ownership in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
  • Experience in Life Sciences, healthcare, pharma, or a related regulated industry.
  • Familiarity with regulatory, clinical, or commercial workflows relevant to Life Sciences organizations.
  • Experience with program management tooling (e.g., Jira, Asana, Smartsheet, Confluence) and portfolio-level reporting.
  • PMP, PgMP, SAFe, or equivalent program/project management certification.
  • Experience building or scaling program governance structures from the ground up.

title: Senior Systems Engineer
location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
description:
Job Description

Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Austin TX IT Innovation Center or Warren Michigan GM Technical Center 3-4 days per week (T-W-Th)

The Role

The Senior Systems Engineer provides application operations support and application ownership for production-critical applications used at vehicle and propulsion manufacturing sites. Using Site Reliability Engineering practices, this role helps ensure application availability, reliable performance, effective monitoring, and timely issue resolution.

You will work across Linux, Windows, Kubernetes, cloud, Oracle, SQL Server, and PostgreSQL environments. You will collaborate with business and technology teams to troubleshoot issues, implement improvements, support deployments, maintain documentation, and deliver reliable services to manufacturing operations.

What You’ll Do

  • Support applications used in vehicle assembly and propulsion manufacturing environments.
  • Monitor the health, availability, and performance of applications and infrastructure.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve application issues within agreed service levels.
  • Design and implement configuration changes that support business needs.
  • Support production issue resolution, code deployments, patch releases, and other critical activities.
  • Perform root-cause analysis with application, infrastructure, development, deployment, and database teams.
  • Create and maintain procedures for troubleshooting, maintenance, monitoring, and recovery.
  • Manage certificates, technical documentation, application ownership activities, and support processes.
  • Use queries and diagnostic tools to investigate issues across databases and operating environments.
  • Build strong relationships with business partners, technical teams, colleagues, and management.
  • Follow established information technology, security, and operational processes.
  • Provide remote technical support to manufacturing sites.
  • Participate in a 24x7 on-call rotation after completing the required acclimation period.
  • Contribute to a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing team culture.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of experience in a technical information technology (IT) role.
  • 3+ years of experience supporting Linux and/or Windows operating systems.
  • Experience with Oracle and/or SQL databases.
  • Knowledge of Docker containers and Kubernetes container orchestration.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to data integrity and accuracy.
  • Ability to support production-critical applications and participate in an on-call rotation.

What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Experience supporting applications in a manufacturing or plant operations environment.
  • Experience with Site Reliability Engineering practices, application monitoring, or service-level objectives.
  • Experience with cloud platforms, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, or infrastructure automation.
  • Experience with observability, incident management, problem management, or root-cause analysis.
  • Experience using Glean or a similar enterprise AI and knowledge-search platform.
  • Ability to use generative AI to troubleshoot incidents, summarize technical issues, create runbooks, and improve application-support workflows.
  • Strong prompt-writing and AI-output validation skills.
  • Understanding of responsible AI use, access controls, data privacy, and protection of confidential information.
  • Experience with AI-assisted automation, scripting, APIs, monitoring, or observability tools.
  • Knowledge of manufacturing, plant operations, or production-critical systems.

Work Environment

This role supports production-critical applications used by manufacturing operations. The position may require support during critical production periods, non-traditional working hours, deployments, patch releases, and on-call coverage. The role provides remote technical support to manufacturing sites and may require work from a designated company facility according to the approved work arrangement.

description:

Transforming lives through excellent education

London Met is an extraordinary institution. Equity and social inclusion have always been our driving principles, and it's what makes the University so unique.   • Advanced communication and presentation skills (executive-level decks, whiteboarding, facilitating decision sessions)
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience required; MBA or other advanced degree preferred.
  • Travel up to ~10%, variable by portfolio

The total compensation package for this role includes base salary and bonus. The base salary range for this position is between $172,000 and $258,000. Placement within the pay range is at Grant Thornton’s discretion, and it is based on multiple factors, including but not limited to, job-related knowledge/skills, experience, business needs, progression within the role, geographic location, and internal equity. title: Stock Clerk (AY1), Fort Bliss, TX
description:
Technica LLC seeks to recruit for the position of Stock Clerk (AY1) on a government contract with a place of performance at Fort Bliss, TX

Position Summary

The Stock Clerk performs warehouse functions which include but, not limited to (i.e., receives, stores, and issues equipment, materials, supplies, and compiles stock records of items within the warehouse and/or storage yard, inventory management, storage management, cataloging, property utilization, remediation packaging etc.) related to depot, local, or other supply activities utilizing the Global Combat Support System-Army (GCSS-Army). This work may require consideration of program requirements, together with specific variations in or from standardized guidelines. The Stock Clerk sorts, weighs incoming articles to verify receipt of items on requisition or invoice, examines stock to verify conformance to specifications, stores articles in bins, on floor or on shelves, according to identifying information, such as style, size or type or material, fills orders or issues supplies from stock, prepares periodic, special, or perpetual inventory of stock, and requisitions articles to fill incoming orders. In addition, this work requires remediation packaging of items/equipment to prolong shelf-life and prevent damage of supplies. The Stock Clerk will prepare items/equipment for shipment out of the facility utilizing Cargo Movement Operations System (CMOS). This work consists of compiling reports on use of stock handling equipment, adjustments of inventory counts and stock records, damage to stock, location changes, and refusal of shipments, may mark identifying codes, figures, or letters on articles, may distribute stock among productions workers, keeping records of material issued, may adjust or repairs to articles carried in stock, and may cut stock to site to fill order. title: Quality Control Analyst I
description:
Quality Control Analyst I

Location: This position is based in our Walkersville, MD office. The typical work schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM EST.

What you will get:

The full-time base annual salary for this position is expected to range between $61,200 to $71,400. In addition, below you will find a comprehensive summary of the benefits package we offer:

  • Performance-related bonus.

  • Medical, dental and vision insurance.

  • 401(k) matching plan.

  • Life insurance, as well as short-term and long-term disability insurance.

  • Employee assistance programs.

  • Paid time off (PTO).

Compensation for this role will be determined by the candidate’s qualifications, skills, experience, and relevant knowledge.

What will you do:

We are seeking a Quality Control Analyst I to perform routine laboratory sampling and testing activities in support of GMP manufacturing operations. This role is primarily focused on the execution of environmental monitoring, utility, raw material, in-process, finished product, and stability testing while ensuring compliance with cGMP requirements, data integrity standards, and approved procedures. The successful candidate will contribute to laboratory operations through accurate testing, documentation, and sample management activities.

  • Perform routine sampling and testing of environmental monitoring (EM), utilities, raw materials, in-process materials, finished products, and stability samples in accordance with approved procedures and cGMP requirements.

  • Execute assigned laboratory testing and support activities within established timelines while maintaining accuracy, quality, and compliance.

  • Accurately document, review, and report laboratory data in compliance with Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.

  • Conduct environmental monitoring activities within classified manufacturing and laboratory environments, including viable and non-viable monitoring, surface sampling, and personnel monitoring as applicable.

  • Support sample receipt, handling, storage, inventory tracking, and shipment coordination with external testing laboratories.

  • Support day-to-day laboratory operations, including housekeeping, inventory management, material stocking, and routine equipment care.

  • Identify, document, and escalate deviations, atypical results, out-of-specification (OOS) results, or compliance concerns in accordance with quality procedures.

  • Participate in training activities to expand technical proficiency and support validation, continuous improvement, or innovation projects as assigned.

What we are looking for:

  • Associate degree, technical certification, military laboratory training, or equivalent combination of education and relevant laboratory experience preferred; relevant GMP laboratory experience may be considered in lieu of formal education.

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life sciences, or other regulated laboratory environment.

  • Experience performing routine laboratory testing and sample handling activities in a GMP-regulated environment.

  • Experience performing environmental monitoring activities, including viable and non-viable air sampling, surface sampling, personnel monitoring, or utility sampling preferred.

  • Working knowledge of aseptic technique, contamination control principles, laboratory practices, and cGMP requirements.

  • Understanding of Good Documentation Practices (GDP), ALCOA+ principles, and data integrity requirements.

  • Ability to accurately follow written procedures, maintain laboratory records, and execute testing with attention to detail.

  • Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple testing priorities under supervision.

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively within a quality and manufacturing environment.

About Lonza

At Lonza, our people are our greatest strength. With 30+ sites across five continents, our globally connected teams work together every day to manufacture the medicines of tomorrow. Our core values of Collaboration, Accountability, Excellence, Passion and Integrity reflect who we are and how we work together. Everyone’s ideas, big or small, have the potential to improve millions of lives, and that’s the kind of work we want you to be part of.

Innovation thrives when people from all backgrounds bring their unique perspectives to the table. At Lonza, we offer equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. If you’re ready to help turn our customers’ breakthrough ideas into viable therapies, we look forward to welcoming you on board.

Ready to shape the future of life sciences? Apply now.

title: Market Research Analyst, Brand Health Tracking
description:
Who We Are:

Ipsos is one of the world's largest research companies and the only one primarily managed by researchers. Ranked the #1 Most Innovative Market Research Supplier by Greenbook’s GRIT report for four consecutive years, we operate in 90 markets, offer more than 75 data-driven solutions, and serve over 5,000 clients worldwide. Our research, methodological, implementation, and subject matter experts help organizations solve complex business challenges through data-driven insights and evidence-based decision-making. We're proud to have been named one of Forbes' America's Best Employers for Company Culture in 2025, Forbes' America's Best Employers for Women in 2026 and recognized by Newsweek as one of the World’s Most Trustworthy Companies in 2026.

We are looking for someone who is deeply curious about people, brands, and business growth. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys asking questions, solving problems, uncovering patterns in data, and translating insights into action. This is an excellent entry-level opportunity for someone who is interested in starting a career in market research.

About Brand Health Tracking:

Brand building drives business growth by strengthening relationships with consumers, building desire over time. The Brand Health Tracking Service Line at Ipsos helps clients understand how people feel about their brands, tracks changes in performance over time, and provides insight into how advertising may be influencing consumer attitudes towards clients’ brands.

What makes this role important at Ipsos?

As part of the Brand Health Tracking team, you'll help some of Canada's leading organizations understand what drives brand performance and business growth. Working across categories including financial services, retail, telecommunications, technology, travel, QSR, CPG, and healthcare, you'll gain exposure to a wide range of business challenges, consumer behaviours, and growth opportunities.

You'll work day-to-day with data to uncover meaningful insights, collaborate across teams to solve client challenges, and develop the skills needed to become a trusted advisor. This role combines analytical thinking, problem solving, project management, and communication, providing a strong foundation for a career in brand strategy, insights, and advisory.

As you build your experience, your role can evolve beyond project execution. You'll have opportunities to contribute to client discussions, help synthesize and present findings, and support recommendations that influence business, brand, and marketing decisions. Over time, you'll develop the skills, confidence, and commercial perspective needed to become a trusted advisor to some of Canada's leading brands, helping turn consumer understanding into actions that drive growth.

What you can expect to be doing:

  • Develop and update surveys, and maintain technical specifications in proprietary software

  • Liaise with internal operations teams to progress projects through their lifecycle

  • Perform quality checks throughout the project lifecycle

  • Perform data verification and prepare reports

  • Identify and solve project issues as they arise

This might be the job for you if you have:

  • Completed Bachelor’s degree

  • Experience in research, analytics, consulting, marketing, project management, business strategy, customer experience, communications, or related fields is an asset.

  • Interest in business, marketing, consumer behavior and brand strategy

  • Outstanding verbal and written communication skills

  • Strong intellectual curiosity, excellent problem solving, and an analytical mindset

  • Ability to simplify complex information

  • High attention to detail: ability to balance overall project goal with key milestones and tasks

  • Emerging leadership skills

  • Advanced proficiency with MS Office Suite; specifically, PowerPoint and Excel

  • Ability to juggle multiple projects and diplomatically respond to conflicting needs

  • Bilingual an asset but not required.

We think you'll be successful if you are:

  • Naturally curious and eager to understand why consumers behave the way they do

  • Someone who asks thoughtful questions and enjoys challenging assumptions

  • A confident communicator

  • Interested in understanding how brands grow and compete

  • Comfortable working with both data and people

  • Motivated by learning and continuous development in terms of new tools, methodologies and skills

If you don’t meet 100% of the requirements, we encourage all who feel they might be a fit for the opportunity to apply. We may consider a variety of backgrounds for a particular role and are also committed to considering candidates for available positions throughout our organization, not just the one you’re applying to!

In accordance with Ontario & British Columbia law, the estimated base salary range for this role is $50,000 to $55,000 CAD. Your final base salary will be determined based on several non-discriminatory factors which may include but are not limited to location, work experience, skills, knowledge, education and/or certifications.

What’s in it for you:

At Ipsos you’ll experience opportunities for Career Development, an exceptional benefits package (including generous PTO, healthcare plans, wellness benefits), a flexible workplace policy, and a strong collaborative culture.

To find out more about all the great reasons to work at Ipsos, how we’re making an impact around the world, and more about our benefits and employee programs, please visit: Why Work at Ipsos | CA

Inclusive Workplace Commitment

Ipsos recognizes the necessity of building an inclusive culture that values each employee’s individuality and diverse perspectives. For more than 40 years, our mission has been to generate and analyze data about society, markets, brands, and behaviors to provide our clients with the insights that elevate their understanding of the world. This could not be fulfilled without Ipsos’ diverse employees who compile and analyze this data—they are the essence of who we are and what we do.

We are committed to providing equal opportunity to all employees, creating an environment that promotes inclusion, and enabling employees from all walks of life to flourish. Ipsos encourages our employees to act in a respectful and responsible manner, in line with code of best practices concerning diversity and inclusion, human rights, equality, and civility for every individual.

Ipsos is An Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or any other protected class and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.

title: Investment Product Analyst
description:
About Schroders

Schroders is a global investment manager which provides active asset management, wealth management and investment solutions. We aim to provide excellent investment performance to clients through active management. We serve a diverse client base that includes pension schemes, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, foundations, high net worth individuals, family offices, as well as end clients through partnerships with distributors, financial advisers, and online platforms.

Established in 1804, we have around 5,500 people across 36 global locations. Schroders' success can be attributed to its diversified business model, spanning different asset classes, client types and geographies.

Position Overview

The Investment Product Analyst will work closely with the combined Credit and Emerging Markets Debt Product and Investment teams to deliver investment and product information to a range of internal and external clients. Excellent data management and technology skills are required, with attention to detail and the ability to meet deadlines. Knowledge of fixed income and equity markets is required.

Responsibilities

  • Prepare and report portfolio characteristics, statistics, and other investment data primarily for Credit and Emerging Markets Debt products to internal and external clients in a timely manner. Accounts include segregated mandates, UCITS, US mutual funds, CITs and LPs.
  • Update data for strategy and fund presentations as well as client marketing material including fund fact sheets, sales aids and quarterly investment reports.
  • Write product and client monthly and quarterly commentaries including market updates, attribution, positioning and outlook.
  • Update consultant and client databases with product data and portfolio information
  • Provide ad hoc analysis and responses for product and client queries
  • Assist with competitive analysis using Morningstar and eVestment
  • Write, update and maintain product language and data for products in the RFP databases and work with RFP and client portfolio managers to customize as needed.
  • Develop comprehensive product knowledge on fixed income investments and all USFI and USMA products.

Basic Qualifications

  • Minimum 2 years fixed income investment experience, preferably at an asset management firm, investment consultant, firm, with basic knowledge of fixed income markets and products
  • Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in a finance related field. CFA or advanced degree a plus
  • Strong math, data management, and quantitative skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office software, especially Excel and PowerPoint. Experience with Macros and VBA a plus
  • Strong writing skills
  • Ability to take initiative, work independently as well as part of a team
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office software, especially Excel and PowerPoint. Experience with Macros and VBA a plus
  • Must be detailed oriented and highly organized with the ability to meet deadlines

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of Thomson Reuters Refinitiv Eikon
  • Understanding of Credit and Emerging Markets Debt
  • Experience with credit research and investing

Compensation

Schroders offers a base salary in a range of $100,000 to $120,000 for this position.

The referenced salary range is based on the Company's good faith belief at the time of posting. Actual compensation may vary based on factors such as geographic location, work experience, market conditions, education/training and skill level.

We recognize potential, whoever you are

Our purpose is to deliver excellent investment performance to clients through active management. We believe diverse perspectives and an inclusive culture help us make better decisions and achieve better outcomes for our clients. That's why inclusion is a strategic priority for us, and we are an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome here, regardless of your race, color, national origin, age, disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religious beliefs, socio-economic background, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

We will consider flexible working arrangements for all roles and provide reasonable accommodations to support applicants and employees, including those with neurodiversity, disability, or physical and mental health needs. For more information, please visit our FAQs.

title: Remote Solutions Consultant
description:
Position Overview

The Inbound Sales Representative helps customers identify and purchase vending machines, smart coolers, micro markets, and other automated retail solutions. This position works exclusively with company-generated inbound leads from individuals and businesses that have already expressed interest in our products and services.

This is a consultative sales role focused on understanding customer needs, recommending solutions, and guiding customers through the purchasing process from initial inquiry to close. The ideal candidate enjoys building relationships, uncovering customer needs, and helping customers make informed purchasing decisions. No cold calling, door-to-door sales, or self-generated prospecting is required.

Success in this role requires the ability to manage multiple customer conversations and communication channels throughout the day while remaining fully engaged with each prospective customer. We value responsiveness and efficiency, but never at the expense of the customer experience. The ideal candidate understands when to move quickly and when to slow down, ask thoughtful questions, and take the time necessary to earn the sale.

This role is best suited for a sales professional who combines a consultative approach with a strong closing mindset. Successful candidates are comfortable guiding customers toward decisions, addressing objections directly, and confidently asking for the sale when the proposed solution meets the customer's needs.

Duties and Responsibilities

· Respond promptly and professionally to company-generated inbound sales inquiries.

· Engage prospective customers by phone, email, live chat, text messaging, video conference, and scheduled callbacks.

· Consult with customers to understand their business goals, locations, operating plans, product needs, budget considerations, and purchasing timeline.

· Recommend appropriate vending, smart cooler, micro market, and automated retail solutions based on each customer’s needs.

· Explain product capabilities, ownership considerations, available services, and applicable purchasing or financing options in a clear and accurate manner.

· Develop and present customized proposals, equipment recommendations, and follow-up communications.

· Guide customers through the complete sales process from initial inquiry through order placement.

· Consistently follow up with active opportunities while prioritizing the most time-sensitive and sales-ready leads.

· Maintain accurate customer records, notes, next steps, and sales activities within the CRM system.

· Coordinate with internal teams to support order accuracy, customer expectations, and a smooth handoff after the sale.

· Follow established sales processes, pricing guidance, documentation standards, and company policies.

· Participate in coaching, training, team meetings, product education, and ongoing professional development.

· Meet established expectations for responsiveness, sales activity, conversion, revenue, follow-up, and customer experience.

· Perform other duties as assigned in support of customers and the sales organization.

Required Qualifications

· Prior experience in sales, inside sales, business development, customer service, or another customer-facing role.

· Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to explain solutions clearly and confidently.

· Demonstrated ability to build rapport, ask effective discovery questions, address concerns, and guide customers toward a decision.

· Ability to work independently, stay organized, and maintain accountability in a remote environment.

· Comfort learning and using CRM systems, phone platforms, email, chat, text messaging, video conferencing, and other digital sales tools.

· Ability to manage multiple customer opportunities, follow-up commitments, and communication channels without losing attention to detail.

· A reliable internet connection and a professional, distraction-controlled home workspace.

· Ability to travel periodically to Des Moines, Iowa, when requested.

Preferred Experience

· Experience working in a remote sales environment with multiple customer communication channels, including phone, email, chat, text messaging, and scheduled callbacks.

· Experience managing a consistent flow of inbound opportunities while maintaining thoughtful, consultative customer engagement.

· Demonstrated ability to balance responsiveness and efficiency without sacrificing the quality of the customer experience.

· Experience independently managing a sales pipeline, prioritizing opportunities, and maintaining consistent follow-up.

· Experience selling equipment, technology, business solutions, capital goods, or products that require discovery and recommendation rather than simple order taking.

· Experience with vending, automated retail, unattended retail, foodservice equipment, or related industries is helpful but not required.

title: Corporate Complaints Officer
description:
• East Suffolk Council: East Suffolk House, Melton, and/or Riverside, Lowestoft
  • £32,578 to £35,570 per annum
  • Band 5 (SCP 18 to 23)
  • 37 hours per week
  • Permanent

East Suffolk Council is an exciting place to work and a great place to make a real difference to people’s lives, delivering vital services to a quarter of a million people across East Suffolk. We currently have an exciting new opportunity to join the East Suffolk Council's Policy, Performance and Risk Team as a Corporate Complaints Officer.

We are looking for a proactive and customer-focused Corporate Complaints Officer to be part of a dedicated team that is responsible for the day-to-day administration of the council's customer feedback process. This varied role involves coordinating complaints and ombudsman enquiries, providing expert advice and training to colleagues, analysing complaint trends to drive service improvements, and helping to embed a positive complaints culture that delivers excellent customer outcomes across the organisation.

Key Responsibilities:
Working as part of a small team you will play a key role in co-ordinating East Suffolk Council’s customer feedback and complaints processes, ensuring complaints are processed professionally, fairly, and in line with council policy, Ombudsman requirements, and best practice standards.

The role involves coordinating Stage 1 and Stage 2 complaints, supporting high-quality investigations, monitoring performance against service standards, and ensuring agreed actions are implemented. You will co-ordinate and respond to enquiries from the Housing Ombudsman service and the Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman (LGSCO) ensuring responses to enquiries in a timely manner. As part of a team you will provide training, support and templates to complaint responders to ensure they are aware of the principles of how to conduct resident focused complaint investigations.

You will need:

We are looking for a highly organised and customer-focused professional with experience in complaints handling, dispute resolution, and delivering excellent customer service. You will have strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to manage sensitive and complex issues tactfully, diplomatically, and with empathy.

The successful candidate will be able to work independently, manage competing priorities, analyse performance data, and produce clear reports and presentations for a range of audiences. You will have experience of investigating and resolving escalated complaints, maintaining accurate and confidential records, and using IT systems and Microsoft Office applications to a high standard.

A good understanding of local government, regulatory requirements, and customer-focused service delivery is desirable, along with the confidence to challenge processes and influence positive outcomes. If you do not strictly meet the essential criteria but feel that your experience evidences competencies in these areas then you are encouraged to apply.

Why work for us?

East Suffolk Council is a great place to work and there are lots of benefits our employees can access. To find out more about why we are so proud of East Suffolk Council, look at our video and hear why our employees think it is such a great place to work.

Here are some of the main benefits:

  • Great opportunities for training and development
  • Generous leave entitlement (equivalent to 25 days a year, increasing to 31 days after 5 years’ service, plus bank holidays)
  • Local government pension scheme
  • Free car parking (for when you are working in the office)
  • Discounts on mobile phones, computers, holiday and travel, fashion and clothing, health and beauty and many other products and services.

Please see our benefits brochure for further information.

Most of our teams are working in an agile way, with a mixture of home and office working, depending on individual preferences and service requirements. If you wish to discuss how that might impact your working arrangements if you were the successful candidate, please contact the recruiting manager listed at the bottom of this advert.

title: Outreach Coordinator
description:
Join the City of Chattanooga Team

Chattanooga, a vibrant and growing community of over 190,000 residents within a metropolitan area of nearly 600,000 is known as the "Scenic City" for a reason. Nestled along the Tennessee River and surrounded by the foothills of the Appalachian Mountains, we are a hub of outdoor adventure and innovation. Home to the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga (UTC) and Chattanooga State Community College, our city blends a rich industrial history with a tech-forward future—famously powered by the nation’s first community-wide "Gig" fiber-optic network.​ The City of Chattanooga was also recently designated as a "National Park City,” the first of its kind in the United States.

Our Organization

As a City, we are powered by a dedicated workforce of approximately ​2,600 employees committed to excellence in public service and making Chattanooga the best community in the country. Our team ensures our city thrives through a wide range of municipal services, including:

  • Public Safety: Chattanooga Police and Fire Departments.
  • Infrastructure & Utilities: Public Works, Waste Resources, and specialized Stormwater management.
  • Quality of Life: Award-winning Parks and Outdoors and Community Development systems and the Chattanooga Public Library.
  • Transportation: The Chattanooga Metropolitan Airport (CHA) and citywide transit and pedestrian friendly initiatives.
  • Innovation: Leading-edge smart-city programs with a commitment to cutting edge workforce development policies to ensure all our residents can get ahead.

Why Choose Chattanooga?

The City of Chattanooga’s workforce is the heartbeat of our community. We don't just offer jobs; we offer careers with purpose: making Chattanooga the best city in America. We are committed to being the premier employer of choice in Southeast Tennessee by providing:

  • Competitive Compensation: Robust pay scales that reflect our commitment to our staff.
  • Work-Life Balance: Generous paid time off and flexible scheduling where possible.
  • Exceptional Wellness: Comprehensive health benefits and wellness programs designed for you and your family that deliver savings to you beyond your paycheck, featuring a centralized health clinic and pharmacy for all City employees. .
  • Growth: A focus on professional development and upward mobility within the organization.
  • ​The Great Outdoors: Your Backyard Playground: Chattanooga isn't just near nature, it's immersed in it. As one of the most biodiverse cities in North America, the "Scenic City" offers an ecological richness that few places on earth can claim. Whether you are an adrenaline junkie or a weekend wanderer, world-class adventure is always less than an hour away.
  • ​Vertical Adventures: Scale legendary sandstone cliffs in what is widely considered the premier rock climbing hub of the Southeast.
  • Water & Rapids: From the high-octane whitewater kayaking of the Ocoee River to world-class bass fishing and peaceful paddling on the Tennessee River.
  • Trails for Miles: Explore a massive network of mountain biking and hiking trails that wind through lush ridges, hidden waterfalls, and deep river gorges.

In Chattanooga, "work-life balance" means you can finish your shift and be at a trailhead or on the water before the sun sets.

Our mission is to work together to build a safe, vibrant, and sustainable city for all Chattanoogans. To do that, it takes a team of skilled and passionate individuals. So, if you’d like to call Chattanooga home – or maybe you already do! – and want to further your career through meaningful work that makes a true impact where you live, we’d love to talk to you.

Salary: $56,187 - $67,880 annually (GS.10)


Work Hours: Monday – Friday, 8:00 A.M. – 4:30 P.M. (EST)
*Hours may vary due to work assignments or projects. Hours can be flexed for required events in the evening and on weekends *


Work Location: 1250 Market Street, Chattanooga, TN


FLSA Status: This is an Exempt position.


Department: City Planning

CLASSIFICATION SUMMARY:
The Outreach Coordinator develops and executes civic environmental strategies to engage City of Chattanooga employees and residents through targeted media campaigns, public speaking, and community events. Responsible for creating multimedia content—including newsletters, web materials, and promotional videos—the role acts as a primary municipal spokesperson, managing resident inquiries, appearing in local media interviews, and maintaining active stakeholder relationships. Additionally, the Coordinator provides dedicated outreach support to key City divisions such as Parks & Outdoors, Stormwater, Community Development, and Solid Waste, while collecting program data to produce analytical reports. Operating in a blend of office and field environments during local events and technical assistance visits, this position bridges public engagement, cross-departmental collaboration, and data-driven strategy to advance citywide sustainability goals.

SERIES LEVEL:
The Outreach Coordinator is a stand-alone position.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: (The following duties ARE NOT intended to serve as a comprehensive list of all duties performed by all employees in this classification, only a representative summary of the primary duties and responsibilities. Incumbent(s) may not be required to perform all duties listed and may be required to perform additional, position-specific duties.)

Draft and maintain a sustainability outreach strategy for both City employees and Chattanooga residents.

Collect and analyze outreach data.

Process resident-related inquiries regarding sustainability and direct them to appropriate City departments when necessary.

Prepare a variety of reports, documents, informational packets, and/or other materials related to project and program activities and initiatives; disseminate information to applicable individuals, external agencies, and/or internal departments.

Design and develop newsletters, videos, brochures, web content, and other components of media campaigns for outreach activities to effectively meet program goals.

Maintain ongoing communication with internal and external stakeholders.

Public speaking and engagement appearances at events, tours, workshops, lunch and learns, trainings, and other outreach opportunities.

Participate in on-screen interviews with local media outlets.

Support additional City departments in relevant sustainability outreach, including but not limited to Parks & Outdoors, Stormwater, Community Development, and Solid Waste.

Incumbents typically work in an office setting, with field work associated with community events and technical assistance visits/meetings.

Must meet regular attendance requirements.

Must be able to maintain good interpersonal relationships with staff, co-workers, managers, and citizens.

Must accomplish the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodations, in a timely manner.

Performs other duties as assigned.

Evenings and occasional weekends may be required based on community opportunities.

DEPARTMENT SPECIFIC DUTIES (if any):
None

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Sustainability, Urban Planning, Communications, Public Relations, Marketing, Education, Public Policy, or a related field supplemented by five (5) years of experience in energy programs, community outreach, public education, sustainability, housing programs, or a related field; or any combination of equivalent experience and education.

LICENSING AND CERTIFICATIONS:
