title: Thermal-Hydraulics Engineer 3
description:
NOTE: THIS POSITION IS AVAILABLE FOR REMOTE WORK FOR INDIVIDUALS LIVING BEYOND A 30 MILE RADIUS OF A PHYSICAL NUSCALE OFFICE BUT WITHIN THE CONTIGUOUS UNITED STATES.

POSITION SUMMARY: The Thermal‑Hydraulics Engineer 3 is an experienced technical contributor within the Nuclear Methods group of the Nuclear Fuels organization. Reporting to the Manager, Nuclear Methods, the engineer works in close coordination with the Thermal Hydraulics, Nuclear Design, and Code Development groups, as well as partners across other Engineering disciplines, Licensing, and Operations. This position is an engineer with experience in nuclear thermal-hydraulic analyses, codes, and methods, as well as familiar with interfaces with core design, neutronics, and design basis event analysis. This role will apply industry best-practices and knowledge of state-of-the-art methods to support development, validation, and licensing of new methods in areas including thermal-hydraulics, coupled codes, and reload safety analysis. The role requires familiarity with PWR thermal‑hydraulic principles, design‑basis safety analysis, and interfaces with core design, fuel design, neutronics, and transient analysis.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Contribute to development and validation of next‑generation multi‑physics methods integrating subchannel TH, system TH, and neutronics.
  • Support method qualification efforts including benchmark selection, acceptance criteria definition, and comparison against experimental data or legacy reference analyses, with particular emphasis in areas of thermal-hydraulic expertise. Develop and review software QA documentation.
  • Prepare and verify subchannel analyses, including steady-state and transient margin evaluations and CHF predictions, in support of new method development.
  • Prepare and verify coupled TH evaluations, including LOCA, non‑LOCA transients, and design‑basis evaluations, in support of new method development using industry-standard and advanced simulation tools.
  • Work collaboratively within the Nuclear Fuels organization to ensure design and analysis interfaces are adequately managed, including with core design, fuel design, subchannel thermal-hydraulics, and transient analysis. Help develop workflows that improve consistency, automation, or integration across multi‑physics safety analyses.
  • Contribute to technical development of licensing technical or topical reports, license applications, and other licensing documentation, and participate in licensing interactions including interface with the government regulator in areas of technical responsibility.
  • Prepare and verify engineering reports, calculations, studies, system descriptions, requirement specifications, and other design documents with particular emphasis on subchannel and system thermal-hydraulics. Work on tasks in multiple and diverse areas.
  • Provide technical leadership within Thermal Hydraulics; mentor junior engineers and lead analysis tasks in areas of expertise.
  • Develop resolutions to complex problems that require the frequent use of creativity and innovation.
  • Perform other duties as assigned. Flexibly support changing organizational priorities, including urgent analysis needs, cross‑functional reviews, technical troubleshooting, or special studies.

CORE COMPETENCIES: To perform the job successfully, the individual should demonstrate competencies in performing the essential functions of this position by performing satisfactorily in each of these competencies.

  • Problem solving: Identifies and resolves problems in a timely manner, gathers and reviews information appropriately. Uses own judgment and acts independently; seeks input from other team members as appropriate for complex or sensitive situations.
  • Oral/written communication: Listens carefully and speaks clearly and professionally in all situations. Edits work for accuracy and clarity. Is able to create, read, and interpret complex written information. Ability to develop strong interpersonal networks within the organization.
  • Planning/organizing: Prioritizes and plans work activities, organizes personal and project timelines and deadlines, tracks project timelines and deadlines, and uses time efficiently.
  • Adaptability: Adapts to changes in the work environment, manages competing demands and is able to deal with frequent interruptions, changes, delays, or unexpected events.
  • Dependability: Consistently on time and at work, responds to management expectations and solicits feedback to improve performance.
  • Team Building: Capable of developing strong interpersonal networks and trust within the organization.
  • Safety Culture: Adheres to the NuScale Safety culture and is expected to model safe behavior and influence peers to meet high standards.
  • Quality Assurance: Commits to the understanding and implementation of quality assurance regulations, standards and guidelines of 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, 10 CFR 21, and NQA-1.

MINIMUM SKILLS, QUALIFICATIONS AND ABILITIES:

  • Education: A minimum of B.S. degree in Nuclear, Mechanical, or Chemical Engineering (or related discipline) from a four-year accredited college or university is required. An advanced degree in Nuclear, Mechanical, or Chemical Engineering is desirable.
  • Experience: A minimum of 5 years of full-time, directly relevant engineering experience is required. Experience in implementing engineering design processes for subchannel thermal-hydraulics, transient analysis, and related safety analysis is required. Experience in neutronics or fuel performance preferred.
  • Industry Requirements: Eligible to work under Department of Energy 10 CFR Part 810.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Ability to understand and communicate clearly using a phone, personal interaction, and computers.

  • Ability to travel nationally and locally using common forms of transportation.

title: Person In Charge (PIC)
description:
Position Purpose: Exemplifies and ensures strong customer service in all aspects of the job. Directs and controls the operation of the Front End in the absence of store management to achieve sales and profit objectives.

Job Description: As a primary contact for customers, the Person In Charge (PIC) provides friendly, courteous, and helpful service. During the absence of the Store Manager and the First & Second Assistant Managers, the PIC is in charge of the store, with analogous authority to make necessary decisions to operate the store at maximum profit, efficiency, and superior customer service. When in charge of the store (generally at night) the PIC will supervise the store employees. The PIC also acts as a Cashier-Checker (see job description). May be required to work in many of the departments within the store.

Key Responsibilities & Accountabilities:

  • Provide customer service as currently defined by the employer within the scope of the position and within company policy.

  • Responsible for appropriately handling emergencies, customer complaints, employee or customer accidents and supervising all store personnel.

  • Maintains high level of familiarity with company policies and procedures.

  • Supervises the sales floor to monitor service and replenishment of products.

  • Replaces stock in displays surrounding the checkout area.

  • Assists in maintaining a clean and safe work environment within the store.

  • Assists other cashiers with computer, register, and scanner problems.

  • Responsible for performing basic office functions to assist customers and personnel.

  • Operates electronically scanning cash register to total customers’ final bill.

  • Receive payment for customer purchase and count back correct change.

  • Bag groceries in paper, canvas, or plastic bags. Lift bags into grocery cart. Offer customer assistance with carry out, and perform that task if a Courtesy Clerk is not available.

title: Senior Director, Sourcing and Contracts
description:
Venture Global LNG (“Venture Global”) is a long-term, low-cost provider of American-produced liquefied natural gas. The company’s Louisiana-based export projects service the global demand for North American natural gas and support the long-term development of clean and reliable North American energy supplies. Using reliable, proven technology in an innovative plant design configuration, Venture Global’s modular, mid-scale plant design will replace traditional designs as it allows for the same efficiency and operational reliability at significantly lower capital cost.

We are seeking qualified applicants for the position:

Senior Director, Sourcing and Contracts

Located:

Arlington

Summary

We are seeking an experienced Director-level leader for our Corporate Sourcing and Contracting team. This individual is an integral member of the Business Management and Supply Chain team and will lead a team of Sourcing and Contracts Principals, Specialists and Analysts in performing daily sourcing, procurement and contracting activities supporting Venture Global’s Engineering, Information Technology and Corporate functional segments. The Director, Corporate Sourcing and Contracts will partner with the internal business leadership across, engineering, information technology, finance, human resources, business development, regulatory compliance and other corporate functional teams to ensure compliant sourcing, negotiation and execution of purchasing contracts for goods and services necessary for continued business operations.

  • Collect and coordinate all purchase and contracting requests and needs from business stakeholders across all corporate functions

  • Use knowledge of sources and suppliers across the industry to find approved alternative suppliers to fulfill the business needs
  • Address supplier shortages, defects and gaps in fulfilment
  • Participate in regular business management, budget and strategic planning sessions
  • Support the execution of Supplier Performance Management program execution,
  • Maintain purchase requests, supplier proposals, purchasing record and contracts, supplier feedback documentation as required per policy
  • Conduct employee performance management including goals setting, performance assessment and feedback, coaching, mentoring and training as required
  • Perform other duties assigned

Qualifications

Required experience

  • 10 - 15 years or more in a similar Sourcing, Contracting, Procurement or Supply Chain leadership role involving Engineering, Information Technology, and/or corporate functional areas
  • Able to effectively lead a team of 5 to 10 direct reports
  • Excellent knowledge of sourcing, contracting, procurement and delivery processes
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to simplify complex concepts and present key details and conclusions
  • Proficient with MS OfficeSuite
  • Interest in and comfort with being a part of a team environment with rapidly changing assignments and priorities
  • Demonstrated initiative and ownership of work with strong attention to detail

title: People and Culture Supervisor
description:
About Four Seasons:

Four Seasons is powered by our people. We are a collective of individuals who crave to become better, to push ourselves to new heights and to treat each other as we wish to be treated in return. Our team members around the world create amazing experiences for our guests, residents, and partners through a commitment to luxury with genuine heart. We know that the best way to enable our people to deliver these exceptional guest experiences is through a world-class employee experience and company culture.

At Four Seasons, we believe in recognizing a familiar face, welcoming a new one and treating everyone we meet the way we would want to be treated ourselves. Whether you work with us, stay with us, live with us or discover with us, we believe our purpose is to create impressions that will stay with you for a lifetime. It comes from our belief that life is richer when we truly connect to the people and the world around us.

About the location:

Four Seasons Resort and Residences Dominican Republic at Tropicalia will feature 95 keys and 25 branded residential homes, 8 distinct F&B outlets, all thoughtfully designed to reflect a contemporary interpretation of the Dominican Republic’s natural beauty. Wellness will be a defining pillar of the property, delivering a holistic experience that harmonizes with the natural environment while enhancing overall wellbeing through the restorative power of nature. The sustainable luxury destination is located on a 60-acre (24 hectare) site along the pristine beachfront of Playa Esmeralda in northeastern Dominican Republic, along the southern shores of Samaná Bay. A site of breathtaking natural beauty, Tropicalia is home to a diverse ecosystem of white-sand beaches; crystalline, aquamarine water and coral reefs; mountains, forests, mangroves, lagoons and rivers; a working coconut plantation; and an organic farm.

About the Role

Four Seasons Resort and Residences Dominican Republic at Tropicalia is seeking a People and Culture Supervisor to join our pre-opening team. Reporting to the People and Culture leadership team, this position will support the effective daily operation of the department across employee services, onboarding, HR administration, benefits, employee relations and regulatory compliance, while creating a welcoming and caring experience for employees and candidates.

What You Will Do

  • Serve as a primary point of contact for employees and candidates, responding to questions and requests in a warm, timely, confidential and professional manner.
  • Support the complete employee lifecycle, including pre-employment documentation, onboarding, employee changes, leave administration, transfers and separations.
  • Prepare employment contracts, letters, certifications and other People and Culture documentation, ensuring accuracy and compliance with company standards and Dominican labor requirements.
  • Maintain complete and confidential employee records in Workday and applicable local systems, ensuring that personnel files and employment information remain accurate and current.
  • Coordinate new-hire documentation and onboarding activities, including document collection, orientation schedules, uniform requirements and departmental follow-up.
  • Support benefits enrollment and administration, including medical insurance, employee meals, uniforms and other property benefits.
  • Assist with employee relations matters by listening to employee concerns, documenting cases appropriately and escalating sensitive matters to People and Culture leadership.
  • Coordinate with Finance and Payroll to ensure the timely and accurate processing of new hires, employee changes, leave, deductions and separations.
  • Prepare and maintain People and Culture reports, including headcount, turnover, attendance, leave balances, staffing updates and other workforce information.
  • Support employee communication, engagement activities, recognition programs and wellbeing initiatives.
  • Assist with compliance processes involving the Ministry of Labor, Social Security Treasury and other applicable government entities.
  • Support recruitment and pre-opening hiring activities as needed, including interview coordination, reference checks, offer preparation and candidate communication.
  • Guide and support People and Culture Coordinators or other assigned team members in completing daily departmental priorities.
  • Protect confidential employee and business information and consistently apply Four Seasons policies, standards and the Golden Rule.

What You Bring

  • University degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Psychology, Hospitality Management or a related field.
  • A minimum of three years of progressive Human Resources or People and Culture experience, preferably within hospitality or a service-oriented organization. Previous supervisory experience is preferred.
  • Working knowledge of Dominican labor legislation, social security requirements and local employment practices.
  • Strong organizational, interpersonal and problem-solving skills, with sound judgment and the ability to handle confidential information.
  • Fluency in Spanish and strong working proficiency in English. Experience with Workday or another HR information system is preferred.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and a comprehensive benefits package.
  • Excellent training and professional-development opportunities.
  • Opportunities for career growth within Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts.
  • Employee travel program, including complimentary and discounted stays at Four Seasons properties worldwide, subject to program eligibility.
  • Complimentary dry cleaning for employee uniforms.
  • Complimentary employee meals while on duty.
  • A supportive and inclusive work environment built on mutual respect, collaboration and the Golden Rule.

Schedule & Hours

  • This is a full-time position.
  • The primary schedule will be during regular business hours; however, flexibility to work early mornings, evenings, weekends or public holidays may be required based on recruitment activities, orientations, employee events and operational needs.

Work Authorization

Candidates must be legally eligible to work in the Dominican Republic.

Four Seasons Resort and Residences Dominican Republic at Tropicalia is committed to providing an inclusive workplace in which all individuals are treated with dignity and respect. title: Senior Platform Engineer
description:
Ready for a challenge?

Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience.

Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe.

About this role

You’ll be working within our Intelligence Platform Core team, responsible for underlying platform infrastructure across our new Data & ML Platforms within JET. Within the past year we’ve built new Data & ML Platforms on AWS and the Intelligence Platform Core team sits at the heart of both of them, creating self service experiences for running data and ML workflows without exposing the underlying complexity of Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure. We aim to provide a scalable, reliable and seamless platform experience for our users.

You’ll be the second full time engineer within this team, joining with the opportunity to shape our Platform vision and team culture as we grow and expand. The platform team also works closely with our Data and ML Platform teams on an advisory basis, providing best practises and advice where needed.

* Please note that this position is located in Bristol (3 days a week from our Bristol office and 2 days working from home)

These are some of the key components to the position:

You will contribute to both the design and implementation of the platform:

  • Collaborate on the design and implementation of platform capabilities using Kubernetes-native patterns and event-driven architectures.
  • Drive the adoption of platform engineering principles, building reusable abstractions and self-service workflows for internal users.
  • Design and implement Kubernetes controllers/operators in Go to automate infrastructure and application lifecycle management.
  • Mentor engineers and contribute to growing platform engineering practices across our pillar in the Data and ML Platform teams.
  • Collaborate across teams to align on platform interfaces, abstractions, and shared infrastructure patterns.
  • Support the hiring of new engineers as we expand the team, setting the bar on quality of code and collaboration.


What will you bring to the team?

  • You have strong experience building cloud-native platforms on AWS, GCP, or Azure, with a deep understanding and hands on experience of Kubernetes.
  • You are proficient in Go, particularly for building backend services, CLIs, or Kubernetes controllers/operators.
  • You are experienced with GitOps and CI/CD systems, and understand how to build reliable, automated delivery pipelines.
  • You understand distributed systems and have experience designing scalable, resilient architectures.
  • You have experience building self-service platforms or internal developer platforms (IDPs).
  • You care deeply about developer experience, usability, and reducing cognitive load through good abstractions.
  • You communicate clearly and enjoy collaborating across teams to drive platform adoption.

Nice to have…

  • Experience with data technologies and processes, such as streaming and batch processes and large data storage systems.

At JET, this is how we play

Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment.

Being the best at what we do isn’t just about delivering on our strategy. It's a competition for something incredibly valuable – our customers' choice. Every time a customer decides where to order, they're picking a side.

At the heart of the JET Customer League are our values and behaviours. They guide every interaction, every decision, every innovation. These are the actions we need to perform consistently and brilliantly, to surpass the competition and earn our customers’ loyalty, again and again.

Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition.

Inclusion, Diversity & Belonging

No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day.

What else are we delivering?

Want to know more about our JETers, culture or company? Have a look at our career site where you can find people's stories, blogs, podcasts and more JET journeys.

Are you ready to join the team? Apply now!

title: Analyst

Responsibilities:

- Accurate and timely assistance with the basic data and preliminary tasks to support the research and analysis of CMBS properties.

- Accurate and timely retrieval, analysis, research, and reporting of CMBS pool-level and property-level performance, including:

  • Identifying and analyzing risky assets based upon qualitative and quantitative factors.
  • Identifying macro and micro risk factors, including market, property type, tenant, and borrower, to determine and measure exposure within the CMBS pools and loan portfolios.
  • Monitoring, analysis, and executive summary reporting on CMBS transactions, including an investigation of potential default or loss scenarios for underlying real estate loan collateral.
  • Productive and timely communication and support other Morningstar Analysts or any third-party contacts to collect data and information to produce quality and timely reporting within prescribed time frames.
  • Research and respond to internal and external inquiries regarding specific aspects of assigned CMBS pools, providing users with information on major credits or portfolio concentrations; and evaluating such detail relative to bond class holdings to ascertain strengths and/or weaknesses of a position.

Requirements:

  • 1-3 years’ relevant experience in the credit research domain, with working knowledge of CMBS transactions. Credit ratings experience preferred
  • Master’s degree, CFA, or FRM preferred.
  • Intermediate-level Excel skills
  • Strong English-language skills, particularly writing.

About Us

Morningstar DBRS is a leading provider of independent rating services and opinions for corporate and sovereign entities, financial institutions, and project and structured finance instruments globally. Rating more than 4,000 issuers and 60,000 securities, it is one of the top four credit rating agencies in the world.

Morningstar DBRS empowers investor success by bringing more transparency and a much-needed diversity of opinion in the credit rating industry. Our approach and size allow us to be nimble enough to respond to customers' needs in their local markets, but large enough to provide the necessary expertise and resources they require. Market innovators choose to work with us because of our agility, tech-forward approach, and exceptional customer service.

Morningstar DBRS is the next generation of credit ratings.

If you receive and accept an offer from us, we require that personal and any related investments be disclosed confidentiality to our Compliance team (days vary by region). Morningstar's hybrid work environment gives you the opportunity to collaborate in-person each week as we've found that we're at our best when we're purposely together on a regular basis. description:

title: Sr Principal Technical Program Manager - Cybersecurity (Hybrid - Seattle)
description:
Job Description

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager, Principal Sr. to lead the delivery of Nordstrom’s highest-impact cybersecurity programs — initiatives that protect the company’s customers, data, and operations across every technology and business function.

This senior-most individual contributor role sits within the CISO’s organization, at the intersection of security engineering, governance risk and compliance (GRC), and enterprise technology delivery. You will drive the programs that reduce Nordstrom’s risk posture at scale — partnering with security, platform, and business teams to plan, sequence, and execute complex, cross-functional security initiatives from charter through measurable outcome.

This is not a role for managing programs at arm’s length. It is a role for someone who translates security strategy into executable delivery plans, manages risk and dependencies across a portfolio of concurrent programs, holds partners accountable to commitments, and reports progress with rigor to senior leadership. You will operate with SVP/VP-level visibility and represent program delivery excellence for Nordstrom’s cybersecurity organization.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Program Strategy & Portfolio Leadership

  • Own end-to-end delivery for a portfolio of enterprise cybersecurity programs (e.g., identity and access management, cloud security, data protection, incident response, vulnerability management, third-party risk) spanning multiple teams and technology domains.
  • Translate security strategy and executive priorities into structured program charters, roadmaps, and delivery plans with clear scope, milestones, and success criteria.
  • Sequence and prioritize competing initiatives across the security portfolio based on risk reduction, business impact, and resource constraints.
  • Partner with the CISO’s leadership team to shape investment priorities and build/partner/buy decisions for major security initiatives.

Program Governance & Risk Management

  • Establish and run program governance — steering committees, checkpoints, and decision forums — that keep security programs on track and escalate issues before they become blockers.
  • Identify, track, and drive resolution of program risks, issues, and dependencies across security, engineering, legal, and business stakeholders.
  • Ensure programs comply with relevant regulatory, audit, and internal control requirements, partnering with GRC and compliance teams as needed.
  • Define and enforce delivery standards and program management best practices across the cybersecurity organization.

Cross-Functional Delivery & Stakeholder Alignment

  • Build and lead cross-functional program teams spanning security engineering, IT, platform, legal, privacy, and business units to execute enterprise-wide security initiatives.
  • Drive alignment among stakeholders with competing priorities, resolving conflicts and unblocking delivery through structured negotiation and clear articulation of tradeoffs.

Job Title: Accessioner

Department: Accessioning

Location: Onsite, 200 Precision Road, Horsham, PA

SUMMARY

The Accessioner is responsible for preparing specimens prior to laboratory analysis and testing. Accessioners are key to our laboratory operations as they handle each specimen and ensures accurate accessioning before they move to the laboratory. Each of our specimens represent one of our valuable patients.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Performs data entry of specimen demographic information

  • Perform all other duties as assigned by leadership

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • None

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience handling various specimen types including blood, oral fluid, urine and viral swabs in viral media or saline preferred.

  • Experience in customer service, data/order entry, and working in a process driven environment preferred.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Moderate - These roles require a combination of movement and stationary work, including frequent standing, walking, and moderate lifting (up to 50 lbs.). Tasks may involve repetitive reaching, bending, pushing, or pulling, along with maintaining awareness in high-traffic or operational areas. Visual focus and spatial awareness are critical in facilities, logistics, or support settings. Emotional demands include managing interruptions, prioritizing tasks, and maintaining compliance with safety standards. Environmental exposures may include equipment noise, shared workspaces, and occasional proximity to hazardous areas. Physical capability screening may be required.

description:
Position Summary:

The Family Retention Specialist is responsible for proactively supporting families who may be at risk of disenrollment due to concerns, transitions, or other service-related challenges. This role serves as a dedicated point of contact to understand family concerns, identify root causes, and coordinate appropriate resolution options in partnership with school and field leaders. The position helps ensure family outreach, case follow-up, and documentation are completed in a timely, consistent, and family-focused manner. Through high-touch support and insight sharing, this role contributes to stronger family relationships, improved retention, and continued process improvement.

Key Responsibilities:

  1. Serve as the primary point of contact for families identified as at risk due to teacher departures, classroom transitions, incident reports, engagement changes, or other known trigger events.
  2. Conduct proactive outreach within established timelines to understand concerns, provide support, and address issues before they lead to disenrollment.
  3. Lead conversations with families who submit disenrollment requests to identify root concerns, present appropriate resolution options, and support retention when possible.
  4. Partner with school directors and field leaders to understand school-level context, coordinate follow-up, and maintain effective feedback loops.
  5. Document family interactions, concerns, actions, outcomes, and resolutions accurately and consistently in the designated case management system.
  6. Identify recurring family concerns and share insights that support service improvements, family engagement, and retention strategies.
  7. Contribute to the design and refinement of outreach scripts, communication cadence, and case management processes as the program evolves.
  8. Represent Learning Care’s mission and values in every interaction and provide a high-touch, family-focused experience.
  9. Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

  1. A bachelor's degree in social work, early childhood education, communications, business, human services, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience, is required.
  2. 3-5 years of experience in customer service, family support, social services, conflict resolution, retention, sales, or a related role is required.
  3. Experience independently managing sensitive or escalated customer or family concerns is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Experience in childcare, early childhood education, family services, enrollment, retention, or a related service environment is preferred.
  2. Experience supporting families through escalated concerns, transitions, or service recovery is preferred.
  3. Experience with case management or customer relationship management systems is preferred.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

title: HPC Systems Administrator
description:

If you’re an engineer, scientist, or builder who thrives on problems no one has solved before, this is your invitation; we want you on the team. About the Lilly and NVIDIA Partnership

The lab brings Lilly scientists, technologists, chemists and biologists together with NVIDIA engineers under one roof. title: Software Development Engineer (Machine Learning)
description:
FortiAIGate is Fortinet's AI security and governance gateway. It sits inline between enterprise users, AI agents, and LLM providers, inspecting prompts and responses in real time to detect prompt injection, jailbreaks, sensitive data exposure, and policy violations — under a strict latency budget.

We are hiring a Machine Learning Engineer to own the detection models behind that product: training, evaluation, optimization, and the serving stack that runs them in production.

Responsibilities

  • Build and train guardrail models. Develop classifiers that detect prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, unsafe content, and sensitive data exposure across prompts, responses, and tool-call payloads — dataset construction through to release.
  • Design and tune the tiered detection cascade. Balance a low-cost first-stage screen against a higher-fidelity semantic stage, tuning thresholds to hit accuracy targets inside a fixed per-request latency budget.
  • Work across encoder and decoder model families. Fine-tune encoder-based classifiers and token-level taggers for detection and extraction; adapt small decoder models for semantic judgment. Use distillation to move capability into models small enough to deploy.
  • Optimize and serve models inline. Quantize, distill, and compile models (ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, INT8/FP8) for GPU appliances. Deploy and tune them on Triton Inference Server and vLLM — batching, concurrent model execution, KV-cache and memory configuration, multi-stage pipelines — and profile out the bottlenecks.
  • Harden models against evasion. Threat research on obfuscation and encoding bypass, dilution attacks, indirect injection, and multi-turn attacks visible only across conversational context. Turn each new bypass into training data and a regression test.
  • Own evaluation and governance detectors. Build benchmark and suites measuring detection rate at production-realistic false positive rates; monitor deployed models for drift. Maintain detection models for personal and regulated data and for natural-language policy, including multilingual coverage.

Required Qualifications

  • Strong Python and production PyTorch experience; comfort with Go/Rust/C/C++ for performance-critical paths is valuable.
  • Demonstrated experience training, fine-tuning, and evaluating transformer models — encoder classifiers, decoder language models, or both — with Hugging Face Transformers or equivalent.
  • Production experience with a modern inference serving system (Triton, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, TGI), including the batching and memory tuning real throughput requires.
  • Practical model optimization: quantization, distillation, pruning, or graph compilation, with a record of holding accuracy while cutting latency or memory.
  • Sound evaluation instincts — able to design test sets that reflect deployment reality and reason about precision/recall where false positives block legitimate user traffic.
  • Working knowledge of tokenization, text normalization, and Unicode handling, and how these become an attack surface in a security product.
  • Familiarity with containerized deployment (Docker, Kubernetes) and standard MLOps practice: experiment tracking, model versioning, reproducible training pipelines.
  • Ability to deliver on schedule in an Agile environment and communicate effectively across technical and non-technical teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Modeling experience in a security or abuse-detection domain, where adversaries adapt to your defenses.
  • Familiarity with the LLM threat landscape — prompt injection, indirect injection, exfiltration through model output — and with the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.
  • Gradient-boosted tree models (LightGBM, XGBoost) and hybrid classical/neural architectures.
  • NER, PII detection, or data classification models, particularly multilingual.
  • CUDA familiarity, GPU profiling, or deploying models under fixed hardware and memory constraints.
  • Synthetic data generation, active learning, or human-in-the-loop labeling where labeled data is scarce.
  • Publications, open-source work, or CTF/red-team experience in adversarial ML or LLM security.

Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship.

The US base salary range for this full-time position is $150,000-$183,000. Fortinet offers employees a variety of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, 401(k), 11 paid holidays, vacation time, and sick time, as well as a comprehensive leave program.

Wage ranges are based on various factors, including the labour market, job type, and job level. Exact salary offers will be determined by factors such as the candidate's subject knowledge, skill level, qualifications, experience, and geographic location.

All roles are eligible to participate in the Fortinet equity program. Bonus eligibility is reviewed at the time of hire and annually at the Company’s discretion.


Why Join Us:

We encourage candidates from all backgrounds and identities to apply. We offer a supportive work environment and a competitive Total Rewards package to support you with your overall health and financial well-being.

Embark on a challenging, enjoyable, and rewarding career journey with Fortinet. Join us in bringing solutions that make a meaningful and lasting impact to our 890,000+ customers around the globe.

title: Ammunition Inspector (ASP), McGregor Range, NM
description:
Technica LLC seeks to fill an Ammunition Inspector (ASP) position to perform on a Government contract with a place of performance at McGregor Range, NM.

Position Responsibilities:

This position performs limited aspects of supply management work as it pertains to ammunition to include but, not limited to, inventory management, storage management, cataloging, property utilization, and inspections related to ammunition supply point activities. Work usually is segregated by commodity area or function, and controlled in terms of difficulty, complexity, or responsibility. Assignments usually relate to stable or standardized segments of technical supply management and ammunition surveillance operations; or to functions or subjects that are narrow in scope or limited in difficulty.

Basic Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Orders, receives, stores, maintains and issues supplies and equipment to support the daily operations.
  • Assists in ammunition accountability records.
  • Determines condition codes of Ammunition and Explosives.
  • Arranges the demilitarization of unserviceable ammunition.
  • Operates the MHP (Munitions History Program).
  • Assists in resolving inventory and/or system problems (Causative Research).
  • Generates magazine storage reports as directed or required.
  • Performance of a variety of routine and special inspections of conventional, unconventional, and foreign ammunition using a wide range of inspection processes and techniques in support of Stockpile Assessment as well as shipping and receiving operations.
  • Assists Quality Assurance Specialist (Ammunition Surveillance) in performing inspection work at all conventional ammunition workstations on wide variety of surveillance operations. This includes receipt, storage, renovation, modification, demilitarization, destruction and shipment of conventional/ nonconventional munitions.
  • Perform DD Form 626 motor vehicle inspections for vehicles transporting hazardous materials and surveillance of unit ammunition turn-ins.
  • Performs other duties as required. (This list is not all inclusive)

Basic Requirements:

  • High school diploma or equivalent is required.
  • Previous Military experience as MOS 89A, 55B, 89B, or 89D, (Army), 2W0X1 (Air Force), MOS A420 (Navy) or 2311 (Marine Corps).
  • Must complete Ammo 45, 67, 68, and 108 within 30 days of receiving CAC (Common Access Card).
  • Must complete Ammo 62 (Technical Transportation of Hazardous Materials) within first year of assignment.
  • 3 years' experience working in ammunition inventory and accountability is required.
  • Driver's license required.
  • US Citizen
  • 18 years of age
  • Must be able to pass pre-employment and background checks related to the position
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a Secret Security Clearance.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Must have a solid background experience and working knowledge performing in the Standard Army Ammunition Systems (SAAS) system
  • Must be knowledgeable and have ability to operate MHP.
  • Must be able to work independently with little or no supervision.
  • Must have high-level of organizational and planning skills.
  • Must have excellent communications skills, both oral and written.
  • Demonstrated skill with all MS software to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Must demonstrate a strong work ethic to accomplish work effectively and economically.
  • Must be competent in DA Pam 385-64, DA Pam 742-1, AR 190-11, and MIL-STD-129R.

Physical and Mental Requirements: (to be performed with or without accommodation)

  • Must be able to lift up to 49 LBS.
  • Must be able to work in all types of weather conditions to include intense heat, heavy wind, blowing sand, heavy rain, and snow and sleet
  • Must possess a forklift license or receive within the first 90 days of assignment.

title: Client Services Coordinator Intern Part-Time (Public Defender Dept.)
description:

The Client Services Coordinator (CSC) part-time intern in the Public Defender’s Office works directly with the Chief Public Defender, 1st Assistant Public Defender, Assistant Public Defenders, Client Services Coordinators, and management staff by performing administrative duties. Work involves walking, talking, hearing, using hands to handle or feel objects, tools, or controls, and reaching with hands and arms. Vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus. Physical lifting of multiple files and file boxes as necessary. The maximum weight of boxes is 15 pounds, which is usually required approximately once per week.

Work is performed in a standard cubicle, individual office, and courtroom environment. The position may require working in moderately noisy to loud environments, including cubicles and communal workspaces, and participating in frequent collaborative team meetings. The work environment may be fast-paced and include frequent interruptions, changing priorities, and interactions with employees, the public, and other stakeholders.

title: Doorways Coordinator
description:
Number of Positions Available:

1

ABOUT US

The Salvation Army is a Christian movement and one of Australia's largest and most-loved charities. We believe in doing good that transforms lives and futures for the better. It is this belief which drives us to find new ways and places where we can make a difference. From times of personal crisis to moments of national grief, we are always here — providing support, safety, community, and opportunity.

Doorways Coordinator

Karratha, WA

Full-time permanent

SCHADS Level 5 plus 9% regional allowance uplift

Why this role matters

The Doorways Coordinator plays a deeply meaningful role in supporting individuals and families across Karratha. Every day you will welcome people with dignity, listen with compassion and help them find pathways that strengthen their wellbeing. This is a role where your leadership directly shapes the experience of community members who walk through the door. You will guide a small team of employees and volunteers who care deeply about making a difference and you will help create a safe, calm and supportive environment for people seeking help. Your work will bring TSA’s values of integrity, respect, diversity, compassion and collaboration to life in a community that truly benefits from strong local support.

About the role

As the Doorways Coordinator, you will oversee the delivery of Doorways services across the Karratha site. You will lead and support a dedicated team of employees and volunteers, ensuring services are delivered with warmth, professionalism and in line with the Doorways Model of Care.

You will build strong relationships with Corps Officers, TSA services and local community partners to understand local needs and strengthen collaboration. You will ensure business processes, reporting, WHS requirements and administrative systems are completed accurately and on time. You may also deliver some case work to support community members to identify goals and access appropriate pathways.

This permanent full-time position within the Community Engagement team, reporting to the Regional Manager. Pay is in accordance with a SCHADS Level 5 plus a 9% regional allowance uplift.

How you will make an impact

  • Coordinate the delivery of emergency relief and material aid services that provide immediate and practical support to people in need.

  • Lead and support a team of employees and volunteers to deliver safe, compassionate and person-centred services.

  • Ensure the site is welcoming, calm and adequately always staffed.

  • Build strong relationships with local Corps, TSA services and community stakeholders to strengthen collaboration and identify opportunities for community support.

  • Coach and guide case workers on complex cases and support best practice service delivery.

  • Maintain accurate client records and data in accordance with TSA standards using SAMIS.

  • Contribute to resolving client concerns and reduce high conflict situations through effective de-escalation and communication skills.

  • Support continuous improvement and best practice in partnership with the Regional Manager.

What you will bring

  • Minimum Diploma or preferred Degree in Social Work, Psychology or a Community or Human Services discipline, along with extensive community sector experience and high-level knowledge and skills.

  • Experience in managing teams within community services and a genuine passion for supporting people.

  • Strong skills in conflict resolution and supporting individuals experiencing trauma or complex needs.

  • Excellent communication, relationship building and collaboration skills.

  • Confidence in managing administrative processes and ensuring compliance with practice standards.

  • A calm, steady and compassionate approach that helps people feel safe and supported.

  • WA Working with Children check or willingness to obtain

  • WA Driving Licence

What We Offer

  • Remote Area Housing Benefit for employees living and working in Karratha (up to $31,800 tax free) and Entertainment Benefit ($2,650 tax free)

  • Flexible working arrangements

  • SCHADS Level 5 – Above Award conditions (9% remote allowance applied to base rate)

  • Employee Assistance Program – confidential counselling service

  • Financial, retail and lifestyle discounts

  • Discounted health and fitness programs through Fitness Passport

  • Up to 8 weeks of leave per year through our purchase leave scheme

  • Generous parental leave (12 weeks)

  • Up to 5 days paid leave per year to support a TSA program or activity

  • A supportive, inclusive culture with passionate and dedicated team members

  • The opportunity to make a meaningful difference in a regional community

How to apply

Please submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your experience and interest in the role.

Applications will close as soon as a suitable candidate is secured.

The Salvation Army is an Equal Opportunity Employer who provides an inclusive work environment and embraces the diverse talent of its people. We value people of all cultures, languages, capacities, sexual orientations, gender identities and/or expressions. We are committed to achieving a diverse workforce and strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal people and Torres Strait Islander people.

The Salvation Army is a child safe organisation and is committed to protecting children and young people from harm. All child facing roles will require the successful completion of a Working with Children Check. Applicants for all roles require a mandatory Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check.

We value Integrity, Compassion, Respect, Diversity, and Collaboration

title: Night Shift Environmental Monitoring Technician
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world. Position Overview:

Provide support for Parenteral Operations by performing environmental monitoring of the classified manufacturing areas and by performing utility sampling and analysis within the manufacturing site. Assist QC- Microbiology management with training. Provide support in the manufacturing areas during routine environmental monitoring and utility sampling.

Responsibilities:
Adhere to and promote compliance with all cGMP procedures, Quality Systems, Good Documentation Practices, and Good Laboratory Practices. Provide support for Parenteral Operations activities by performing environmental monitoring of classified manufacturing areas. Provide support for manufacturing and laboratory activities by performing utility sampling and analysis. Provide support with routine lab maintenance and lab inventory management. Assist with technical training and mentoring of QC-Microbiology Technicians through formal process/program. Open to flexible work environment. Participate in department/company continuous improvement projects and initiatives. Assist with authoring Standard Operating Procedures and Work Instruction documentation. Adhere to and promote compliance of all safety standards.

Basic Requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Microbiology or related field; Associates degree or High School Diploma or equivalent 2+ years demonstrated relevant experience in performing Environmental Monitoring in a GMP Pharmaceutical Manufacturing facility, preferably associated with aseptic production.

The number of years of experience can vary based on educational qualifications. Demonstrated ability in performing environmental monitoring techniques including, but not limited to viable surface monitoring, viable and non-viable air monitoring, compressed air monitoring, and water and clean steam collection and analysis.

Experience with cGMP requirements and regulatory compliance associated with a cGMP Manufacturing facility.

Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1

Additional Skills/Preferences:
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to train/mentor QC Environmental Monitoring Technicians. description:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. Key Responsibilities

  • Lead RSCR Operations activities supporting Reference Standards and Critical Reagents inventory management, equipment and storage operations, material lifecycle oversight, and global distribution logistics.

title: Senior Cyber Strategist
description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation's space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space — delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you'll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

The Information Systems and Cyber Division (ISCD) is a unique engineering division partnering across the full space enterprise to advance next-generation digital solutions and software-enabled mission capabilities. With customers spanning the DoD, Intelligence Community (IC), civil and commercial space, ISCD blends expertise in software architecture, AI/ML systems, data fabric/architecture, advanced cloud and edge platforms, cybersecurity, and full-stack engineering through mission-focused, collaborative, multi-disciplinary teams. These collaborative teams leverage hands-on prototyping and applied R&D to support customer concepts, software architecture and development, and integration of the latest digital technology solutions. By bringing multi-disciplinary technical insight to critical space missions, ISCD is positioned at the forefront of innovative software and technology for excited new ways to make real-world impact.

Aerospace’s Cyberspace Systems & Security Subdivision (CS3) is seeking a Senior Cyber Strategist to shape the future of cybersecurity for space systems. This role combines strategic planning, product line development, technical leadership, and stakeholder engagement to drive cybersecurity innovation across Aerospace and the broader space enterprise. You will work closely with key stakeholders including government agencies, program offices, prime contractors, commercial vendors, and internal teams to develop comprehensive cybersecurity strategies, identify emerging opportunities, and translate strategic vision into actionable technical solutions and organizational capabilities.

This is a fulltime position 4-5 days/week onsite in El Segundo, CA.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Identify and develop new product lines at the intersection of AI and cybersecurity, translating emerging technology trends into actionable capabilities
  • Build and maintain strategic relationships with government customers, DoD and IC program offices, industry partners, and research institutions.
  • Track and pursue new opportunities based on governmental policy changes and evolution of technology, with particular focus on Cyber + AI convergence.
  • Lead business development activities that align technical capabilities with customer mission needs.
  • Communicate complex technical concepts and strategic vision to diverse audiences including government program offices and executive leadership.
  • Drive next actions for CS3 internal product lines, as well as other community engagement activities to advance cyber security across the space enterprise.
  • Partner with national laboratories, research institutions, and industry partners to transition emerging security technologies and research outcomes into operational capabilities.

What You Need to be Successful

Minimum Requirements for the Senior Project Leader - Cyber Security Architecture and Information Systems Security

  • Bachelor's degree in STEM, National Security, or Information Security/Technology, Cybersecurity, or related technical subject area.
  • 12 plus years of relevant experience in a position related to cyber security
  • Demonstrated ability to develop strategic plans, roadmaps, and organizational strategies that align technical capabilities with mission objectives
  • Strong customer engagement and business development skills with ability to communicate complex technical concepts to diverse audiences including government program offices and executive leadership
  • Ability to identify market gaps and technology trends, building strategies to position capabilities ahead of emerging mission needs.
  • Experience leading strategic initiatives and developing new product lines in cybersecurity, AI, or related technology domains.
  • Willing to travel occasionally to work location or customer site approx. 20% of the time if required
  • This position requires ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

  • Advanced degree in STEM or related discipline
  • Prior experience within a business strategy or corporate development team, ideally within a fast-paced environment focused on innovative technologies.
  • Current and active TS/SCI clearance

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. Individual salaries within that range are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge and skills.

(Min - Max)

$171,400.00 - $257,100.00

Leadership Competencies

Our leadership philosophy is simple: every employee, regardless of level and role, can demonstrate leadership. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who:

  • Operate Strategically
  • Lead Change
  • Engage with Impact
  • Foster Innovation
  • Deliver Results

Ways We Reward Our Employees

During your interview process, our team will provide details of our industry-leading benefits.

Benefits vary and are applicable based on Job Type. A few highlights include:

  • Comprehensive health care and wellness plans

title: Business Solutions Associate
description:
Born in exuberant, ebullient Saint Germain, Paris, in 1961, Diptyque is a creator of evocative perfumes for the self and the home, scented skincare products and desirable decorative objects. Striking a balance between reverie, nature and art, Diptyque extends an invitation to step inside a universe replete with creations that set the imagination free to wander.

Business Solutions Associate

Diptyque – Luxury Fragrance House has established itself as one of the most renowned, leading fragrance houses within the luxury market today. Founded in 1961, the Maison is known for its mix of iconic scented candles, personal fragrances, bath and body products, and home décor. Its flagship boutique is in Paris’ 5th arrondissement at 34 Boulevard Saint Germain.

The Business Solutions Associate supports the Business Solutions team in delivering, maintaining, and improving critical business applications across retail, e-commerce, finance, and supply chain operations.

Reporting to the Business Solutions Manager, this role focuses on execution, coordination, and operational support across systems such as ERP, POS, EDI, and related integrations. The Associate plays a key role in ensuring system stability, supporting users, and driving continuous improvement initiatives.

The current job description may not fully capture the scope and expectations of the role, which may include additional responsibilities as assigned.

Key Accountabilities and Responsibilities

Business Applications Support & Operations

  • Provide day-to-day support across core business applications (ERP, POS, EDI, and other integrated systems)
  • Act as first-level business support when issues are not covered by external partners
  • Track, triage, and follow up on tickets with external vendors and internal stakeholders
  • Communicate effectively with users regarding issue status, resolution timelines, and workaround

Examples:

  • Inventory period closing support, reconciliation activities, and operational adjustments
  • POS user management and troubleshooting reporting discrepancies
  • Monitoring invoice or transaction status across financial systems

Incident Management & Vendor Coordination

  • Coordinate issue resolution with external partners (e.g., ERP, POS, EDI vendors)
  • Escalate critical issues to the Business Solutions Manager when required
  • Ensure timely follow-up and accountability from vendors
  • Maintain clear documentation of recurring issues and resolutions

Continuous Improvement & Enhancements

  • Support small to medium initiatives and system enhancements
  • Perform testing, validation, and coordination for system updates and improvements
  • Investigate recurring issues and propose improvement actions
  • Contribute to process optimization and system efficiency

Examples:

  • NAV improvements (fields, dimensions, workflows)
  • Reporting enhancements and process automation
  • Ongoing improvements in warehouse or retail processes

Solution Coordination (ERP/POS/EDI/Interfaces)

  • Assist in maintaining and improving core business systems:
    • ERP (NAV and integrations with WMS)
    • POS systems
    • EDI and data exchange flows
  • Coordinate enhancements, testing, and documentation activities
  • Support master data updates (customers, vendors, items)
  • Ensure alignment between systems and business processes

Interface Monitoring & Data Integrity

  • Monitor system interfaces and data flows
  • Identify anomalies, investigate root causes, and coordinate resolution
  • Ensure data accuracy across systems and support reconciliation efforts
  • Contribute to maintaining monitoring tools and reporting

Project Support

  • Support the Business Solutions Manager in project execution and delivery
  • Coordinate tasks, track progress, and assist with documentation
  • Participate in testing cycles (UAT), deployments, and business rollouts

Requirements and Qualifications

Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Business Administration, Finance, or related fields
  • 2–5 years of experience in business systems, IT applications, or functional support roles
  • Experience in retail, e-commerce, or supply chain environments is a plus

Technical & Functional Skills

  • Familiarity with ERP systems (e.g., Microsoft Dynamics NAV or similar)
  • Understanding of POS, EDI, or system integrations is a plus
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities in parallel

Soft Skills

  • Strong communication skills with both technical and business stakeholders
  • Structured, detail-oriented, and proactive approach
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, multi-vendor environment
  • Ownership mindset with strong follow-through

Key Success Factors

  • Ability to drive issues to resolution and hold vendors accountable
  • Strong operational rigor and attention to detail (critical in your environment)
  • Effective coordination across business teams and external partners
  • Continuous focus on process improvement and system reliability

Position Scope & Evolution

This role is designed to grow over time depending on experience and performance, with potential progression towards:

  • Increased ownership of specific applications (ERP, POS, EDI)
  • Lead role on small to mid-size projects
  • Expanded involvement in business solution strategy

title: ESIS Senior Claims Representative, AGL
description:
We recognize our clients’ desire to do things differently, and we are confident that our integrated approach will deliver better overall results. ESIS’ specialized claim intervention strategy integrates an effective deployment of resources and appropriate actions, which are essential to our success

ESIS, Inc. (ESIS) provides sophisticated risk management services designed to reduce claims frequency and loss costs. ESIS, the Risk Management Services Company of Chubb, provides claims, risk control & loss information systems to Fortune 1000 accounts. ESIS employs more than 1,500 professionals in nine regional centers and 15 major claims offices, as well as local representatives in select jurisdictions. We take our fiduciary responsibilities seriously and are proud to manage over $2.5 billion of customer losses and over 320,000 new claims annually. We specialize in large accounts which have multi-state operations. For information regarding ESIS please visit www.esis.com.

Summary:

ESIS is seeking an experienced Auto, General & Liability (AGL) Claim Specialist for the Overland Park, KS office. The person in this role will handle and maintain all AGL claims and file reviews under general supervision of a supervisor and as part of the ESIS team.

KEY OBJECTIVE:

Under the direction of the Claims Team Leader investigates and settles claims promptly, equitably and within established best practices guidelines.

MAJOR DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Duties include but are not limited to:

  • Under limited supervision, Receives assignments and reviews claim and policy information to provide background for investigation and may determine the extent of the policy’s obligation to the insured depending on the line of business.
  • Contacts, interviews and obtains statements(recorded or in person) from insureds, claimants, witnesses, physicians, attorneys, police officers, etc. to secure necessary claim information.
  • Depending on line of business may inspect and appraise damage for property losses or arranges for such appraisal.
  • Evaluates facts supplied by investigation to determine extent of liability of the insured, if any, and extend of the company’s obligation to the insured under the policy contract.
  • Prepares reports on investigation, settlements, denials of claims, individual evaluation of involved parties etc.
  • Sets reserves within authority limits and recommends reserve changes to Team Leader.
  • Reviews progress and status of claims with Team Leader and discusses problems and suggested remedial actions.
  • Prepares and submits to Team Leader unusual or possible undesirable exposures.
  • Assists Team Leader in developing methods and improvements for handling claims.
  • Settles claims promptly and equitably.
  • Manages litigated files by directing defense counsel to ensure best possible outcomes.
  • Obtains releases, proofs of loss or compensation agreements and issues company drafts in payments for claims.
  • Informs claimants, insureds/customers or attorney of denial of claim when applicable.
  • High level of technical claims knowledge and competence as evidenced by a minimum of 7 years claims handling experience in specific line of business (Auto & General Liability). Experience within a TPA environment strongly preferred. Required to obtains specific state licenses.
  • Knowledge of coverages; along with a good understanding of applicable legal principles and litigation management.
  • Knowledge of auto liability cost containment programs and proven account management skills a must.
  • Strong litigation management skills.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and interpersonal skills to effectively interact with all levels of an organization both internal and external.
  • Strong analytical and problem solving ability.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide consistent superior service to customers.

An applicable resident or designated home state adjuster’s license is required for ESIS Field Claims Adjusters. Adjusters that do not fulfill the license requirements will not meet ESIS’s employment requirements for handling claims. ESIS supports independent self-study time and will allow up to 4 months to pass the adjuster licensing exam.

title: Seasonal Project Assistants “Mouse-Mast Project”
description:
This position is full time (35 hours/week) or part time (12+ hours/week). This is an hourly, non-exempt, non-benefited position. Wage starts at $20/hour and is commensurate with education and experience.

Summary: Research the dynamics of mammalian communities and the relationships between mammals, ticks, oak trees, and Lyme disease. Position reports to Dr. Richard S. Ostfeld and Dr. Shannon LaDeau.

Job Description: Duties include sampling abundance of ticks, wildlife camera deployment and image processing, tree seed collection, creating soil core enclosures for measuring tick survival within eastern deciduous forest plots, and general data and GIS work.

Qualifications: Meticulous attention to detail and experience in field ecology is required. Prior experience with GIS is preferred.

Conditions: Location is the Cary Institute of Ecosystem Studies in New York’s Hudson River Valley, and nearby urban parks. This is primarily a field position with a lot of daily hiking. Early morning, late afternoon. Employment can begin Sept 28, with an end date of approximately mid-November 2026 or February 2027.

On-site housing is available.

Closing Date: Position is open until filled. Review of applications will begin on Sept 22, 2026.

To Apply: Please submit job application via . Under “Resume” on the application page, click the “Upload Resume” link to upload a single PDF file consisting of a letter of application, a resume, and the names, phone numbers, and email addresses of three professional references.

The Cary Institute is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) employer. It is the policy of the Cary Institute to provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, familial status, protected veteran or disabled status, or genetic information.

The Cary Institute of Ecosystem Studies is an independent environmental research organization dedicated to understanding ecosystems and addressing key environmental challenges. With a focus on freshwater, forests, disease, and cities, our scientists are global experts in ecology and tackle issues such as climate change, biodiversity change and human impacts on land and water.
At the Cary Institute, we prioritize sharing our science to enhance ecological literacy and foster informed decision-making.

title: ADMINISTRATIVE.GRAPHIC DESIGNER II
description:
PURPOSE & IMPACT

Nabors is seeking a Graphic Designer to create high-quality visual communications that engage employees, support internal initiatives, and strengthen the Nabors brand across the organization. This role primarily develops internal communications, executive and leadership materials, employee engagement campaigns, corporate event assets, presentations, digital signage, and other branded communications.
This position works closely with Communications, HR, leadership, and business stakeholders to translate ideas and information into clear, engaging visual solutions. The role is expected to operate with growing independence, manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced corporate environment, and provide reliable creative support to the marketing-focused graphic designer and business teams when customer-facing or external needs arise.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
Essential functions are organized by the core skill domains required for this role. Each function describes measurable outcomes that draw on the identified skills.


Internal Communications & Creative Execution
Primary Skills: Graphic Design • Visual Communication • Creative Development • Employee Communications
• Design compelling visual communications for internal campaigns, leadership messaging, employee programs, corporate initiatives, and company-wide communications.
• Create graphics and materials for town halls, employee events, meetings, executive communications, engagement activities, recognition programs, and internal campaigns.
• Develop presentations, digital signage, email graphics, infographics, posters, banners, templates, and other branded communication materials.
• Apply layout, typography, color, imagery, and visual hierarchy to improve clarity, engagement, and audience understanding.
• Deliver polished design work that is appropriate for internal audiences while maintaining the quality and professionalism expected of the Nabors brand.


Brand Standards & Visual Consistency
Primary Skills: Branding • Design Standards • Quality Control • Attention to Detail
• Ensure all creative work aligns with Nabors brand standards, visual identity requirements, and approved messaging direction.
• Maintain consistent application of brand elements across employee communications, leadership materials, events, presentations, and business-unit deliverables.
• Partner with the Brand & Graphics Manager to maintain templates, design systems, and reusable creative assets.
• Review materials for visual accuracy, alignment, formatting, image quality, and brand consistency before distribution.
• Recommend practical design improvements that strengthen professionalism, consistency, and communication effectiveness both within Nabors Communications, as well as cross-functionally.


Digital & Multimedia Communications
Primary Skills: Digital Design • Email & Intranet Graphics • Multimedia Content • Production Adaptation
• Develop digital graphics for email communications, intranet updates, digital signage, presentations, internal campaigns, and other employee-facing channels.
• Create platform-appropriate assets that support employee engagement, recruiting, leadership communications, corporate initiatives, and internal awareness campaigns.
• Assist with slide visuals, iconography, image editing, basic video graphics, and motion graphics as needed.
• Adapt designs for multiple formats, screen sizes, audiences, and communication channels while preserving visual consistency.
• Maintain design quality while meeting fast-moving communication timelines and shifting business priorities.


Presentation, Event & Campaign Design
Primary Skills: Presentation Design • Corporate Events • Campaign Execution • Production Readiness

• Develop visual concepts, templates, signage, banners, handouts, environmental graphics, and other supporting assets for internal communications, employee engagement initiatives, company events, town halls, conferences, and meetings.
• Prepare accurate, production-ready files for print, digital distribution, presentations, and on-site use, coordinating specifications with print vendors, promotional suppliers, and outside creative partners as needed.


Cross-Functional Collaboration & Project Management
Primary Skills: Communication • Stakeholder Management • Prioritization • Creative Problem Solving
• Work directly with Communications, HR, leadership, business-unit stakeholders, and other internal partners to understand design needs and project objectives.
• Manage multiple concurrent design requests while balancing deadlines, revisions, stakeholder feedback, and changing priorities, and proactively communicate project status, risks, and timeline constraints in a professional, solutions-oriented manner.
• Ask effective questions to clarify scope, audience, message, timeline, and intended use of each deliverable.
• Provide design recommendations that improve clarity, brand alignment, employee engagement, and overall communication impact.


Creative Asset & File Management
Primary Skills: Organization • Asset Management • Design Software • Process Discipline
• Maintain organized working files, final files, templates, source images, icons, and creative assets.
• Follow file naming, storage, version control, and handoff practices that support efficient team workflows.
• Update existing materials as branding, messaging, organizational priorities, and communication needs evolve.
• Support continuous improvement of creative processes, templates, and shared asset repositories.
• Protect confidential, proprietary, and pre-release business information when handling internal and corporate communications.


ADDITIONAL SUPPORT
• Provide design support for external marketing, recruiting, business-development, product, and customer-facing materials when workload or business needs require additional creative capacity.
• Partner with the marketing-focused graphic designer on brochures, product sheets, trade-show graphics, social assets, customer presentations, and other external deliverables as assigned.
